## Where this goes next

The pipeline works; the constraint now is the *hypothesis space*, not the
machinery. Ranked roughly by expected value per unit of effort:

<div class="la-next"><div class="la-card"><h4>Widen the data surface</h4><p>Every signal is bounded by what the panel contains. The highest-leverage additions are short interest and borrow cost (crowding and limits to arbitrage), institutional 13F holdings (ownership churn), analyst revisions and dispersion (expectation dynamics), and options-implied volatility surfaces (skew as a crash-risk premium). Each new provider under <code>data/features/</code> multiplies the hypothesis space rather than adding to it.</p><span class="eff">high impact · medium effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Walk-forward, not full-sample</h4><p>The harness currently scores each signal over the whole history. A purged, embargoed walk-forward protocol — fit and select on an expanding window, evaluate only on the untouched next block — would turn every number on this page into an out-of-sample one, and would catch signals that only work in the regime they were invented from.</p><span class="eff">high impact · medium effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Let the agents read their own failures</h4><p>The idea agent sees which themes are thin, but not <em>why</em> past ideas died. Feeding back the specific failure — the validator's complaint, the coverage gate, the factor attribution that revealed a tilt — should raise the hit rate per unit of spend, and it costs nothing but prompt tokens.</p><span class="eff">high impact · low effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Search combinations, not just singles</h4><p>Most published anomalies are weak alone and strong combined. A composite layer — rank-average within a theme, or a shrunk regression on standardized signals — would test whether the farmed library is greater than its parts. The novelty machinery already stores the return streams needed for it.</p><span class="eff">medium impact · low effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Model capacity honestly</h4><p>Costs are a flat per-unit-traded charge. Real capacity binds through market impact that scales with size and inversely with liquidity. A square-root impact model plus an explicit AUM assumption would tell us which of these signals survive at size rather than only on paper.</p><span class="eff">medium impact · medium effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Turn the delisting assumption into a measurement</h4><p>Delisted names currently book a configurable return, defaulted to a liquidation at the last observed price. Sharadar's corporate-actions table carries the actual delisting events; using them would replace an assumption with data, and would matter most for exactly the distressed, cheap names that value signals load on.</p><span class="eff">medium impact · low effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Regime-condition the evaluation</h4><p>A signal that works only in high-dispersion or high-rate regimes is still useful — if you know which regime you are in. Conditioning the report on macro states already in the panel would separate genuinely broken signals from ones that are simply out of season.</p><span class="eff">medium impact · medium effort</span></div><div class="la-card"><h4>Raise the bar as the library grows</h4><p>The deflation hurdle scales with the number of trials, so the more this pipeline runs, the harder it becomes to claim a discovery — correctly. The counter-move is not a lower bar but a better prior: pre-register the economic mechanism before the backtest, and treat signals whose mechanism was stated in advance as a separate, smaller family of tests.</p><span class="eff">structural · ongoing</span></div></div>

The honest summary is that a language model is a good generator of *plausible*
hypotheses and a poor judge of which ones are real. That division of labour is the
whole design: let the model propose freely, and make the harness — not the model —
decide what counts.


## The signal library

<details class="la-details">
<summary>All 170 signals — what each one measures, and the code that computes it
<span class="hint">click to expand</span></summary>
<div class="la-body">
<p class="la-lib-intro">
One entry per signal currently in the library: the reference anomalies from the
literature and every agent-written signal that compiled and passed validation.
The calculation shown is the <code>compute</code> method itself, read straight out of
the module at publish time — the page cannot drift away from the code it documents.
Each returns a <em>raw</em> score; the harness multiplies it by the expected sign, so
after orientation a high score always means "go long".
</p>
<h4 class="la-group">Cross-sectional signals (121)</h4><p class="la-group-note">Scored for every stock every month. The strategy is long the top third of the oriented score and short the bottom third, rebalanced monthly.</p><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_sensitivity_amplified_balance_sheet_safety</code><span class="la-tag">combo</span><span class="gist">Interaction of credit-beta sensitivity with fundamental balance-sheet safety: among stocks whose returns load…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of credit-beta sensitivity with fundamental balance-sheet safety: among stocks whose returns load heavily on credit-market moves, those with low leverage, high EBIT coverage, high liquidity and cash reserves are over-discounted and expected to outperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> combo</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debt = panel['debt']
    assets = panel['assets']
    ebit = panel['ebit']
    currentratio = panel['currentratio']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    liabilities = panel['liabilities']
    beta_credit = panel['beta_credit_252']
    # base validity mask: require all raw inputs present
    base_valid = (
        debt.notna() &amp; assets.notna() &amp; ebit.notna() &amp;
        currentratio.notna() &amp; cashneq.notna() &amp;
        liabilities.notna() &amp; beta_credit.notna()
    )
    assets_pos = assets &gt; 0
    debt_pos = debt &gt; 0
    lev = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    lev_mask = base_valid &amp; assets_pos
    lev.loc[lev_mask] = debt.loc[lev_mask] / assets.loc[lev_mask]
    denom = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    cov_mask = base_valid &amp; debt_pos
    denom.loc[cov_mask] = debt.loc[cov_mask]
    # fallback to eps-like max(debt, eps) per formula, but eps not mapped -&gt; use debt only
    cov = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    cov.loc[cov_mask] = ebit.loc[cov_mask] / denom.loc[cov_mask]
    cov = cov.clip(-5, 5)
    liq = currentratio.clip(upper=5)
    liq = liq.where(base_valid)
    cashr = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    cashr.loc[lev_mask] = cashneq.loc[lev_mask] / assets.loc[lev_mask]
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'lev': lev,
        'cov': cov,
        'liq': liq,
        'cashr': cashr,
        'beta_credit': beta_credit.where(base_valid),
    }, index=panel.index)
    def per_date(g: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
        valid_rows = g[['lev', 'cov', 'liq', 'cashr', 'beta_credit']].notna().all(axis=1)
        g_valid = g.loc[valid_rows]
        out = pd.Series(np.nan, index=g.index)
        if g_valid.empty:
            return out
        z_lev = self._zscore(g_valid['lev'])
        z_cov = self._zscore(g_valid['cov'])
        z_liq = self._zscore(g_valid['liq'])
        z_cashr = self._zscore(g_valid['cashr'])
        safety = -z_lev + 0.5 * z_cov + 0.5 * z_liq + 0.5 * z_cashr
        abs_beta = g_valid['beta_credit'].abs()
        w = abs_beta.rank(pct=True)
        sig = safety * (0.25 + w)
        out.loc[g_valid.index] = sig
        return out
    raw_signal = df.groupby(level='date', group_keys=False).apply(per_date)
    # macro_baa_spread past-only z-score scaling
    baa = panel['macro_baa_spread']
    baa_by_date = baa.groupby(level='date').first()
    baa_by_date = baa_by_date.sort_index()
    mean_rolling = baa_by_date.expanding(min_periods=2).mean().shift(1)
    std_rolling = baa_by_date.expanding(min_periods=2).std().shift(1)
    z_baa = (baa_by_date - mean_rolling) / std_rolling
    z_baa = z_baa.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    z_baa_clipped = z_baa.clip(-1, 1)
    multiplier = 1 + 0.5 * z_baa_clipped
    multiplier = multiplier.fillna(1.0)
    multiplier_full = panel.index.get_level_values('date').map(multiplier)
    multiplier_full = pd.Series(multiplier_full, index=panel.index)
    result = raw_signal * multiplier_full
    result.name = self.name
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>funding_conditioned_beta_tilt</code><span class="la-tag">combo</span><span class="gist">Flips the sign of the beta tilt with the funding-liquidity cycle, measured by the joint 12-month change in…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Flips the sign of the beta tilt with the funding-liquidity cycle, measured by the joint 12-month change in fed funds rate and Baa credit spread. During funding easing episodes, high-beta names are favored; during tightening, low-beta names are favored.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> combo</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta = panel['beta_252']
    fedfunds_chg = panel['macro_fedfunds_chg12m']
    baa_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    nobs = panel['nobs']
    tighten = fedfunds_chg + baa_chg
    ease = -tighten
    score = beta * np.tanh(ease)
    invalid = beta.isna() | fedfunds_chg.isna() | baa_chg.isna() | (nobs &lt; 200)
    score = score.where(~invalid, np.nan)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>net_cash_yield_rate_change_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">combo</span><span class="gist">Interaction between net-cash-to-marketcap ratio and the signed 12-month change in the 2-year Treasury yield</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction between net-cash-to-marketcap ratio and the signed 12-month change in the 2-year Treasury yield. Cash-rich firms benefit from rising short rates via interest income while net-debt firms benefit from falling rates via cheaper refinancing; this macro-conditioned quality/leverage signal flips sign with the direction of the short-rate cycle.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> combo</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    debt = panel['debt']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    cond = panel['macro_dgs2_chg12m']
    valid = cashneq.notna() &amp; debt.notna() &amp; marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; cond.notna()
    net_cash_yield = (cashneq - debt) / marketcap
    net_cash_yield = net_cash_yield.where(valid)
    def winsorize(s):
        if s.notna().sum() == 0:
            return s
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    net_cash_yield_w = net_cash_yield.groupby(level='date').transform(winsorize)
    signal = net_cash_yield_w * cond
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>operating_leverage_business_cycle</code><span class="la-tag">combo</span><span class="gist">Operating leverage (opex/assets) conditioned on the trailing 12m change in industrial production and…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Operating leverage (opex/assets) conditioned on the trailing 12m change in industrial production and recession state: high fixed-cost intensity firms are expected to outperform when industrial activity is improving (and underperform when it is deteriorating), capturing a macro-state-dependent risk premium orthogonal to static value/quality factors.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> combo</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    opex = panel['opex']
    assets = panel['assets']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    valid = (assets &gt; 0) &amp; (revenue &gt; 0)
    ol = (opex / assets).where(valid)
    ol_clipped = ol.clip(lower=0, upper=2)
    def zscore(s):
        mu = s.mean()
        sd = s.std()
        if sd is None or sd == 0 or pd.isna(sd):
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        return (s - mu) / sd
    ol_z = ol_clipped.groupby(level='date').transform(zscore)
    indpro_chg = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m']
    usrec = panel['macro_usrec']
    cyc = np.tanh(indpro_chg / 2.0) * (1 - 0.5 * usrec)
    cyc = cyc.where(indpro_chg.notna() &amp; usrec.notna())
    raw = ol_z * cyc
    return raw.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>rollover_risk_credit_cycle_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">combo</span><span class="gist">Interaction between near-term rollover risk (net current debt / assets) and the 12-month change in the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction between near-term rollover risk (net current debt / assets) and the 12-month change in the Baa-Treasury credit spread. Firms with high net short-term debt suffer when credit spreads widen and benefit when spreads tighten, so the score sign-flips with the credit cycle.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> combo</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debtc = panel['debtc']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    assets = panel['assets']
    tighten = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    valid = debtc.notna() &amp; cashneq.notna() &amp; assets.notna() &amp; tighten.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
    rollover = (debtc - cashneq) / assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    rollover = rollover.clip(-1, 1)
    score = -rollover * tighten
    score = score.where(valid, np.nan)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>asset_growth</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth (YoY); low-growth firms outperform</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth (YoY); low-growth firms outperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel["assets"].where(panel["assets"] &gt; 0)
    return _yoy(assets)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>external_finance_dependence_credit_shock</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Rajan-Zingales style external finance dependence (capex exceeding internal operating cash flow) combined with…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Rajan-Zingales style external finance dependence (capex exceeding internal operating cash flow) combined with short-term debt load, interacted with the 12-month change in the Baa credit spread. Firms with high financing need are hurt when credit spreads widen and helped when spreads tighten; the harness orients the score so that expected sign is positive.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    capex = panel['capex']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    debtc = panel['debtc']
    macro_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    dep = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    stdebt = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    dep_valid = valid_assets &amp; capex.notna() &amp; ncfo.notna() &amp; assets.notna()
    dep.loc[dep_valid] = (capex.loc[dep_valid].abs() - ncfo.loc[dep_valid]) / assets.loc[dep_valid]
    stdebt_valid = valid_assets &amp; debtc.notna() &amp; assets.notna()
    stdebt.loc[stdebt_valid] = debtc.loc[stdebt_valid] / assets.loc[stdebt_valid]
    base_missing = (
        (~valid_assets)
        | capex.isna()
        | ncfo.isna()
        | assets.isna()
        | debtc.isna()
        | macro_chg.isna()
    )
    dep = dep.where(~base_missing)
    stdebt = stdebt.where(~base_missing)
    def cross_section_z(group: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        n_valid = group.notna().sum()
        if n_valid &lt; 20:
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=group.index)
        return _zscore(group)
    dep_z = dep.groupby(level='date').apply(cross_section_z)
    dep_z.index = dep_z.index.droplevel(0) if isinstance(dep_z.index, pd.MultiIndex) and dep_z.index.nlevels &gt; panel.index.nlevels else dep_z.index
    stdebt_z = stdebt.groupby(level='date').apply(cross_section_z)
    stdebt_z.index = stdebt_z.index.droplevel(0) if isinstance(stdebt_z.index, pd.MultiIndex) and stdebt_z.index.nlevels &gt; panel.index.nlevels else stdebt_z.index
    need = dep_z + stdebt_z
    tight = np.tanh(macro_chg / 0.5)
    raw_signal = -need * tight
    raw_signal = raw_signal.where(~base_missing)
    return raw_signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>inventory_growth_gap</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Gap between inventory growth and sales growth over trailing 12 months</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Gap between inventory growth and sales growth over trailing 12 months. High inventory growth relative to sales growth signals over-optimistic demand forecasts, future write-downs, and margin pressure, predicting negative future abnormal returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    inventory = panel['inventory']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    assets = panel['assets']
    inv_l12 = inventory.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    rev_l12 = revenue.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    inv_g = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_inv = inv_l12 &gt; 0
    inv_g[valid_inv] = inventory[valid_inv] / inv_l12[valid_inv] - 1.0
    sales_g = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_rev = rev_l12 &gt; 0
    sales_g[valid_rev] = revenue[valid_rev] / rev_l12[valid_rev] - 1.0
    inv_g_clipped = inv_g.clip(-1, 3)
    sales_g_clipped = sales_g.clip(-1, 3)
    raw = inv_g_clipped - sales_g_clipped
    valid_mask = (
        (assets &gt; 0)
        &amp; (inventory &gt; 0)
        &amp; (inv_l12 &gt; 0)
        &amp; (revenue &gt; 0)
        &amp; (rev_l12 &gt; 0)
    )
    raw = raw.where(valid_mask, np.nan)
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>late_quarter_buyback_share_shrinkage</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Signal detects late-quarter share buybacks by comparing weighted-average shares to point-in-time basic shares…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Signal detects late-quarter share buybacks by comparing weighted-average shares to point-in-time basic shares outstanding: sharesbas materially below shareswa implies repurchases concentrated late in the quarter, not yet reflected in annual issuance measures. The signal is confirmed with actual cash outflow for equity (negative ncfcommon relative to market cap) to filter mechanical share-count artifacts.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    shareswa = panel['shareswa']
    sharesbas = panel['sharesbas']
    ncfcommon = panel['ncfcommon']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid_shares = (shareswa &gt; 0) &amp; (sharesbas &gt; 0)
    shrink = (shareswa - sharesbas) / shareswa.where(shareswa &gt; 0)
    shrink = shrink.where(valid_shares)
    cash_conf = (-ncfcommon / marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0))
    cash_conf = cash_conf.where((marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; ncfcommon.notna(), 0.0)
    cash_conf = cash_conf.clip(-0.25, 0.25)
    signal = shrink + 0.5 * cash_conf
    invalid = shrink.isna() | (shrink.abs() &gt; 0.5)
    signal = signal.where(~invalid, np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>net_share_issuance</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">YoY growth in shares outstanding; net issuers underperform, repurchasers outperform</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>YoY growth in shares outstanding; net issuers underperform, repurchasers outperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    shares = panel["sharesbas"].where(panel["sharesbas"] &gt; 0)
    return _yoy(shares)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>payout_funding_gap</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Payout-versus-free-cash-flow funding gap: payout = max(-ncfdiv,0) + max(-ncfcommon,0); gap = (payout - fcf) /…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Payout-versus-free-cash-flow funding gap: payout = max(-ncfdiv,0) + max(-ncfcommon,0); gap = (payout - fcf) / assets, winsorized at 1/99% per date. Firms paying out far more cash than their free cash flow supports are unlikely to sustain the distribution and tend to underperform; self-funded payers (negative gap) tend to outperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ncfdiv = panel['ncfdiv']
    ncfcommon = panel['ncfcommon']
    fcf = panel['fcf']
    assets = panel['assets']
    valid = ncfdiv.notna() &amp; ncfcommon.notna() &amp; fcf.notna() &amp; assets.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
    payout = (-ncfdiv).clip(lower=0) + (-ncfcommon).clip(lower=0)
    gap = (payout - fcf) / assets
    gap = gap.where(valid, np.nan)
    def _winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        if s.notna().sum() == 0:
            return s
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    gap = gap.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorize)
    return gap.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>unproductive_acquisition_growth</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Growth in goodwill/intangibles (acquisition footprint) net of revenue growth</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Growth in goodwill/intangibles (acquisition footprint) net of revenue growth. High acquisition-driven balance-sheet expansion unaccompanied by revenue growth signals overpayment/empire-building and predicts lower future returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    intangibles = panel['intangibles']
    assets = panel['assets']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    grp = panel.index.get_level_values('ticker')
    lag_intangibles = intangibles.groupby(grp).shift(12)
    lag_assets = assets.groupby(grp).shift(12)
    lag_revenue = revenue.groupby(grp).shift(12)
    acq = (intangibles - lag_intangibles) / lag_assets
    acq = acq.where(lag_assets &gt; 0, np.nan)
    acq = acq.where(intangibles.notna() &amp; lag_intangibles.notna(), np.nan)
    acq = acq.clip(-1, 1)
    rev_g = (revenue - lag_revenue) / lag_revenue.abs()
    rev_g = rev_g.where(lag_revenue &gt; 0, np.nan)
    rev_g = rev_g.where(revenue.notna() &amp; lag_revenue.notna(), np.nan)
    rev_g = rev_g.clip(-2, 2)
    df = pd.DataFrame({'acq': acq, 'rev_g': rev_g})
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    def cs_zscore(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean = s.groupby(dates).transform('mean')
        std = s.groupby(dates).transform('std')
        z = (s - mean) / std
        return z.where(std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    z_acq = cs_zscore(df['acq'])
    z_rev = cs_zscore(df['rev_g'])
    signal = z_acq - z_rev
    signal = signal.where(df['acq'].notna() &amp; df['rev_g'].notna(), np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_beta_defensive</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Cross-asset correlation factor: prefer defensive stocks least hurt by credit-spread widening (higher corr to…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-asset correlation factor: prefer defensive stocks least hurt by credit-spread widening (higher corr to spread changes).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    return panel["corr_credit_252"]</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_beta_leverage_mismatch</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Mismatch between a stock's trailing credit-spread beta (market-implied distress risk) and its reported…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Mismatch between a stock's trailing credit-spread beta (market-implied distress risk) and its reported balance-sheet leverage (debt/assets). Stocks whose market-perceived credit risk is far higher than fundamentals justify are expected to underperform (distress-risk anomaly).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">from __future__ import annotations
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from llm_alpha.signals.base import BaseSignal
class CreditBetaLeverageMismatch(BaseSignal):
    name = "credit_beta_leverage_mismatch"
    category = "low_risk"
    strategy_type = "cross_sectional"
    expected_sign = 1
    description = (
        "Cross-asset residual comparing equity's market-implied distress "
        "sensitivity (negative of credit beta) to balance-sheet net leverage. "
        "Stocks whose equity underprices credit risk relative to true leverage "
        "(implied distress low, leverage high) are expected to underperform; "
        "the reverse mismatch is expected to earn a premium."
    )
    data_sources = ('price', 'fundamental', 'macro')
    def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
        beta_credit = panel['beta_credit_252']
        corr_credit = panel['corr_credit_252']
        debt = panel['debt']
        cashneq = panel['cashneq']
        assets = panel['assets']
        valid_beta_corr = beta_credit.notna() &amp; corr_credit.notna()
        implied_distress = -beta_credit
        implied_distress = implied_distress.where(
            valid_beta_corr &amp; (corr_credit.abs() &gt;= 0.02)
        )
        assets_valid = assets.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
        netlev = (debt - cashneq) / assets
        netlev = netlev.where(assets_valid)
        netlev = netlev.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=2.0)
        valid = valid_beta_corr &amp; assets_valid
        implied_distress = implied_distress.where(valid)
        netlev = netlev.where(valid)
        def zscore(s):
            grp = s.groupby(level='date')
            mean = grp.transform('mean')
            std = grp.transform('std')
            return (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
        z1 = zscore(implied_distress)
        z2 = zscore(netlev)
        signal = z1 - z2
        signal = signal.where(z1.notna() &amp; z2.notna())
        return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>leverage_credit_beta_complacency</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Interaction of balance-sheet net leverage with complacency toward credit risk (low absolute correlation to…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of balance-sheet net leverage with complacency toward credit risk (low absolute correlation to credit-spread changes). Highly levered firms whose equity returns are largely uncorrelated with credit conditions are hypothesized to harbor unpriced distress risk, predicting subsequent underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debt = panel['debt']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    assets = panel['assets']
    corr_credit = panel['corr_credit_252']
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    netlev = (debt - cashneq) / assets.where(valid_assets)
    netlev = netlev.where(valid_assets)
    complacency = 1.0 - corr_credit.abs()
    complacency = complacency.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    # drop rows missing required inputs
    base_valid = debt.notna() &amp; cashneq.notna() &amp; assets.notna() &amp; valid_assets &amp; corr_credit.notna()
    netlev = netlev.where(base_valid)
    complacency = complacency.where(base_valid)
    lev_r = netlev.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    comp_r = complacency.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    signal = lev_r * comp_r
    signal = signal.where(lev_r.notna() &amp; comp_r.notna())
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>lottery_demand_sentiment_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Interaction of a lottery-stock proxy (high vol, low nominal price, small size) with a publication-lagged…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of a lottery-stock proxy (high vol, low nominal price, small size) with a publication-lagged consumer-sentiment state variable. Lottery stocks are expected to be overpriced (and thus underperform) when sentiment/optimism is high, with the effect attenuating or reversing after prolonged pessimism.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    closeunadj = panel['closeunadj']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    log_price = np.log(closeunadj.where(closeunadj &gt; 0))
    log_mcap = np.log(marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0))
    neg_log_price = -log_price
    neg_log_mcap = -log_mcap
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'vol_252': vol_252,
        'neg_log_price': neg_log_price,
        'neg_log_mcap': neg_log_mcap,
    }, index=panel.index)
    r_vol = df.groupby(level='date')['vol_252'].transform(_rank_scaled)
    r_price = df.groupby(level='date')['neg_log_price'].transform(_rank_scaled)
    r_mcap = df.groupby(level='date')['neg_log_mcap'].transform(_rank_scaled)
    lottery = r_vol + r_price + r_mcap
    lottery = lottery.where(
        vol_252.notna() &amp; (closeunadj &gt; 0) &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
    )
    # date-level sentiment series
    umcsent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').first()
    umcsent_chg12m = panel['macro_umcsent_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    umcsent = umcsent.sort_index()
    umcsent_chg12m = umcsent_chg12m.sort_index()
    # backward-looking: use shift(1) before rolling to avoid look-ahead
    umcsent_lag = umcsent.shift(1)
    roll_mean = umcsent_lag.rolling(120, min_periods=36).mean()
    roll_std = umcsent_lag.rolling(120, min_periods=36).std()
    sz = (umcsent - roll_mean) / roll_std
    sz = sz.clip(-2, 2)
    chg_lag = umcsent_chg12m.shift(1)
    chg_roll_mean = chg_lag.rolling(120, min_periods=36).mean()
    chg_roll_std = chg_lag.rolling(120, min_periods=36).std()
    chg_z = (umcsent_chg12m - chg_roll_mean) / chg_roll_std
    chg_z = chg_z.clip(-2, 2)
    sent_state = 0.5 * sz + 0.5 * chg_z
    # broadcast sent_state to panel index
    sent_state_full = panel.index.get_level_values('date').map(sent_state)
    sent_state_full = pd.Series(sent_state_full, index=panel.index)
    score = -lottery * sent_state_full
    valid = (
        lottery.notna()
        &amp; sent_state_full.notna()
        &amp; panel['macro_umcsent'].notna()
        &amp; panel['macro_umcsent_chg12m'].notna()
    )
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>low_volatility</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Low-volatility anomaly: trailing 1y realized vol of daily returns (low = long)</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Low-volatility anomaly: trailing 1y realized vol of daily returns (low = long).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    return panel["vol_252"]</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_churn</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Measures churn/instability in a stock's trailing macro factor betas (credit, rates, oil, usd, vix) over 12…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Measures churn/instability in a stock's trailing macro factor betas (credit, rates, oil, usd, vix) over 12 months, cross-sectionally z-scored per factor per date and averaged. High churn indicates an unstable risk profile that predicts lower future risk-adjusted returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    factors = [
        'beta_credit_252',
        'beta_rates_252',
        'beta_oil_252',
        'beta_usd_252',
        'beta_vix_252',
    ]
    z_scores = []
    for f in factors:
        cur = panel[f]
        lag = cur.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        d = (cur - lag).abs()
        d = d.where(cur.notna() &amp; lag.notna())
        std_by_date = d.groupby(level='date').transform('std')
        z = d / std_by_date.where(std_by_date &gt; 0)
        z_scores.append(z)
    z_df = pd.concat(z_scores, axis=1)
    z_df.columns = factors
    count = z_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mean_z = z_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = mean_z.where(count &gt;= 3)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_churn_instability</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Measures instability of a stock's macro factor exposures (rates, credit, oil, usd, vix betas) over the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Measures instability of a stock's macro factor exposures (rates, credit, oil, usd, vix betas) over the trailing 12 months. High churn in factor loadings implies ambiguous risk profile and speculative-flow-driven comovement, predicting underperformance; stable-exposure firms earn higher realized returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    factors = ['beta_rates_252', 'beta_credit_252', 'beta_oil_252',
               'beta_usd_252', 'beta_vix_252']
    s_list = []
    for f in factors:
        if f not in panel.columns:
            continue
        cur = panel[f]
        lag = panel[f].groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        d_f = (cur - lag).abs()
        d_f = d_f.where(cur.notna() &amp; lag.notna())
        med = d_f.groupby(level='date').transform('median')
        s_f = d_f / med.where(med &gt; 0)
        s_list.append(s_f)
    if not s_list:
        return pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    s_df = pd.concat(s_list, axis=1)
    count = s_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    churn = s_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    churn = churn.where(count &gt;= 3)
    return churn.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_instability</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Measures instability of a stock's macro factor exposures (rates, oil, usd, credit, vix betas) via the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Measures instability of a stock's macro factor exposures (rates, oil, usd, credit, vix betas) via the 12-month absolute change in each beta, cross-sectionally ranked per date and averaged across available factors. Stocks with unstable macro exposures are hypothesized to underperform, so the raw score (higher = more unstable) is used with a negative expected sign.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    fields = [
        'beta_rates_252',
        'beta_oil_252',
        'beta_usd_252',
        'beta_credit_252',
        'beta_vix_252',
        'beta_252',
    ]
    rank_frames = []
    for f in fields:
        if f not in panel.columns:
            continue
        current = panel[f]
        lagged = current.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        diff = (current - lagged).abs()
        valid = current.notna() &amp; lagged.notna()
        diff = diff.where(valid)
        rank = diff.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
        rank_frames.append(rank)
    if not rank_frames:
        return pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    rank_df = pd.concat(rank_frames, axis=1)
    count_valid = rank_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mean_rank = rank_df.mean(axis=1)
    score = mean_rank.where(count_valid &gt;= 4)
    score.name = self.name
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_instability_ambiguity</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Instability of a stock's cross-asset macro betas (oil, usd, rates, credit, vix) over the trailing 12 months,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Instability of a stock's cross-asset macro betas (oil, usd, rates, credit, vix) over the trailing 12 months, standardized by cross-sectional dispersion each date. Stocks with unstable macro exposures have opaque/changing risk profiles and tend to underperform, so a higher instability score predicts LOWER returns (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    eps = 1e-8
    factors = [
        'beta_oil_252',
        'beta_usd_252',
        'beta_rates_252',
        'beta_credit_252',
        'beta_vix_252',
    ]
    deltas = []
    for f in factors:
        if f not in panel.columns:
            continue
        b = panel[f]
        b_lag = b.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        valid = b.notna() &amp; b_lag.notna()
        abs_chg = (b - b_lag).abs()
        cs_std = abs_chg.where(valid).groupby(level='date').transform('std')
        d = abs_chg / (cs_std + eps)
        d = d.where(valid)
        deltas.append(d)
    if not deltas:
        return pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    deltas_df = pd.concat(deltas, axis=1)
    valid_count = deltas_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    instability = deltas_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    instability = instability.where(valid_count &gt;= 3)
    return instability.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_rotation_instability</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Measures instability (rotation) of a firm's vector of macro betas (credit, oil, rates, usd, vix) over a…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Measures instability (rotation) of a firm's vector of macro betas (credit, oil, rates, usd, vix) over a trailing 12-month window. Firms whose macro exposure vector rotates sharply are opaque and subject to parameter/model uncertainty, generating mispricing that on average resolves adversely, leading to lower subsequent returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta_cols = [
        'beta_credit_252',
        'beta_oil_252',
        'beta_rates_252',
        'beta_usd_252',
        'beta_vix_252',
    ]
    def winsorized_zscore(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        grp = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        z = (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
        z = z.clip(-4, 4)
        return z
    z_diffs = []
    missing_flags = []
    for col in beta_cols:
        if col not in panel.columns:
            # treat as fully missing component
            nan_series = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
            z_diffs.append(nan_series)
            missing_flags.append(pd.Series(True, index=panel.index))
            continue
        raw = panel[col]
        valid_mask = raw.notna()
        z = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
        z.loc[valid_mask] = winsorized_zscore(raw.loc[valid_mask])
        z_lag = z.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        missing = z.isna() | z_lag.isna()
        diff_sq = (z - z_lag) ** 2
        z_diffs.append(diff_sq)
        missing_flags.append(missing)
    missing_count = pd.concat(missing_flags, axis=1).sum(axis=1)
    diff_matrix = pd.concat(z_diffs, axis=1)
    # sum of squared diffs, treating missing contributions as 0 (only allowed if &lt;=1 missing)
    diff_matrix_filled = diff_matrix.fillna(0.0)
    sum_sq = diff_matrix_filled.sum(axis=1)
    churn = np.sqrt(sum_sq)
    churn[missing_count &gt; 1] = np.nan
    churn.name = self.name
    return churn</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_exposure_drift</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Measures the drift in a stock's macro exposure profile (rates, oil, USD, credit, VIX betas) over the trailing…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Measures the drift in a stock's macro exposure profile (rates, oil, USD, credit, VIX betas) over the trailing 12 months via cross-sectional z-score changes. Stocks with unstable macro exposures are harder to model and attract speculative demand, leading to subsequent underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    betas = [
        'beta_rates_252',
        'beta_oil_252',
        'beta_usd_252',
        'beta_credit_252',
        'beta_vix_252',
    ]
    drift_terms = []
    for b in betas:
        col = panel[b]
        # cross-sectional zscore within each date
        grp = col.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        z = (col - mean) / std
        z = z.where(std &gt; 0, np.nan)
        z = z.clip(lower=-4, upper=4)
        z_lag = z.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
        d = (z - z_lag).abs()
        drift_terms.append(d)
    drift_df = pd.concat(drift_terms, axis=1)
    drift_df.columns = betas
    nonnull_count = drift_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    avg_drift = drift_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = avg_drift.where(nonnull_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_exposure_instability</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Instability of a stock's macro exposure vector: measures the cross-sectional standardized 12-month absolute…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Instability of a stock's macro exposure vector: measures the cross-sectional standardized 12-month absolute change in beta_oil_252, beta_rates_252, beta_usd_252, beta_credit_252, beta_vix_252. High instability indicates an opaque, churning macro identity, which predicts subsequent underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">from __future__ import annotations
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from llm_alpha.signals.base import BaseSignal
class MacroExposureInstability(BaseSignal):
    name = "macro_exposure_instability"
    category = "low_risk"
    strategy_type = "cross_sectional"
    expected_sign = -1
    description = (
        "Measures instability of a stock's macro factor betas (oil, rates, usd, "
        "credit, vix) over a 12-month horizon. Stocks with unstable macro "
        "exposures are hard to hedge/value and earn lower subsequent returns; "
        "stable macro-exposure stocks earn higher returns (expected_sign=-1)."
    )
    data_sources = ('price', 'macro')
    def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
        factors = [
            'beta_oil_252',
            'beta_rates_252',
            'beta_usd_252',
            'beta_credit_252',
            'beta_vix_252',
        ]
        s_list = []
        for f in factors:
            if f not in panel.columns:
                continue
            cur = panel[f]
            lag = panel[f].groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
            d_f = (cur - lag).abs()
            d_f = d_f.where(cur.notna() &amp; lag.notna())
            # cross-sectional median of |d_f| per date
            med = d_f.groupby(level='date').transform('median')
            mad = (d_f - med).abs()
            mad_med = mad.groupby(level='date').transform('median')
            s_f = d_f / mad_med.where(mad_med &gt; 0)
            s_f = s_f.where(mad_med &gt; 0)
            s_list.append(s_f)
        if len(s_list) == 0:
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
        s_df = pd.concat(s_list, axis=1)
        count_avail = s_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
        instab = s_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
        instab = instab.where(count_avail &gt;= 3)
        # orthogonalization term: date-level cross-sectional rank of vol_252
        if 'vol_252' in panel.columns:
            vol = panel['vol_252']
            vol_rank = vol.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
            vol_rank = vol_rank.fillna(0.0)
        else:
            vol_rank = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
        score = instab - 0.5 * vol_rank
        score = score.where(instab.notna())
        return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_systematic_variance_share</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Systematic variance share: sum of squared trailing 252d correlations of a stock's returns to five macro…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Systematic variance share: sum of squared trailing 252d correlations of a stock's returns to five macro factors (credit, rates, oil, usd, vix), clipped to [0,1]. Low share indicates idiosyncratic, opaque, lottery-like names that historically underperform (Ang et al., Durnev/Morck).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = [
        'corr_credit_252',
        'corr_rates_252',
        'corr_oil_252',
        'corr_usd_252',
        'corr_vix_252',
    ]
    valid = pd.Series(True, index=panel.index)
    for c in cols:
        valid &amp;= panel[c].notna()
    nobs_ok = panel['nobs'] &gt;= 200
    share = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    for c in cols:
        share = share + panel[c].fillna(0) ** 2
    share = share.clip(lower=0, upper=1)
    score = share.where(valid &amp; nobs_ok)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>rate_duration_mispricing</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Shorts hidden long-duration equities (high PB, low yield, high realized rate beta) during rising-yield…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Shorts hidden long-duration equities (high PB, low yield, high realized rate beta) during rising-yield regimes and reverses during falling-yield regimes, by comparing realized rate beta to fundamental duration implied by valuation/dividend structure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pb = panel['pb']
    divyield = panel['divyield']
    beta_rates = panel['beta_rates_252']
    macro_chg = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m']
    pb_valid = pb.where(pb &gt; 0)
    log_pb = np.log(pb_valid)
    def cs_zscore(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        grouped = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grouped.transform('mean')
        std = grouped.transform('std')
        z = (s - mean) / std
        return z.where(std &gt; 0)
    log_pb_z = cs_zscore(log_pb)
    # only include divyield in z-score for rows with valid pb
    divyield_masked = divyield.where(pb_valid.notna())
    divyield_z = cs_zscore(divyield_masked)
    dur_z = log_pb_z - divyield_z
    implied_beta = -dur_z
    beta_rates_masked = beta_rates.where(pb_valid.notna())
    beta_rates_z = cs_zscore(beta_rates_masked)
    mismatch = beta_rates_z - implied_beta
    rate_trend = np.tanh(macro_chg)
    signal = -mismatch * rate_trend
    # apply missing-data policy
    valid_mask = pb_valid.notna() &amp; divyield.notna() &amp; beta_rates.notna() &amp; macro_chg.notna()
    signal = signal.where(valid_mask)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>residual_vix_hedge_premium</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Residual VIX beta after removing market-beta component via per-date cross-sectional OLS of beta_vix_252 on…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Residual VIX beta after removing market-beta component via per-date cross-sectional OLS of beta_vix_252 on [1, beta_252]. High residual VIX beta stocks act as crash hedges and are bid up, earning lower subsequent returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = ['beta_vix_252', 'beta_252']
    df = panel[cols].copy()
    result = df.groupby(level='date', group_keys=False).apply(self._fit_resid)
    result = result.reindex(panel.index)
    result.name = self.name
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>unpriced_leverage_credit_insensitivity</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Mismatch between balance-sheet leverage and realized equity credit-beta: highly levered firms whose equity…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Mismatch between balance-sheet leverage and realized equity credit-beta: highly levered firms whose equity shows low sensitivity to credit spread moves are 'credit-complacent' and prone to sharp repricing when credit conditions tighten. Score = z(net leverage) - z(-beta_credit_252).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debt = panel['debt']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    assets = panel['assets']
    beta_credit = panel['beta_credit_252']
    corr_credit = panel['corr_credit_252']
    valid = (
        assets.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
        &amp; debt.notna() &amp; cashneq.notna()
        &amp; beta_credit.notna() &amp; corr_credit.notna()
    )
    netlev = (debt - cashneq) / assets
    netlev = netlev.clip(-1, 2)
    credit_exposure = -beta_credit
    netlev_v = netlev.where(valid)
    credit_exposure_v = credit_exposure.where(valid)
    def zscore(s):
        grp = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        return (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
    zl = zscore(netlev_v)
    zc = zscore(credit_exposure_v)
    score = zl - zc
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>vix_beta_drift</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Signal based on the 12-month drift in trailing VIX beta, scaled by realized volatility</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Signal based on the 12-month drift in trailing VIX beta, scaled by realized volatility. A deteriorating (more negative) VIX beta signals quietly accumulating crash exposure not yet priced in, predicting underperformance; an improving VIX beta signals a cheap hedge, predicting outperformance. Restricted to stocks with meaningful trailing correlation to VIX (|corr_vix_252| &gt;= 0.02).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta_vix = panel['beta_vix_252']
    corr_vix = panel['corr_vix_252']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    beta_vix_lag12 = beta_vix.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    dbeta = beta_vix - beta_vix_lag12
    scale = vol_252.clip(lower=0.05, upper=2.0)
    signal = dbeta / scale
    valid = (
        beta_vix.notna()
        &amp; beta_vix_lag12.notna()
        &amp; corr_vix.notna()
        &amp; vol_252.notna()
        &amp; (vol_252 &gt; 0)
        &amp; (corr_vix.abs() &gt;= 0.02)
    )
    signal = signal.where(valid, np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>annual_return_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Annual return seasonality: average of same-calendar-month ret_1m from prior years (lags 12,24,36,48,60…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Annual return seasonality: average of same-calendar-month ret_1m from prior years (lags 12,24,36,48,60 months) predicts future returns (Heston-Sadka 2008 style seasonality). Requires at least 3 non-NaN lags.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">from __future__ import annotations
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from llm_alpha.signals.base import BaseSignal
class AnnualReturnSeasonality(BaseSignal):
    name = "annual_return_seasonality"
    category = "other"
    strategy_type = "cross_sectional"
    expected_sign = 1
    description = (
        "Same-calendar-month return seasonality: average of a stock's ret_1m "
        "at annual lags (12,24,36,48,60 months) minus the average of its "
        "ret_1m over non-seasonal lags (13..23 months). Captures the "
        "Heston-Sadka same-month seasonality effect, largely orthogonal to "
        "12-1 momentum."
    )
    data_sources = ('price',)
    def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
        ret = panel['ret_1m']
        grp = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
        same_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
        other_lags = list(range(13, 24))
        same_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in same_lags]
        other_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in other_lags]
        same_df = pd.concat(same_shifts, axis=1)
        other_df = pd.concat(other_shifts, axis=1)
        same_count = same_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
        same_mean = same_df.mean(axis=1)
        same_mean = same_mean.where(same_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
        other_count = other_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
        other_mean = other_df.mean(axis=1)
        other_mean = other_mean.where(other_count &gt; 0, 0.0)
        signal = same_mean - other_mean
        signal = signal.where(same_mean.notna(), np.nan)
        return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>annual_return_seasonality_purged</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Heston-Sadka style calendar-month seasonality: average of same-calendar-month returns at 1-5 year annual…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Heston-Sadka style calendar-month seasonality: average of same-calendar-month returns at 1-5 year annual lags, purged by subtracting the average of adjacent (non-annual) lags to remove generic momentum/reversal, isolating pure seasonal return predictability.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    grp = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    annual_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    adjacent_lags = [11, 13, 23, 25, 35, 37]
    annual_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in annual_lags]
    adjacent_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in adjacent_lags]
    annual_df = pd.concat(annual_shifts, axis=1)
    adjacent_df = pd.concat(adjacent_shifts, axis=1)
    annual_count = annual_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    seas_mean = annual_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    nonseas_mean = adjacent_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = seas_mean - nonseas_mean
    signal = signal.where(annual_count &gt;= 3)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>cross_asset_news_diffusion_momentum</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Combines trailing macro-factor loadings (beta_usd_252, beta_oil_252, beta_rates_252 gated by correlation…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Combines trailing macro-factor loadings (beta_usd_252, beta_oil_252, beta_rates_252 gated by correlation strength) with recent standardized macro shocks (USD, oil, 10y rate) to capture slow diffusion of cross-asset news into stock prices.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel
    def date_level_shock(chg_series):
        # date-level series (same value across tickers per date)
        date_level = chg_series.groupby(level='date').first()
        roll_std = date_level.rolling(36, min_periods=18).std()
        sh_date = date_level / roll_std.replace(0, np.nan)
        # map back to (date,ticker)
        dates = chg_series.index.get_level_values('date')
        return sh_date.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
    # USD shock: pct change over 3 months
    usd_shift3 = df.groupby(level='ticker')['macro_usd'].shift(3)
    chg_usd = df['macro_usd'] / usd_shift3.replace(0, np.nan) - 1
    sh_usd = pd.Series(date_level_shock(chg_usd), index=df.index)
    # Oil shock: pct change over 3 months
    oil_shift3 = df.groupby(level='ticker')['macro_oil'].shift(3)
    chg_oil = df['macro_oil'] / oil_shift3.replace(0, np.nan) - 1
    sh_oil = pd.Series(date_level_shock(chg_oil), index=df.index)
    # Rates shock: level difference over 3 months
    rates_shift3 = df.groupby(level='ticker')['macro_dgs10'].shift(3)
    chg_rates = df['macro_dgs10'] - rates_shift3
    sh_rates = pd.Series(date_level_shock(chg_rates), index=df.index)
    def loading(beta_col, corr_col):
        beta = df[beta_col]
        corr = df[corr_col]
        valid = corr.abs() &gt; 0.15
        load = beta.where(valid, 0.0)
        load = load.where(beta.notna() &amp; corr.notna(), np.nan)
        return load
    load_usd = loading('beta_usd_252', 'corr_usd_252')
    load_oil = loading('beta_oil_252', 'corr_oil_252')
    load_rates = loading('beta_rates_252', 'corr_rates_252')
    term_usd = load_usd * sh_usd
    term_oil = load_oil * sh_oil
    term_rates = load_rates * sh_rates
    terms = pd.concat([term_usd, term_oil, term_rates], axis=1)
    terms.columns = ['usd', 'oil', 'rates']
    # a term contributes 0 if its inputs are missing/invalid, but overall
    # signal is NaN if ALL three loadings are missing
    loadings_all_nan = load_usd.isna() &amp; load_oil.isna() &amp; load_rates.isna()
    signal = terms.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
    signal = signal.where(~loadings_all_nan, np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>frog_in_the_pan_gradual_momentum</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Interacts 12-1 momentum with 'information discreteness' of the path: momentum accumulated via many small…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interacts 12-1 momentum with 'information discreteness' of the path: momentum accumulated via many small same-sign monthly moves (gradual) is up-weighted, while momentum driven by a few large jumps is down-weighted, per Da, Gurun and Warachka's frog-in-the-pan hypothesis.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_1m = panel["ret_1m"]
    ret_12_1 = panel["ret_12_1"]
    vol_252 = panel["vol_252"]
    grp = ret_1m.groupby(level="ticker")
    pos_sum = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    count = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    for k in range(1, 13):
        r_k = grp.shift(k)
        valid = r_k.notna()
        pos_sum = pos_sum + (r_k &gt; 0).astype(float).where(valid, 0.0)
        count = count + valid.astype(float)
    pos = pos_sum / count
    neg = 1.0 - pos
    enough = count &gt;= 9
    sign_ret = np.sign(ret_12_1)
    ID = sign_ret * (neg - pos)
    cont = -ID
    denom_ok = vol_252 &gt; 0
    base = ret_12_1 / vol_252.where(denom_ok, np.nan)
    # cross-sectional z-score of base, per date
    def zscore(s):
        mu = s.mean()
        sd = s.std()
        if sd is None or sd == 0 or pd.isna(sd):
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        return (s - mu) / sd
    z = base.groupby(level="date").transform(zscore)
    score = z * (0.5 + cont)
    valid_mask = enough &amp; ret_12_1.notna() &amp; denom_ok &amp; base.notna() &amp; z.notna()
    score = score.where(valid_mask, np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>fundamental_momentum_price_gap</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Gap between fundamental momentum (YoY change in gross profit and operating cash flow scaled by assets) and…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Gap between fundamental momentum (YoY change in gross profit and operating cash flow scaled by assets) and price momentum (6m and 12-1m returns). Positive gap indicates improved fundamentals without commensurate price appreciation, predicting underreaction drift; near-neutral to raw price momentum.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    gp = panel['gp']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    assets = panel['assets']
    ret_6m = panel['ret_6m']
    ret_12_1 = panel['ret_12_1']
    gp_lag12 = gp.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    ncfo_lag12 = ncfo.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    dgp = (gp - gp_lag12) / assets.where(valid_assets)
    dcfo = (ncfo - ncfo_lag12) / assets.where(valid_assets)
    dgp = dgp.where(valid_assets &amp; gp_lag12.notna())
    dcfo = dcfo.where(valid_assets &amp; ncfo_lag12.notna())
    def cs_rank(s):
        return s.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    rank_dgp = cs_rank(dgp)
    rank_dcfo = cs_rank(dcfo)
    rank_ret6 = cs_rank(ret_6m)
    rank_ret12_1 = cs_rank(ret_12_1)
    fund_mom = pd.concat([rank_dgp, rank_dcfo], axis=1).mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    price_mom = pd.concat([rank_ret6, rank_ret12_1], axis=1).mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = fund_mom - price_mom
    invalid = dgp.isna() &amp; dcfo.isna()
    signal = signal.where(~invalid)
    missing_price = ret_6m.isna() &amp; ret_12_1.isna()
    signal = signal.where(~missing_price)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>gradual_information_momentum</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Frog-in-the-pan style momentum: conditions 12-1 momentum on the gradualness of the underlying monthly return…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Frog-in-the-pan style momentum: conditions 12-1 momentum on the gradualness of the underlying monthly return path (Da-Gurun-Warachka information discreteness proxy). Momentum is weighted up for stocks with many small same-signed monthly moves (gradual info flow) and down for stocks whose 12-month return was driven by a few discrete jumps.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_1m = panel["ret_1m"]
    ret_12_1 = panel["ret_12_1"]
    grouped = ret_1m.groupby(level="ticker")
    pos_count = None
    nonmiss_count = None
    for k in range(1, 13):
        lagged = grouped.shift(k)
        is_pos = (lagged &gt; 0).astype(float)
        is_nonmiss = lagged.notna().astype(float)
        is_pos = is_pos.where(lagged.notna(), 0.0)
        if pos_count is None:
            pos_count = is_pos
            nonmiss_count = is_nonmiss
        else:
            pos_count = pos_count + is_pos
            nonmiss_count = nonmiss_count + is_nonmiss
    pos_frac = pos_count / nonmiss_count.replace(0, np.nan)
    pos_frac = pos_frac.where(nonmiss_count &gt;= 9)
    sign_mom = np.sign(ret_12_1)
    ID = sign_mom * (1 - 2 * pos_frac)
    def cross_sectional_pct_rank(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        return s.groupby(level="date").rank(pct=True, method="average")
    def cross_sectional_zscore(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean = s.groupby(level="date").transform("mean")
        std = s.groupby(level="date").transform("std")
        z = (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
        return z
    id_pct_rank = cross_sectional_pct_rank(ID)
    g = 1 - id_pct_rank
    mom_z = cross_sectional_zscore(ret_12_1)
    signal = mom_z * g
    signal = signal.where(ret_12_1.notna())
    signal = signal.where(pos_frac.notna())
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>momentum_12_1</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Jegadeesh-Titman 12-1 month price momentum (skip most recent month)</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Jegadeesh-Titman 12-1 month price momentum (skip most recent month).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    return panel["ret_12_1"]</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>pure_calendar_month_seasonality_spread</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Seasonal spread: average of a stock's ret_1m in the same calendar month over prior years (lags 11,23,35,47,59…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonal spread: average of a stock's ret_1m in the same calendar month over prior years (lags 11,23,35,47,59 months) minus the average of all trailing 60 monthly returns, isolating pure calendar-month seasonality net of the stock's unconditional mean return level.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    grp = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    same_lags = [11, 23, 35, 47, 59]
    same_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in same_lags]
    same_df = pd.concat(same_shifts, axis=1)
    same_mean = same_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    same_count = same_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    all_lags = list(range(0, 60))
    all_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in all_lags]
    all_df = pd.concat(all_shifts, axis=1)
    all_mean = all_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    all_count = all_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    score = same_mean - all_mean
    valid = (same_count &gt;= 3) &amp; (all_count &gt;= 36)
    score = score.where(valid, np.nan)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>quiet_strength_low_attention_high</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Interaction of proximity-to-52-week-high with low turnover (low dollar volume relative to market cap) and…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of proximity-to-52-week-high with low turnover (low dollar volume relative to market cap) and 12-1 momentum, capturing 'quiet strength': slow diffusion of good news in low-attention names near their highs, which should earn positive future drift versus high-turnover attention-saturated names near their highs.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    dvol_21 = panel['dvol_21']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    ret_12_1 = panel['ret_12_1']
    valid = (
        high_ratio.notna()
        &amp; dvol_21.notna()
        &amp; marketcap.notna()
        &amp; ret_12_1.notna()
        &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
        &amp; (dvol_21 &gt; 0)
    )
    turn = dvol_21 / marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0)
    log_turn = np.log(turn.where(turn &gt; 0))
    ret_clipped = ret_12_1.clip(-1, 3)
    def zscore(s):
        grp = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        return (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
    zh = zscore(high_ratio.where(valid))
    zt = zscore(log_turn.where(valid))
    zm = zscore(ret_clipped.where(valid))
    score = 0.5 * zh + 0.5 * zm - zt
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_month_annual_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Firm-level same-calendar-month annual seasonality: average of a stock's ret_1m from the same calendar month…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Firm-level same-calendar-month annual seasonality: average of a stock's ret_1m from the same calendar month over the prior 1-5 years predicts current-month return (Heston &amp; Sadka seasonality effect).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    shifts = []
    for k in range(1, 6):
        s_k = ret.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12 * k)
        shifts.append(s_k)
    stacked = pd.concat(shifts, axis=1)
    count_valid = stacked.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mean_val = stacked.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = mean_val.where(count_valid &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_month_minus_offseason_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Firm-level calendar-month seasonality spread: mean of same-calendar-month historical 1m returns (at lags…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Firm-level calendar-month seasonality spread: mean of same-calendar-month historical 1m returns (at lags 12,24,36,48,60 months) minus mean of off-season average monthly return over the same lags. Isolates pure seasonal mispricing (Heston-Sadka / Keloharju-Linnainmaa-Nyberg).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_1m = panel['ret_1m']

    lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]

        other_list.append(other_k)

    count_available = same_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    same_mean = same_df.mean(axis=1)
    other_mean = other_df.mean(axis=1)
    signal = same_mean - other_mean
    signal = signal.where(count_available &gt;= 2)

<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:

<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:

<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    g = panel['ret_1m'].groupby(level='ticker')

<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:

<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel["ret_1m"]

    same_month = same_month.where(same_month_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    base_lag1 = grp.shift(1)
    base_grp = base_lag1.groupby(level="ticker")
    base_mean = base_grp.rolling(window=60, min_periods=36).mean()
    base_mean.index = base_mean.index.droplevel(0)
    base_mean = base_mean.reindex(ret.index)
    signal = same_month - base_mean
    signal = signal.where(same_month.notna() &amp; base_mean.notna(), np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>seasonal_same_month_return_persistence</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Same-calendar-month seasonality in stock returns: uses average return in the same calendar month over the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Same-calendar-month seasonality in stock returns: uses average return in the same calendar month over the past ~5 years (lags 11,23,35,47,59 months) relative to the average return over the other recent months (lags 1-10) to capture firm-specific seasonal return persistence.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    g = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    seasonal_lags = [11, 23, 35, 47, 59]
    seasonal_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in seasonal_lags]
    seasonal_df = pd.concat(seasonal_shifts, axis=1)
    seasonal_count = seasonal_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    seas = seasonal_df.mean(axis=1)
    seas = seas.where(seasonal_count &gt;= 3)
    other_lags = list(range(1, 11))
    other_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in other_lags]
    other_df = pd.concat(other_shifts, axis=1)
    other_count = other_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    other = other_df.mean(axis=1)
    other = other.where(other_count &gt;= 1)
    score = seas - other
    score = score.where(seasonal_count &gt;= 3)
    score.index = panel.index
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>annual_return_seasonality_spread</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Seasonality spread: mean of same-calendar-month returns over prior years (12/24/36/48/60 month lags) minus…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonality spread: mean of same-calendar-month returns over prior years (12/24/36/48/60 month lags) minus the stock's average trailing 60-month return, isolating the pure seasonal component of monthly returns as documented by Heston and Sadka.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    g = panel['ret_1m'].groupby(level='ticker')
    lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    shifted = [g.shift(k) for k in lags]
    same_month_df = pd.concat(shifted, axis=1)
    same_month = same_month_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    same_month_count = same_month_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    same_month = same_month.where(same_month_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    shifted1 = g.shift(1)
    all_month = (
        shifted1.groupby(level='ticker')
        .rolling(60, min_periods=24)
        .mean()
    )
    # rolling on grouped series returns a MultiIndex with an extra ticker level
    all_month = all_month.droplevel(0)
    all_month = all_month.reindex(panel.index)
    signal = same_month - all_month
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>attention_shock_amplified_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Short-horizon reversal amplified by abnormal dollar-volume shocks: reversal (ret_1m scaled by vol_252) is…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Short-horizon reversal amplified by abnormal dollar-volume shocks: reversal (ret_1m scaled by vol_252) is combined multiplicatively with a rank-normalized measure of how far current log dollar volume deviates from its trailing 12-month average, capturing attention/liquidity-driven demand shocks that tend to reverse.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dvol_21 = panel["dvol_21"]
    ret_1m = panel["ret_1m"]
    vol_252 = panel["vol_252"]
    base = np.log(dvol_21.where(dvol_21 &gt; 0))
    grp = base.groupby(level="ticker")
    lags = [grp.shift(k) for k in range(1, 13)]
    lag_df = pd.concat(lags, axis=1)
    nonmissing_count = lag_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    avg = lag_df.mean(axis=1)
    vshock = base - avg
    vshock = vshock.where(nonmissing_count &gt;= 9)
    # cross-sectional rank normalization into [-0.5, 0.5], per date
    def rank_norm(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        valid = s.dropna()
        if len(valid) == 0:
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        ranks = valid.rank(method="average")
        n = len(valid)
        if n &gt; 1:
            normed = (ranks - 1) / (n - 1) - 0.5
        else:
            normed = pd.Series(0.0, index=valid.index)
        out = pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        out.loc[valid.index] = normed
        return out
    vshock_c = vshock.groupby(level="date").apply(rank_norm)
    vshock_c.index = vshock.index
    # reversal component
    r = ret_1m.where(vol_252 &gt; 0) / vol_252.where(vol_252 &gt; 0)
    def winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        valid = s.dropna()
        if len(valid) == 0:
            return s
        lo = valid.quantile(0.01)
        hi = valid.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    r_wins = r.groupby(level="date").apply(winsorize)
    r_wins.index = r.index
    signal = r_wins * (0.5 + vshock_c)
    # enforce missing-data policy: require dvol_21, ret_1m, vol_252 valid
    valid_mask = dvol_21.notna() &amp; ret_1m.notna() &amp; vol_252.notna() &amp; (vol_252 &gt; 0)
    signal = signal.where(valid_mask)
