    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>attention_shock_return_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interaction of abnormal turnover (attention shock) with trailing 1m return</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of abnormal turnover (attention shock) with trailing 1m return. High abnormal turnover accompanying a large recent gain forecasts reversal; high abnormal turnover accompanying a loss forecasts a bounce. Uses log turnover relative to its trailing 12m (min 6) mean, times ret_1m, with expected_sign=-1 so the harness implements the reversal orientation.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dvol = panel['dvol_21']
    mcap = panel['marketcap']
    ret_1m = panel['ret_1m']
    turn = (dvol / mcap).where((dvol &gt; 0) &amp; (mcap &gt; 0))
    lt = np.log(turn)
    lt_shifted = lt.groupby(level='ticker').shift(1)
    base = (
        lt_shifted.groupby(level='ticker')
        .rolling(12, min_periods=6)
        .mean()
        .reset_index(level=0, drop=True)
    )
    abn = lt - base
    score = abn * ret_1m
    score = score.where(abn.notna() &amp; ret_1m.notna())
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>attention_spike_return_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interaction of abnormal 21d dollar volume (attention spike) with recent 1m return scaled by volatility:…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of abnormal 21d dollar volume (attention spike) with recent 1m return scaled by volatility: reverses momentum on high-attention runs and rewards liquidity discount on high-attention sell-offs.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dvol = panel['dvol_21']
    ret_1m = panel['ret_1m']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    grp = dvol.groupby(level='ticker')
    lagged = [grp.shift(k) for k in range(1, 13)]
    stacked = pd.concat(lagged, axis=1)
    valid_count = stacked.notna().sum(axis=1)
    avg_dvol = stacked.mean(axis=1)
    valid_avg = (valid_count &gt;= 6) &amp; (avg_dvol &gt; 0)
    avg_dvol = avg_dvol.where(valid_avg)
    valid_dvol = dvol &gt; 0
    abn_vol = np.log(dvol / avg_dvol)
    abn_vol = abn_vol.where(valid_dvol &amp; valid_avg)
    abn_vol_clipped = abn_vol.clip(-2, 2)
    vol_floor = vol_252.clip(lower=0.05)
    valid_vol = vol_252 &gt; 0
    scaled_ret = ret_1m / vol_floor
    scaled_ret = scaled_ret.where(valid_vol)
    scaled_ret_clipped = scaled_ret.clip(-3, 3)
    signal = -1.0 * abn_vol_clipped * scaled_ret_clipped
    valid = (
        valid_avg
        &amp; valid_dvol
        &amp; valid_vol
        &amp; ret_1m.notna()
        &amp; dvol.notna()
    )
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>dollar_trend_fx_beta_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interacts a stock's trailing USD beta with the realized 12-month dollar trend: cross-sectionally z-scored,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interacts a stock's trailing USD beta with the realized 12-month dollar trend: cross-sectionally z-scored, winsorized beta_usd_252 (excluding names with weak |corr_usd_252|) is scaled by tanh of the fractional 12m dollar trend, producing a sign-switching macro-conditioned score.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta = panel['beta_usd_252']
    corr = panel['corr_usd_252']
    macro_usd = panel['macro_usd']
    macro_usd_chg12m = panel['macro_usd_chg12m']
    # base validity: all inputs present
    valid = beta.notna() &amp; corr.notna() &amp; macro_usd.notna() &amp; macro_usd_chg12m.notna()
    # winsorize beta at 1st/99th percentile per date
    def winsorize(s):
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    beta_masked = beta.where(valid)
    beta_wins = beta_masked.groupby(level='date').transform(winsorize)
    # cross-sectional zscore per date
    def zscore(s):
        mu = s.mean()
        sd = s.std()
        if sd is None or not np.isfinite(sd) or sd == 0:
            return s * np.nan
        return (s - mu) / sd
    zb = beta_wins.groupby(level='date').transform(zscore)
    # exclude weak corr names
    weak_corr = corr.abs() &lt;= 0.05
    zb = zb.where(~weak_corr)
    # dollar trend, same for all tickers on a date
    trend = macro_usd_chg12m / macro_usd.where(macro_usd &gt; 0)
    trend_signal = np.tanh(trend / 0.05)
    # if macro_usd or macro_usd_chg12m missing for date -&gt; NaN for all tickers that date
    macro_valid_by_date = (macro_usd.notna() &amp; macro_usd_chg12m.notna()).groupby(level='date').transform('all')
    signal = zb * trend_signal
    signal = signal.where(valid &amp; macro_valid_by_date)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>expected_earnings_announcement_month</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Scores stocks by how close their expected next earnings announcement is to the upcoming month, based on the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Scores stocks by how close their expected next earnings announcement is to the upcoming month, based on the gap between the current point-in-time date and the last SEC filing date. Firms whose gap since last filing is close to ~72 days (implying an announcement roughly one quarter after the prior filing) score highest, capturing the earnings-announcement attention premium.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    asof_date = pd.to_datetime(panel['asof_date'])
    fund_datekey = pd.to_datetime(panel['fund_datekey'])
    gap_days = (asof_date - fund_datekey).dt.days
    score = np.exp(-((gap_days - 72.0) ** 2) / (2 * 15.0 ** 2))
    invalid = fund_datekey.isna() | gap_days.isna() | (gap_days &gt; 200)
    score = score.where(~invalid, np.nan)
    score = score.reindex(panel.index)
    score.name = self.name
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>filing_staleness_information_neglect</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Abnormal filing staleness: days elapsed since the most recent SEC filing (fund_datekey) relative to the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Abnormal filing staleness: days elapsed since the most recent SEC filing (fund_datekey) relative to the industry-median lag on the same date. Unusually stale filings signal information friction / neglect and predict negative future drift; fresh filings predict positive drift.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    asof = pd.to_datetime(panel['asof_date'])
    datekey = pd.to_datetime(panel['fund_datekey'])
    lag_days = (asof - datekey).dt.days
    valid = datekey.notna() &amp; (lag_days &gt;= 0) &amp; (lag_days &lt;= self.MAX_LAG_DAYS)
    lag_valid = lag_days.where(valid)
    industry = panel['industry']
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'lag': lag_valid,
        'industry': industry,
    }, index=panel.index)
    group_keys = [df.index.get_level_values('date'), df['industry']]
    group_median = df.groupby(group_keys)['lag'].transform('median')
    group_count = df.groupby(group_keys)['lag'].transform('count')
    abn = df['lag'] - group_median
    abn = abn.where(group_count &gt;= self.MIN_GROUP_SIZE)
    abn = abn.where(valid)
    abn.name = self.name
    return abn</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>hidden_rate_duration_mismatch</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Combines fundamental duration proxies (log P/B, log P/S) with trailing realized rate beta to identify…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Combines fundamental duration proxies (log P/B, log P/S) with trailing realized rate beta to identify long-duration names whose historical beta understates true rate sensitivity; conditions the mismatch score on the 12-month change in the 10y yield to time macro-state-dependent duration risk.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pb = panel['pb']
    ps = panel['ps']
    beta_rates = panel['beta_rates_252']
    dgs10_chg12m = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m']
    log_pb = np.log(pb.where(pb &gt; 0))
    log_ps = np.log(ps.where(ps &gt; 0))
    def cs_zscore(s):
        grp = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        return (s - mean) / std.where(std &gt; 0)
    zpb = cs_zscore(log_pb)
    zps = cs_zscore(log_ps)
    zrb = cs_zscore(beta_rates)
    hidden_duration = zpb + zps + zrb
    signal = -hidden_duration * np.tanh(dgs10_chg12m)
    mask = zpb.notna() &amp; zps.notna() &amp; zrb.notna() &amp; dgs10_chg12m.notna()
    signal = signal.where(mask)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>hidden_refinancing_rate_exposure</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interaction of net short-term debt burden (fundamental rollover risk) with a stock's realized beta to rates:…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of net short-term debt burden (fundamental rollover risk) with a stock's realized beta to rates: firms with high net short-term debt but positive rate beta are mispriced 'hidden' rollover-risk exposures, whose returns should suffer when short rates rise (and benefit when they fall). Signal = z(net_st) * z(beta_rates_252) * clipped 12m change in 2y yield.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debtc = panel['debtc']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    assets = panel['assets']
    beta_rates = panel['beta_rates_252']
    macro_chg = panel['macro_dgs2_chg12m']
    valid = (
        debtc.notna()
        &amp; cashneq.notna()
        &amp; assets.notna()
        &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
        &amp; beta_rates.notna()
        &amp; macro_chg.notna()
    )
    net_st = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    net_st[valid] = (debtc[valid] - cashneq[valid]) / assets[valid]
    beta_valid = beta_rates.where(valid)
    z1 = net_st.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorized_zscore)
    z2 = beta_valid.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorized_zscore)
    mismatch = z1 * z2
    macro_clipped = macro_chg.clip(lower=-1.5, upper=1.5)
    score = mismatch * macro_clipped
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>long_term_reversal_sentiment_conditioned</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Long-term (t-36 to t-12) reversal signal conditioned on past-only consumer sentiment state: reversal weighted…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Long-term (t-36 to t-12) reversal signal conditioned on past-only consumer sentiment state: reversal weighted more heavily when sentiment is above its own trailing average (elevated optimism), consistent with Baker-Wurgler/Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan sentiment-conditioned mispricing correction.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    r1 = ret_12m.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    r2 = ret_12m.groupby(level='ticker').shift(24)
    cum_36_12 = (1 + r1) * (1 + r2) - 1
    # date-level sentiment series
    sent_by_date = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    sent_by_date = sent_by_date.sort_index()
    rolling_mean = sent_by_date.rolling(36, min_periods=24).mean().shift(1)
    sent_state = sent_by_date / rolling_mean.where(rolling_mean &gt; 0)
    w_by_date = pd.Series(
        np.where(sent_state &gt; 1.0, 1.0, 0.3),
        index=sent_state.index,
    )
    w_by_date = w_by_date.where(sent_state.notna())
    # broadcast weight to (date, ticker) index
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    w = w_by_date.reindex(dates)
    w.index = panel.index
    score = cum_36_12 * w
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_beta_dispersion_crowding_rotation</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Entropy of squared macro correlations (oil, rates, usd, credit, vix) capturing the shape of a stock's macro…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Entropy of squared macro correlations (oil, rates, usd, credit, vix) capturing the shape of a stock's macro exposure profile. Diffuse macro exposure (high entropy) earns a premium for undiversifiable macro risk; concentrated exposure in a single fashionable factor is subject to crowded-flow reversals.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = ['corr_oil_252', 'corr_rates_252', 'corr_usd_252',
            'corr_credit_252', 'corr_vix_252']
    df = panel[cols].copy()
    n_valid = df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    sq = df.pow(2)
    sq_filled = sq.fillna(0.0)
    sum_sq = sq_filled.sum(axis=1)
    valid_mask = (n_valid &gt;= 4) &amp; (sum_sq &gt; 0)
    w = sq_filled.div(sum_sq.where(sum_sq &gt; 0, np.nan), axis=0)
    entropy = -(w * np.log(w + 1e-12)).sum(axis=1)
    score = entropy.where(valid_mask, np.nan)
    score.name = self.name
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_trend_attributed_return_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Contrarian signal on the macro-attributed component of past returns: sums cross-sectionally z-scored macro…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Contrarian signal on the macro-attributed component of past returns: sums cross-sectionally z-scored macro betas (rates, oil, usd, credit, vix) signed by the direction of the corresponding 12-month macro trend. Stocks with high macro-attributed 'performance' are expected to mean-revert as macro trends are less persistent than the market extrapolates.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta_cols = {
        'rates': 'beta_rates_252',
        'oil': 'beta_oil_252',
        'usd': 'beta_usd_252',
        'credit': 'beta_credit_252',
        'vix': 'beta_vix_252',
    }
    chg_cols = {
        'rates': 'macro_dgs10_chg12m',
        'oil': 'macro_oil_chg12m',
        'usd': 'macro_usd_chg12m',
        'credit': 'macro_baa_spread_chg12m',
        'vix': 'macro_vix_chg12m',
    }
    contributions = []
    valid_masks = []
    for f in beta_cols:
        beta_col = beta_cols[f]
        chg_col = chg_cols[f]
        if beta_col not in panel.columns or chg_col not in panel.columns:
            continue
        beta = panel[beta_col]
        chg = panel[chg_col]
        # cross-sectional zscore per date, clipped
        grp = beta.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        zb = (beta - mean) / std
        zb = zb.where(std &gt; 0, np.nan)
        zb = zb.clip(-3, 3)
        d = np.sign(chg)
        d = d.where(chg.notna() &amp; (chg != 0), np.nan)
        contrib = d * zb
        valid = contrib.notna()
        contributions.append(contrib.fillna(0.0))
        valid_masks.append(valid)
    if not contributions:
        return pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    total = contributions[0]
    for c in contributions[1:]:
        total = total + c
    count = valid_masks[0].astype(int)
    for v in valid_masks[1:]:
        count = count + v.astype(int)
    result = total.where(count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    result.name = None
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_trend_beta_alignment</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Aligns stocks' trailing cross-asset macro betas (oil, USD, rates, credit) with the prevailing direction of…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aligns stocks' trailing cross-asset macro betas (oil, USD, rates, credit) with the prevailing direction of the corresponding macro trend, exploiting gradual investor diffusion of macro information into stock prices with differentiated factor exposure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    # --- date-level macro trends (unique per date) ---
    macro_cols = [
        'macro_oil', 'macro_oil_chg12m',
        'macro_usd', 'macro_usd_chg12m',
        'macro_dgs10_chg12m', 'macro_baa_spread_chg12m',
    ]
    macro_df = panel[macro_cols].copy()
    macro_df = macro_df.reset_index(level='ticker', drop=True)
    macro_df = macro_df[~macro_df.index.duplicated(keep='first')].sort_index()
    # unitless trends with guarded denominators
    oil_denom = macro_df['macro_oil'].where(macro_df['macro_oil'] &gt; 0)
    usd_denom = macro_df['macro_usd'].where(macro_df['macro_usd'] &gt; 0)
    raw_tr_oil = macro_df['macro_oil_chg12m'] / oil_denom
    raw_tr_usd = macro_df['macro_usd_chg12m'] / usd_denom
    raw_tr_rate = macro_df['macro_dgs10_chg12m']
    raw_tr_cred = macro_df['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    tr_oil = self._z_exp_past_only(raw_tr_oil)
    tr_usd = self._z_exp_past_only(raw_tr_usd)
    tr_rate = self._z_exp_past_only(raw_tr_rate)
    tr_cred = self._z_exp_past_only(raw_tr_cred)
    # broadcast date-level trends back onto panel
    tr_oil_b = tr_oil.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
    tr_usd_b = tr_usd.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
    tr_rate_b = tr_rate.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
    tr_cred_b = tr_cred.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
    tr_oil_s = pd.Series(tr_oil_b, index=panel.index)
    tr_usd_s = pd.Series(tr_usd_b, index=panel.index)
    tr_rate_s = pd.Series(tr_rate_b, index=panel.index)
    tr_cred_s = pd.Series(tr_cred_b, index=panel.index)
    # --- cross-sectional z-scores of betas within each date ---
    def cs_z(col: str) -&gt; pd.Series:
        s = panel[col]
        grp = s.groupby(level='date')
        mean = grp.transform('mean')
        std = grp.transform('std')
        z = (s - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
        return z
    bo = cs_z('beta_oil_252')
    bu = cs_z('beta_usd_252')
    br = cs_z('beta_rates_252')
    bc = cs_z('beta_credit_252')
    n_valid = (
        bo.notna().astype(int)
        + bu.notna().astype(int)
        + br.notna().astype(int)
        + bc.notna().astype(int)
    )
    score = (
        bo.fillna(0) * tr_oil_s
        + bu.fillna(0) * tr_usd_s
        + br.fillna(0) * tr_rate_s
        + bc.fillna(0) * tr_cred_s
    )
    score = score.where(n_valid &gt;= 3)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_trend_beta_spillover</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Combines each stock's trailing macro betas (oil, usd, rates, credit) with the past-only standardized 12m…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Combines each stock's trailing macro betas (oil, usd, rates, credit) with the past-only standardized 12m trend in the corresponding macro factor to capture slow diffusion of macro trends into exposed equities.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    # date-level macro series (one value per date)
    macro_oil = panel['macro_oil'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_oil_chg12m = panel['macro_oil_chg12m'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_usd = panel['macro_usd'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_usd_chg12m = panel['macro_usd_chg12m'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_dgs10_chg12m = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_baa_spread_chg12m = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro_oil = macro_oil.sort_index()
    macro_oil_chg12m = macro_oil_chg12m.sort_index()
    macro_usd = macro_usd.sort_index()
    macro_usd_chg12m = macro_usd_chg12m.sort_index()
    macro_dgs10_chg12m = macro_dgs10_chg12m.sort_index()
    macro_baa_spread_chg12m = macro_baa_spread_chg12m.sort_index()
    oil_denom = macro_oil - macro_oil_chg12m
    oil_tr = macro_oil_chg12m / oil_denom.where(oil_denom &gt; 0)
    usd_denom = macro_usd - macro_usd_chg12m
    usd_tr = macro_usd_chg12m / usd_denom.where(usd_denom &gt; 0)
    rate_tr = macro_dgs10_chg12m
    cred_tr = macro_baa_spread_chg12m
    def past_only_z(x: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        x_shift = x.shift(1)
        std = x_shift.expanding(min_periods=36).std()
        return x / std.where(std &gt; 0)
    z_oil = past_only_z(oil_tr)
    z_usd = past_only_z(usd_tr)
    z_rate = past_only_z(rate_tr)
    z_cred = past_only_z(cred_tr)
    # map back to panel by date
    z_oil_p = dates.map(z_oil)
    z_usd_p = dates.map(z_usd)
    z_rate_p = dates.map(z_rate)
    z_cred_p = dates.map(z_cred)
    z_oil_p = pd.Series(z_oil_p, index=panel.index)
    z_usd_p = pd.Series(z_usd_p, index=panel.index)
    z_rate_p = pd.Series(z_rate_p, index=panel.index)
    z_cred_p = pd.Series(z_cred_p, index=panel.index)
    # winsorize betas cross-sectionally per date
    beta_oil = panel['beta_oil_252'].groupby(level='date').transform(self._winsorize)
    beta_usd = panel['beta_usd_252'].groupby(level='date').transform(self._winsorize)
    beta_rates = panel['beta_rates_252'].groupby(level='date').transform(self._winsorize)
    beta_credit = panel['beta_credit_252'].groupby(level='date').transform(self._winsorize)
    term_oil = beta_oil * z_oil_p
    term_usd = beta_usd * z_usd_p
    term_rate = beta_rates * z_rate_p
    term_cred = beta_credit * z_cred_p
    terms = pd.concat(
        [term_oil.rename('t_oil'), term_usd.rename('t_usd'),
         term_rate.rename('t_rate'), term_cred.rename('t_cred')],
        axis=1
    )
    valid_count = terms.notna().sum(axis=1)
    total = terms.sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    result = total.where(valid_count &gt;= 3)
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_trend_exposure_alignment</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Aligns firm-level macro betas (oil, USD, rates, credit) with the persistent trend in those macro factors…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aligns firm-level macro betas (oil, USD, rates, credit) with the persistent trend in those macro factors (expanding z-scored 12m changes), exploiting slow diffusion of cross-asset macro trends into equity cash-flow expectations.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    idx = panel.index
    macro_cols = {
        'oil': 'macro_oil_chg12m',
        'usd': 'macro_usd_chg12m',
        'rates': 'macro_dgs10_chg12m',
        'credit': 'macro_baa_spread_chg12m',
    }
    beta_cols = {
        'oil': 'beta_oil_252',
        'usd': 'beta_usd_252',
        'rates': 'beta_rates_252',
        'credit': 'beta_credit_252',
    }
    # Build date-level macro series (one value per date) and compute expanding z-scores
    z_terms = {}
    dates = idx.get_level_values('date')
    for key, col in macro_cols.items():
        if col in panel.columns:
            per_date = panel[col].groupby(level='date').first()
            per_date = per_date.sort_index()
            z_per_date = self._expanding_z(per_date)
            z_terms[key] = z_per_date.reindex(dates).to_numpy()
        else:
            z_terms[key] = np.zeros(len(idx))
    # Winsorize betas cross-sectionally per date
    beta_win = {}
    beta_missing_mask = pd.Series(False, index=idx)
    for key, col in beta_cols.items():
        if col in panel.columns:
            b = panel[col]
            beta_missing_mask = beta_missing_mask | b.isna()
            b_w = self._winsorize_by_date(b)
            beta_win[key] = b_w
        else:
            beta_missing_mask = pd.Series(True, index=idx)
            beta_win[key] = pd.Series(np.nan, index=idx)
    score = pd.Series(0.0, index=idx)
    for key in macro_cols.keys():
        b = beta_win[key].fillna(0.0)
        z = pd.Series(z_terms[key], index=idx)
        score = score + b * z
    score = score.where(~beta_missing_mask, np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>oil_beta_trend_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interaction of trailing stock beta to oil price moves with a 12m oil price trend regime scaler</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of trailing stock beta to oil price moves with a 12m oil price trend regime scaler. Long high-oil-beta stocks when oil has trended up over the past year, short them when oil has trended down, capturing gradual diffusion of commodity trends into cash-flow-exposed equity valuations.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta_oil = panel['beta_oil_252']
    corr_oil = panel['corr_oil_252']
    oil_chg12m = panel['macro_oil_chg12m']
    oil_trend = np.tanh(oil_chg12m / 20.0)
    exposure = beta_oil.where(corr_oil.abs() &gt; 0.05)
    def _zscore(x):
        std = x.std()
        if std is None or std == 0 or pd.isna(std):
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=x.index)
        return (x - x.median()) / std
    exposure_z = exposure.groupby(level='date').transform(_zscore)
    signal = exposure_z * oil_trend
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>pre_earnings_filing_clock_premium</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Within-firm earnings-announcement-clock seasonality: proxies proximity to the next expected SEC filing using…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Within-firm earnings-announcement-clock seasonality: proxies proximity to the next expected SEC filing using days since the last point-in-time filing date. Peaks when days_since_filing is near 85 (i.e., the next filing is likely due within the coming month), capturing the documented earnings announcement premium driven by announcement-risk compensation and attention scarcity.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    datekey = pd.to_datetime(panel["fund_datekey"], errors="coerce")
    asof = pd.to_datetime(panel["asof_date"], errors="coerce")
    valid_dates = datekey.notna() &amp; asof.notna()
    days_since_filing = (asof - datekey).dt.days
    cycle_position = -(days_since_filing - 85).abs().astype(float)
    in_range = (days_since_filing &gt;= 20) &amp; (days_since_filing &lt;= 200)
    signal = cycle_position.where(valid_dates &amp; in_range, np.nan)
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>predicted_dividend_month_premium</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Predicts dividend-clientele driven price pressure by inferring implied monthly dividend yield from the wedge…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Predicts dividend-clientele driven price pressure by inferring implied monthly dividend yield from the wedge between adjusted and raw close returns, then projecting it forward 12 months using sticky dividend payment calendars, with support confirmation from recent dividend history.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    closeadj = panel['closeadj']
    close = panel['close']
    grp_adj = closeadj.groupby(level='ticker')
    grp_close = close.groupby(level='ticker')
    closeadj_prev = grp_adj.shift(1)
    close_prev = grp_close.shift(1)
    valid = (
        closeadj.notna() &amp; closeadj_prev.notna() &amp; (closeadj_prev != 0)
        &amp; close.notna() &amp; close_prev.notna() &amp; (close_prev != 0)
    )
    radj = (closeadj / closeadj_prev) - 1.0
    rraw = (close / close_prev) - 1.0
    diff = radj - rraw
    impl_yld = diff.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.05)
    impl_yld = impl_yld.where(valid, np.nan)
    # split artifact detection
    split_artifact = diff.abs() &gt; 0.5
    impl_yld = impl_yld.where(~split_artifact, np.nan)
    # need sufficient history for shift(12): closeadj/close shifted 12 must exist
    closeadj_12 = grp_adj.shift(12)
    close_12 = grp_close.shift(12)
    closeadj_13 = grp_adj.shift(13)
    close_13 = grp_close.shift(13)
    hist_ok = (
        closeadj_12.notna() &amp; closeadj_13.notna()
        &amp; close_12.notna() &amp; close_13.notna()
    )
    impl_yld_grp = impl_yld.groupby(level='ticker')
    pred = impl_yld_grp.shift(12)
    pred = pred.where(hist_ok, np.nan)
    shift3 = impl_yld_grp.shift(3)
    shift12 = impl_yld_grp.shift(12)
    support_cond = (shift3 &gt; 0) | (shift12 &gt; 0)
    support = support_cond.astype(float)
    support = support.where(shift3.notna() | shift12.notna(), np.nan)
    score = pred * support
    # no dividend history in past 12m -&gt; score 0
    # define "dividend history in past 12m" as any positive impl_yld in trailing 12 shifts (1..12)
    pos_yld = (impl_yld &gt; 0).astype(float)
    pos_yld_grp = pos_yld.groupby(level='ticker')
    rolling_hist = pos_yld_grp.transform(
        lambda s: s.shift(1).rolling(window=12, min_periods=1).max()
    )
    no_history = rolling_hist.fillna(0) == 0
    score = score.where(~no_history, 0.0)
    score = score.reindex(panel.index)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>rate_beta_duration_mismatch</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Mismatch between valuation-implied duration and realized rate beta, aligned with the sign of the trailing 12m…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Mismatch between valuation-implied duration and realized rate beta, aligned with the sign of the trailing 12m change in 10y yields; signal is masked where the stock's rate correlation is weak.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pb = panel['pb']
    ps = panel['ps']
    divyield = panel['divyield'].fillna(0)
    beta_rates = panel['beta_rates_252']
    corr_rates = panel['corr_rates_252']
    macro_chg = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m']
    def rk(x):
        return x.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    D = (rk(pb) + rk(ps) + (1 - rk(divyield))) / 3
    beta_mean = beta_rates.groupby(level='date').transform('mean')
    beta_std = beta_rates.groupby(level='date').transform('std')
    zb = (beta_rates - beta_mean) / beta_std.where(beta_std &gt; 0)
    D_std = D.groupby(level='date').transform('std')
    zD = (D - 0.5) / D_std.where(D_std &gt; 0)
    mismatch = zb + zD
    signal = mismatch * np.sign(macro_chg)
    invalid = (
        pb.isna()
        | ps.isna()
        | beta_rates.isna()
        | corr_rates.isna()
        | macro_chg.isna()
        | (corr_rates.abs() &lt; 0.02)
    )
    signal = signal.where(~invalid, np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>relative_month_of_year_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Stock-level calendar month-of-year seasonality: average return in the same calendar month over the past 1-5…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Stock-level calendar month-of-year seasonality: average return in the same calendar month over the past 1-5 years, benchmarked against the average return in adjacent calendar months to strip out level/drift effects. Higher relative same-month seasonality predicts higher future return.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    grp = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    same_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    adj_lags = [11, 13, 23, 25, 35, 37, 47, 49]
    same_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in same_lags]
    adj_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in adj_lags]
    same_df = pd.concat(same_shifts, axis=1)
    adj_df = pd.concat(adj_shifts, axis=1)
    same_count = same_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    adj_count = adj_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    same_mean = same_df.mean(axis=1)
    adj_mean = adj_df.mean(axis=1)
    signal = same_mean - adj_mean
    valid = (same_count &gt;= 3) &amp; (adj_count &gt;= 5)
    signal = signal.where(valid, np.nan)
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>residual_same_month_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Heston-Sadka same-calendar-month seasonality: average of a stock's ret_1m in the same calendar month over the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Heston-Sadka same-calendar-month seasonality: average of a stock's ret_1m in the same calendar month over the trailing 5 years, minus its average ret_12m/12 over the same lags to strip out level/momentum, isolating a firm-specific seasonal return component.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    g = panel.groupby(level='ticker')
    ret1m_lags = [g['ret_1m'].shift(k) for k in (12, 24, 36, 48, 60)]
    ret12m_lags = [g['ret_12m'].shift(k) for k in (12, 24, 36, 48, 60)]
    ret1m_df = pd.concat(ret1m_lags, axis=1)
    ret12m_df = pd.concat(ret12m_lags, axis=1)
    valid_count = ret1m_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    seas = ret1m_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    seas = seas.where(valid_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    base = ret12m_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True) / 12.0
    base_valid = ret12m_df.notna().any(axis=1)
    base = base.where(base_valid, 0.0)
    signal = seas - base
    signal = signal.where(seas.notna(), np.nan)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_calendar_month_return_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Seasonal same-calendar-month return predictability (Heston &amp; Sadka): averages a stock's ret_1m from 12, 24,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonal same-calendar-month return predictability (Heston &amp; Sadka): averages a stock's ret_1m from 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months ago (same calendar month in prior years) to predict its return this month, requiring at least 3 valid lags.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    grouped = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    winsorized_lags = []
    for k in lags:
        lagged = grouped.shift(k)
        # cross-sectional winsorization at 1st/99th percentile, per date
        def _winsorize(s):
            lo = s.quantile(0.01)
            hi = s.quantile(0.99)
            return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
        wins = lagged.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorize)
        winsorized_lags.append(wins)
    stacked = pd.concat(winsorized_lags, axis=1)
    stacked.columns = [f"lag_{k}" for k in lags]
    count_valid = stacked.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mean_val = stacked.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = mean_val.where(count_valid &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_calendar_month_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Seasonality factor based on Heston and Sadka (2008): averages a stock's same-calendar-month historical…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonality factor based on Heston and Sadka (2008): averages a stock's same-calendar-month historical 1-month returns lagged 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months, winsorized cross-sectionally at the 1st/99th percentile per date, requiring at least 3 non-missing lags.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    ret = panel["ret_1m"]
    winsorized_lags = []
    for k in lags:
        r_k = ret.groupby(level="ticker").shift(k)
        def _winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
            valid = s.dropna()
            if valid.empty:
                return s
            lo = valid.quantile(0.01)
            hi = valid.quantile(0.99)
            return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
        r_k_w = r_k.groupby(level="date").transform(_winsorize)
        winsorized_lags.append(r_k_w)
    lag_df = pd.concat(winsorized_lags, axis=1)
    lag_df.columns = [f"lag_{k}" for k in lags]
    valid_count = lag_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mean_ret = lag_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    signal = mean_ret.where(valid_count &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_month_return_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Same-calendar-month return seasonality: average of ret_1m at lags of 12,24,36,48,60 months (same calendar…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Same-calendar-month return seasonality: average of ret_1m at lags of 12,24,36,48,60 months (same calendar month) minus average of ret_1m at all other lags 1..60 (excluding multiples of 12). Requires at least 3 non-missing same-month observations.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret = panel['ret_1m']
    grp = ret.groupby(level='ticker')
    same_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    other_lags = [k for k in range(1, 61) if k % 12 != 0]
    same_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in same_lags]
    other_shifts = [grp.shift(k) for k in other_lags]
    same_df = pd.concat(same_shifts, axis=1)
    other_df = pd.concat(other_shifts, axis=1)
    same_count = same_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    same_mean = same_df.mean(axis=1)
    other_mean = other_df.mean(axis=1)
    signal = same_mean - other_mean
    valid = (same_count &gt;= 3) &amp; other_mean.notna()
    signal = signal.where(valid, np.nan)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_month_return_seasonality_spread</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Firm-level calendar-month return seasonality: averages a stock's own ret_1m in the same calendar month over…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Firm-level calendar-month return seasonality: averages a stock's own ret_1m in the same calendar month over the last 1-5 years (lags 12,24,36,48,60) and differences it against the average return in non-anniversary months (lags 3,6,9,15,18,21,27,33), isolating a seasonal effect distinct from generic long-horizon momentum/reversal.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    g = panel['ret_1m'].groupby(level='ticker')
    seasonal_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    nonseasonal_lags = [3, 6, 9, 15, 18, 21, 27, 33]
    seasonal_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in seasonal_lags]
    nonseasonal_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in nonseasonal_lags]
    seasonal_df = pd.concat(seasonal_shifts, axis=1)
    nonseasonal_df = pd.concat(nonseasonal_shifts, axis=1)
    seasonal_count = seasonal_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    nonseasonal_count = nonseasonal_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    seasonal_mean = seasonal_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    nonseasonal_mean = nonseasonal_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    seasonal_mean = seasonal_mean.where(seasonal_count &gt;= 3)
    nonseasonal_mean = nonseasonal_mean.where(nonseasonal_count &gt;= 4)
    signal = seasonal_mean - nonseasonal_mean
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_month_seasonal_persistence</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Same-calendar-month seasonal persistence: average of a stock's ret_1m lagged by 12,24,36,48,60 months minus…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Same-calendar-month seasonal persistence: average of a stock's ret_1m lagged by 12,24,36,48,60 months minus average of ret_1m lagged by 13,25,37 months (adjacent-month control), requiring at least 3 non-NaN seasonal lags.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    g = panel['ret_1m'].groupby(level='ticker')
    seas_lags = [12, 24, 36, 48, 60]
    nonseas_lags = [13, 25, 37]
    seas_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in seas_lags]
    seas_df = pd.concat(seas_shifts, axis=1)
    seas_count = seas_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    seas_mean = seas_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    seas_mean = seas_mean.where(seas_count &gt;= 3)
    nonseas_shifts = [g.shift(k) for k in nonseas_lags]
    nonseas_df = pd.concat(nonseas_shifts, axis=1)
    nonseas_mean = nonseas_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    nonseas_mean = nonseas_mean.fillna(0.0)
    score = seas_mean - nonseas_mean
    score = score.where(seas_count &gt;= 3)
    score = score.reindex(panel.index)
    score.name = self.name
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>same_quarter_earnings_seasonality</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Seasonal earnings anticipation signal: compares net income from the same fiscal quarter one year ago (about…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonal earnings anticipation signal: compares net income from the same fiscal quarter one year ago (about to be reported again) to the firm's trailing four-quarter average net income, scaled by assets from that period. Captures underreaction to persistent seasonal earnings patterns (Chang, Hartzmark, Solomon, Sosyura 2017) distinct from generic momentum or SUE.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ni = panel['netinc']
    a = panel['assets']
    grp = ni.groupby(level='ticker')
    seasonal_lag = grp.shift(12)
    lags = [grp.shift(k) for k in [3, 6, 9, 12]]
    lag_df = pd.concat(lags, axis=1)
    lag_df.columns = ['l3', 'l6', 'l9', 'l12']
    count_valid = lag_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    base = lag_df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    base = base.where(count_valid &gt;= 3, np.nan)
    assets_lag12 = a.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    denom = assets_lag12.where(assets_lag12 &gt; 0, np.nan)
    raw = (seasonal_lag - base) / denom
    def winsorize(x):
        valid = x.dropna()
        if valid.empty:
            return x
        lo, hi = valid.quantile(0.01), valid.quantile(0.99)
        return x.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    raw = raw.groupby(level='date').transform(winsorize)
    return raw.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>tax_loss_overhang_seasonal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Calendar-conditioned tax-loss-selling reversal: identifies loss-overhang stocks (large distance from 52-week…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Calendar-conditioned tax-loss-selling reversal: identifies loss-overhang stocks (large distance from 52-week high with negative trailing 12m return), tilted toward smaller caps, and shorts them during Oct-Nov selling pressure while going long at end of December to capture the January rebound.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid = high_ratio.notna() &amp; ret_12m.notna() &amp; marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
    overhang = (1 - high_ratio) * (ret_12m &lt; 0).astype(float)
    neg_log_mcap = -np.log(marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0))
    rank = neg_log_mcap.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    size_tilt = 1 + rank
    ov = overhang * size_tilt
    ov = ov.where(valid, np.nan)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    month = pd.to_datetime(dates).month
    w = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    w[month == 12] = 1.0
    w[(month == 10) | (month == 11)] = -1.0
    score = w * ov
    # months where w==0 -&gt; score should be 0, not NaN, even if ov is NaN
    score = score.where(~((w == 0)), 0.0)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>tax_loss_overhang_turn_of_year</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Tax-loss selling overhang: small-cap stocks trading far below their 52-week high with poor 12m returns…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Tax-loss selling overhang: small-cap stocks trading far below their 52-week high with poor 12m returns experience selling pressure in Oct-Nov (negative score) that reverses into a January rebound (positive score), concentrated in smaller, more retail-held names.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    valid = high_ratio.notna() &amp; vol_252.notna()
    mult = pd.Series(0.5, index=panel.index)
    mult = mult.where(~(ret_12m &lt; 0), 1.0)
    pressure = (1.0 - high_ratio) * np.sqrt(vol_252.clip(lower=0)) * mult
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    month = pd.Series(dates, index=panel.index).dt.month
    signal = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    signal = signal.where(~month.isin([11, 12]), -pressure)
    signal = signal.where(~month.isin([1]), pressure)
    signal = signal.where(valid, np.nan)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>tax_loss_selling_seasonal_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Tax-loss selling seasonal reversal: stocks with large embedded losses, far from 52-week highs, high…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Tax-loss selling seasonal reversal: stocks with large embedded losses, far from 52-week highs, high volatility, and small market cap face price pressure from taxable-investor loss harvesting in Nov-Dec, which reverses in January. Score is negative loss-overhang in Nov/Dec (anticipating further pressure downward) and positive loss-overhang in January (anticipating rebound).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    valid = (
        (marketcap &gt; 0)
        &amp; high_ratio.gt(0) &amp; high_ratio.le(1)
        &amp; (vol_252 &gt; 0)
        &amp; ret_12m.notna()
    )
    log_mc = np.log(marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0))
    loss_overhang = (
        (1 - high_ratio)
        * (ret_12m &lt; 0).astype(float)
        * vol_252
        / log_mc
    )
    loss_overhang = loss_overhang.where(valid)
    month = panel.index.get_level_values('date').month
    month = pd.Series(month, index=panel.index)
    score = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    mask_pressure = month.isin([11, 12])
    mask_rebound = month.eq(1)
    score = score.where(~mask_pressure, -loss_overhang)
    score = score.where(~mask_rebound, loss_overhang)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>tax_loss_selling_turn_of_year_pressure</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Capital-loss overhang (max(0,-ret_12m)) scaled by proximity-to-low (1 - high_ratio) and volatility, applied…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Capital-loss overhang (max(0,-ret_12m)) scaled by proximity-to-low (1 - high_ratio) and volatility, applied only in Nov/Dec: shorted in November while tax-loss selling pressure is ongoing, bought at end-December to capture the January rebound.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    valid = ret_12m.notna() &amp; high_ratio.notna() &amp; vol_252.notna()
    pressure = (-ret_12m).clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 - high_ratio) * vol_252
    month = panel.index.get_level_values('date').month
    month = pd.Series(month, index=panel.index)
    signal = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    dec_mask = valid &amp; (month == 12)
    nov_mask = valid &amp; (month == 11)
    signal[dec_mask] = pressure[dec_mask]
    signal[nov_mask] = -pressure[nov_mask]
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>tax_loss_selling_turn_of_year_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Tax-loss-selling turn-of-year reversal: stocks far below their 52-week high with poor 12-1 momentum…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Tax-loss-selling turn-of-year reversal: stocks far below their 52-week high with poor 12-1 momentum experience selling pressure from taxable investors harvesting losses in Nov-Dec, which reverses in January. Signal is positive in January, negative in Nov/Dec, and zero otherwise, scaled by an embedded capital-loss proxy normalized by log market cap.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    ret_12_1 = panel['ret_12_1']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid = (
        high_ratio.notna() &amp; ret_12_1.notna() &amp; marketcap.notna()
        &amp; (marketcap &gt; 1)
        &amp; (high_ratio &gt; 0) &amp; (high_ratio &lt;= 1)
    )
    log_mc = np.log(marketcap.where(valid))
    neg_ret = (-ret_12_1).clip(lower=0.0)
    embedded_loss = (1 - high_ratio) * (1 + neg_ret) / log_mc
    embedded_loss = embedded_loss.where(valid)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    month = pd.Series(dates, index=panel.index).dt.month
    mult = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    mult[month == 1] = 1.0
    mult[month.isin([11, 12])] = -1.0
    raw = mult * embedded_loss
    raw = raw.where(valid)
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>turn_of_year_tax_loss_pressure</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Tax-loss-selling overhang: stocks far below 52-week high, volatile, and down over the trailing year…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Tax-loss-selling overhang: stocks far below 52-week high, volatile, and down over the trailing year experience predictable selling pressure into year-end (Nov/Dec) as taxable investors realize losses, and a mechanical reversal in January when the selling pressure abates. Score is negative overhang in Nov/Dec (short loss-overhang names) and positive overhang in January (own loss-overhang names), NaN otherwise.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    valid = high_ratio.notna() &amp; ret_12m.notna() &amp; vol_252.notna()
    loss_flag = (ret_12m &lt; 0).astype(float)
    overhang = (1.0 - high_ratio) * vol_252 * loss_flag
    overhang = overhang.where(valid, np.nan)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    month = pd.Series(dates, index=panel.index).dt.month
    score = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    nov_dec_mask = month.isin([10, 11])
    jan_mask = month == 12
    score = score.where(~nov_dec_mask, -overhang)
    score = score.where(~jan_mask, overhang)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>turn_of_year_tax_loss_rebound_intensity</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Seasonally-gated tax-loss selling rebound signal: combines proximity to 52-week low, poor 12-month returns,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Seasonally-gated tax-loss selling rebound signal: combines proximity to 52-week low, poor 12-month returns, and high volatility (scaled inversely by log market cap) into a loss-selling pressure measure. This pressure is expressed long in Nov/Dec/Jan (tax-loss selling and January rebound window) and reversed (shorted) in May/Jun/Jul (mid-year window-dressing/momentum dominance), zero otherwise.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ret_12m = panel['ret_12m']
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid = (
        ret_12m.notna()
        &amp; high_ratio.notna()
        &amp; vol_252.notna()
        &amp; marketcap.notna()
        &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
    )
    log_mktcap = np.log(marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0))
    neg_ret = (-ret_12m).clip(lower=0)
    pressure = (1 - high_ratio) * neg_ret * vol_252 / log_mktcap
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    month = pd.Series(dates, index=panel.index).dt.month
    gate = pd.Series(0.0, index=panel.index)
    gate[month.isin([11, 12, 1])] = 1.0
    gate[month.isin([5, 6, 7])] = -0.5
    score = gate * pressure
    score = score.where(valid, np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>usd_exposure_dollar_trend_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interaction of a stock's trailing USD beta with the prevailing 12m dollar trend (normalized by expanding…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of a stock's trailing USD beta with the prevailing 12m dollar trend (normalized by expanding past-only volatility), capturing slow incorporation of currency exposure into prices conditioned on FX momentum.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    beta = panel['beta_usd_252'].copy()
    corr = panel['corr_usd_252']
    # winsorize beta at 1/99 pct cross-sectionally each date
    def winsorize(s):
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    beta_w = beta.groupby(level='date').transform(winsorize)
    # keep only where corr magnitude significant
    exposure = beta_w.where(corr.abs() &gt; 0.05, np.nan)
    # date-level trend computation
    usd_chg = panel['macro_usd_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    usd_chg = usd_chg.sort_index()
    # expanding past-only std (exclude current date), min_periods for stability
    past_std = usd_chg.shift(1).expanding(min_periods=12).std()
    trend = usd_chg / past_std
    trend = trend.where(past_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    trend_full = trend.reindex(panel.index.get_level_values('date')).values
    trend_series = pd.Series(trend_full, index=panel.index)
    signal = exposure * trend_series
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>vix_conditioned_reversal_flip</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Short-term reversal scaled by trailing volatility and conditioned on a VIX z-score: when VIX is unusually…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Short-term reversal scaled by trailing volatility and conditioned on a VIX z-score: when VIX is unusually elevated relative to its trailing history, reversal is strong and rewarded; when VIX is unusually low, the sign flips toward continuation.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    vix = panel['macro_vix'].groupby(level='date').first()
    vix = vix.sort_index()
    vix_shift = vix.shift(1)
    vix_mean = vix_shift.rolling(60, min_periods=24).mean()
    vix_std = vix_shift.rolling(60, min_periods=24).std()
    vz = (vix - vix_mean) / vix_std
    vz = vz.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    vz = vz.clip(-2, 2)
    vz_mapped = panel.index.get_level_values('date').map(vz)
    vz_mapped = pd.Series(vz_mapped, index=panel.index)
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    ret_1m = panel['ret_1m']
    vol_safe = vol_252.where(vol_252 &gt; 0)
    scaled_rev = -ret_1m / vol_safe
    score = scaled_rev * vz_mapped
    score = score.where(vol_safe.notna() &amp; ret_1m.notna() &amp; vz_mapped.notna())
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>abnormal_reporting_lag</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Filing delay (fund_datekey - fund_calendardate) abnormally long relative to the firm's own history 12 months…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Filing delay (fund_datekey - fund_calendardate) abnormally long relative to the firm's own history 12 months ago, combined with staleness of the current filing (asof_date - fund_datekey), predicts underperformance due to market underreaction to soft disclosure-timing signals of bad news.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    datekey = pd.to_datetime(panel['fund_datekey'])
    calendardate = pd.to_datetime(panel['fund_calendardate'])
    asof = pd.to_datetime(panel['asof_date'])
    valid = datekey.notna() &amp; calendardate.notna() &amp; asof.notna()
    lag_days = (datekey - calendardate).dt.days.astype(float)
    lag_days = lag_days.where(valid, np.nan)
    lag_days = lag_days.clip(lower=0, upper=400)
    stale_days = (asof - datekey).dt.days.astype(float)
    stale_days = stale_days.where(valid, np.nan)
    lag_shift12 = lag_days.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    ab_lag = lag_days - lag_shift12
    ab_lag = ab_lag.where(lag_shift12.notna(), np.nan)
    z_ab_lag = _cs_z(ab_lag)
    z_stale = _cs_z(stale_days)
    score = 0.7 * z_ab_lag + 0.3 * z_stale
    score = score.where(valid &amp; lag_shift12.notna(), np.nan)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>accruals</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Sloan accruals = (net income - operating cash flow) / assets; high accruals underperform</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Sloan accruals = (net income - operating cash flow) / assets; high accruals underperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel["assets"]
    return ((panel["netinc"] - panel["ncfo"]) / assets).where(assets &gt; 0)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>book_tax_gap_earnings_quality</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Book-tax gap earnings quality: firms with effective tax rates near peer median (i.e., not unusually low) and…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Book-tax gap earnings quality: firms with effective tax rates near peer median (i.e., not unusually low) and with book income confirmed by taxable income (high netinc/ebt conformity) exhibit more persistent earnings and higher future abnormal returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    taxexp = panel['taxexp']
    ebt = panel['ebt']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    sector = panel['sector']
    valid = (
        ebt.notna() &amp; (ebt &gt; 0)
        &amp; taxexp.notna()
        &amp; revenue.notna() &amp; (revenue &gt; 0)
        &amp; sector.notna()
    )
    etr = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    etr_raw = taxexp / ebt
    etr_raw = etr_raw.clip(lower=0, upper=0.6)
    etr[valid] = etr_raw[valid]
    conf = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    conf_raw = netinc / ebt
    conf[valid] = conf_raw[valid]
    date_level = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    # Median etr within (date, sector), computed only over valid rows.
    etr_valid_only = etr.where(valid)
    group_keys = [date_level, sector]
    sector_median = etr_valid_only.groupby(group_keys).transform('median')
    raw = etr - sector_median
    # Cross-sectional zscore of conf within date, computed only over valid rows.
    conf_valid_only = conf.where(valid)
    grp = conf_valid_only.groupby(date_level)
    mean_c = grp.transform('mean')
    std_c = grp.transform('std')
    zscore_conf = (conf_valid_only - mean_c) / std_c.replace(0, np.nan)
    signal = raw - 0.25 * zscore_conf
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>cash_backed_earnings_surprise</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) combined with a penalty for accrual-driven surprise: isolates the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) combined with a penalty for accrual-driven surprise: isolates the cash-backed portion of earnings surprises which is expected to drift more persistently, while accrual-tainted surprises mean-revert.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    epsdil = panel['epsdil']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    assets = panel['assets']
    g = epsdil.groupby(level='ticker')
    # SUE calculation
    d_eps = epsdil - g.shift(12)
    def rolling_std_24(s):
        return s.rolling(24, min_periods=8).std()
    d_eps_std = d_eps.groupby(level='ticker').transform(rolling_std_24)
    d_eps_std = d_eps_std.where(d_eps_std &gt; 0)
    sue = d_eps / d_eps_std
    sue = sue.clip(-5, 5)
    # Accruals calculation
    acc = (netinc - ncfo) / assets
    acc = acc.where(assets &gt; 0)
    acc = acc.clip(-0.5, 0.5)
    d_acc = acc - acc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    d_acc = d_acc.clip(-0.5, 0.5)
    def zscore_by_date(s):
        def _z(x):
            mu = x.mean()
            sd = x.std()
            if sd is None or sd == 0 or np.isnan(sd):
                return pd.Series(np.nan, index=x.index)
            return (x - mu) / sd
        return s.groupby(level='date').transform(_z)
    z_sue = zscore_by_date(sue)
    z_dacc = zscore_by_date(d_acc)
    score = z_sue - z_dacc
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>depreciation_conservatism_reserve</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Accounting conservatism reserve: firms with high depreciation rate (depamor/tangibles) and capital intensity…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Accounting conservatism reserve: firms with high depreciation rate (depamor/tangibles) and capital intensity (capex/assets) relative to industry peers understate earnings/book value, implying hidden value and future upward re-rating.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    depamor = panel["depamor"]
    tangibles = panel["tangibles"]
    capex = panel["capex"]
    assets = panel["assets"]
    industry = panel["industry"]
    dep_rate = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_tang = tangibles &gt; 0
    dep_rate.loc[valid_tang] = depamor.loc[valid_tang] / tangibles.loc[valid_tang]
    capint = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    capint.loc[valid_assets] = capex.loc[valid_assets] / assets.loc[valid_assets]
    valid = (
        valid_tang
        &amp; valid_assets
        &amp; depamor.notna()
        &amp; tangibles.notna()
        &amp; capex.notna()
        &amp; assets.notna()
        &amp; industry.notna()
    )
    dep_rate = dep_rate.where(valid)
    capint = capint.where(valid)
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "dep_rate": dep_rate,
        "capint": capint,
        "industry": industry,
    })
    group_keys = [df.index.get_level_values("date"), df["industry"]]
    dep_med = df.groupby(group_keys)["dep_rate"].transform("median")
    capint_med = df.groupby(group_keys)["capint"].transform("median")
    score = (df["dep_rate"] - dep_med) + 0.5 * (df["capint"] - capint_med)
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>earnings_smoothing_detection</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Ratio of rolling volatility of net income (scaled by assets) to rolling volatility of operating cash flow…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Ratio of rolling volatility of net income (scaled by assets) to rolling volatility of operating cash flow (scaled by assets), per ticker over the trailing 36 months (min 24). A low ratio indicates aggressive earnings smoothing via accruals relative to underlying cash flow volatility, which predicts lower future returns; expected_sign=+1 (high ratio = less smoothing = better quality).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    valid_assets = assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    ni = panel['netinc'] / valid_assets
    cf = panel['ncfo'] / valid_assets
    ni = ni.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cf = cf.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    sd_ni = ni.groupby(level='ticker').rolling(36, min_periods=24).std()
    sd_cf = cf.groupby(level='ticker').rolling(36, min_periods=24).std()
    sd_ni.index = sd_ni.index.droplevel(0)
    sd_cf.index = sd_cf.index.droplevel(0)
    sd_cf_valid = sd_cf.where(sd_cf &gt; 0)
    signal = sd_ni / sd_cf_valid
    signal = signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>earnings_smoothing_opacity</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Ratio of cash-flow volatility to earnings volatility (Leuz-Nanda-Wysocki style opacity index): trailing…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Ratio of cash-flow volatility to earnings volatility (Leuz-Nanda-Wysocki style opacity index): trailing 36-month std of NCFO/assets divided by trailing 36-month std of NI/assets, log-transformed. High smoothing (low earnings vol relative to cash-flow vol) suggests earnings management/opacity and predicts lower future returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    e = (netinc / assets).where(valid_assets)
    c = (ncfo / assets).where(valid_assets)
    lags = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21]
    e_lags = []
    c_lags = []
    grouped_e = e.groupby(level='ticker')
    grouped_c = c.groupby(level='ticker')
    for k in lags:
        e_lags.append(grouped_e.shift(k))
        c_lags.append(grouped_c.shift(k))
    e_df = pd.concat(e_lags, axis=1)
    c_df = pd.concat(c_lags, axis=1)
    e_count = e_df.count(axis=1)
    c_count = c_df.count(axis=1)
    sd_e = e_df.std(axis=1, ddof=1)
    sd_c = c_df.std(axis=1, ddof=1)
    sd_e = sd_e.where(e_count &gt;= 6)
    sd_c = sd_c.where(c_count &gt;= 6)
    signal = (sd_c / sd_e).where(sd_e &gt; 0)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>earnings_smoothing_vs_cashflow_volatility</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Leuz-Nanda-Wysocki style earnings-smoothing proxy: ratio of trailing 24-month rolling standard deviation of…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Leuz-Nanda-Wysocki style earnings-smoothing proxy: ratio of trailing 24-month rolling standard deviation of operating-cash-flow-to-assets to the rolling standard deviation of net-income-to-assets. High values indicate heavily smoothed earnings relative to underlying cash flow volatility, a marker of low earnings quality that predicts underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    ni_a = (netinc / assets).where(valid_assets)
    cfo_a = (ncfo / assets).where(valid_assets)
    df = pd.DataFrame({'ni_a': ni_a, 'cfo_a': cfo_a}, index=panel.index)
    # Ensure strictly backward-looking rolling computation: sort by date
    # within each ticker before applying rolling window operations.
    df = df.sort_index(level=['ticker', 'date'])
    def _roll_std(x: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        return x.rolling(window=24, min_periods=12).std()
    s_ni = df.groupby(level='ticker')['ni_a'].apply(_roll_std)
    s_cfo = df.groupby(level='ticker')['cfo_a'].apply(_roll_std)
    # groupby.apply with a Series-returning function may produce an extra
    # level in the index; align back to df's index safely.
    s_ni.index = df.index
    s_cfo.index = df.index
    signal = (s_cfo / s_ni).where(s_ni &gt; 0)
    # Reindex to the original panel order.
    signal = signal.reindex(panel.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>earnings_smoothness_vs_cashflow</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Ratio of volatility of scaled net income to volatility of scaled operating cash flow, following…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Ratio of volatility of scaled net income to volatility of scaled operating cash flow, following Leuz-Nanda-Wysocki earnings smoothness proxy. High ratio (unmanaged earnings) predicts higher subsequent returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    scale = panel['assets'].where(panel['assets'] &gt; 0)
    e = panel['netinc'] / scale
    c = panel['ncfo'] / scale
    g_e = e.groupby(level='ticker')
    g_c = c.groupby(level='ticker')
    lags = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21]
    E = pd.concat([g_e.shift(k) for k in lags], axis=1)
    C = pd.concat([g_c.shift(k) for k in lags], axis=1)
    sd_e = E.std(axis=1, ddof=1, skipna=True).where(E.count(axis=1) &gt;= 6)
    sd_c = C.std(axis=1, ddof=1, skipna=True).where(C.count(axis=1) &gt;= 6)
    ratio = sd_e / sd_c.where(sd_c &gt; 0)
    ratio = ratio.where(sd_e.notna() &amp; sd_c.notna() &amp; (sd_c &gt; 0))
    return ratio.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>effective_tax_rate_earnings_quality</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Effective tax rate (taxexp/ebt) as earnings-quality diagnostic: firms with high, rising cash-taxed earnings…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Effective tax rate (taxexp/ebt) as earnings-quality diagnostic: firms with high, rising cash-taxed earnings (high ETR level and increasing ETR) are flagged as higher quality and expected to outperform, while low/falling ETR firms (book-tax gap) are flagged as low quality earnings likely to mean-revert.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    taxexp = panel['taxexp']
    ebt = panel['ebt']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    assets = panel['assets']
    valid = (ebt &gt; 0) &amp; (netinc &gt; 0) &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
    etr = taxexp / ebt.where(ebt &gt; 0)
    etr = etr.where(valid)
    etr = etr.clip(lower=-0.2, upper=0.6)
    etr_lag = etr.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    change = etr - etr_lag
    change = change.where(~(etr_lag.isna() &amp; etr.notna()), 0.0)
    score = 0.6 * etr + 0.4 * change
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>excess_speculative_volatility</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Compares price return volatility to earnings (ROA) volatility</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Compares price return volatility to earnings (ROA) volatility. Stocks whose return volatility greatly exceeds their fundamental (earnings) volatility are driven by speculative/noise trading rather than fundamentals and tend to underperform. Score = z_cs(log(vol_252)) - z_cs(log(earn_vol + 1e-4)).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    roa_q = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_assets = assets &gt; 0
    roa_q[valid_assets] = netinc[valid_assets] / assets[valid_assets]
    lags = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21]
    shifted_list = []
    grouped = roa_q.groupby(level='ticker')
    for k in lags:
        shifted_list.append(grouped.shift(k))
    roa_df = pd.concat(shifted_list, axis=1)
    count_valid = roa_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    earn_vol = roa_df.std(axis=1, ddof=1)
    earn_vol = earn_vol.where(count_valid &gt;= 6, np.nan)
    vol_252 = panel['vol_252']
    log_vol = np.log(vol_252.where(vol_252 &gt; 0))
    log_earn_vol = np.log(earn_vol + 1e-4)
    df = pd.DataFrame({'log_vol': log_vol, 'log_earn_vol': log_earn_vol})
    def zscore(s):
        mean = s.mean()
        std = s.std(ddof=0)
        if std is None or std == 0 or pd.isna(std):
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        return (s - mean) / std
    z_vol = df['log_vol'].groupby(level='date').transform(zscore)
    z_earn_vol = df['log_earn_vol'].groupby(level='date').transform(zscore)
    score = z_vol - z_earn_vol
    score = score.where(log_vol.notna() &amp; log_earn_vol.notna(), np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>financial_slack_under_tightening</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Balance-sheet slack (cash + 4*OCF - current debt, scaled by assets) cross-sectionally ranked and conditioned…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Balance-sheet slack (cash + 4*OCF - current debt, scaled by assets) cross-sectionally ranked and conditioned on a past-only expanding z-score of the 12m change in fed funds rate and Baa spread, so the slack premium is amplified in monetary/credit tightening regimes and dampened/reversed in easing regimes.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    debtc = panel['debtc']
    assets = panel['assets']
    valid = (
        assets.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
        &amp; cashneq.notna() &amp; ncfo.notna() &amp; debtc.notna()
    )
    slack = (cashneq + 4.0 * ncfo - debtc) / assets
    slack = slack.where(valid)
    def rank_z(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        r = s.rank(pct=True)
        mean = r.mean()
        std = r.std()
        if std is None or std == 0 or pd.isna(std):
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=s.index)
        return (r - mean) / std
    slack_z = slack.groupby(level='date').transform(rank_z)
    # date-level macro series
    ff_chg = panel['macro_fedfunds_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().fillna(0.0)
    baa_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().fillna(0.0)
    def expanding_z(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        s = s.sort_index()
        mean = s.expanding().mean().shift(1)
        std = s.expanding().std().shift(1)
        z = (s - mean) / std
        z = z.where(std &gt; 0)
        return z
    ff_z = expanding_z(ff_chg)
    baa_z = expanding_z(baa_chg)
