    tight = (0.6 * ff_z + 0.4 * baa_z).clip(-2, 2)
    tight = tight.fillna(0.0)
    tight_full = slack_z.index.get_level_values('date').map(tight)
    tight_full = pd.Series(tight_full.values, index=slack_z.index)
    signal = slack_z * tight_full
    signal = signal.where(slack_z.notna())
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>gross_profitability</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Novy-Marx gross profitability = gross profit / total assets</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Novy-Marx gross profitability = gross profit / total assets.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel["assets"]
    return (panel["gp"] / assets).where(assets &gt; 0)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>hidden_credit_risk_mismatch</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Identifies highly levered firms whose equity shows little or no measured sensitivity to credit spread changes…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Identifies highly levered firms whose equity shows little or no measured sensitivity to credit spread changes (near-zero/positive corr to credit), combined with weak liquidity, indicating dormant/unpriced default risk that tends to resolve violently during funding shocks and is associated with low future returns (distress-risk anomaly).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debt = panel['debt']
    cashneq = panel['cashneq']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    currentratio = panel['currentratio']
    corr_credit = panel['corr_credit_252']
    valid = (
        debt.notna()
        &amp; cashneq.notna()
        &amp; marketcap.notna()
        &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
        &amp; currentratio.notna()
        &amp; corr_credit.notna()
    )
    netdebt_mcap = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    netdebt_mcap.loc[valid] = (debt[valid] - cashneq[valid]) / marketcap[valid]
    currentratio_valid = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    currentratio_valid.loc[valid] = currentratio[valid]
    corr_credit_valid = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    corr_credit_valid.loc[valid] = corr_credit[valid]
    score = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    def process_group(idx):
        g_valid = valid.loc[idx]
        if not g_valid.any():
            return pd.Series(np.nan, index=idx)
        g_netdebt = netdebt_mcap.loc[idx][g_valid]
        g_currentratio = currentratio_valid.loc[idx][g_valid]
        g_corr_credit = corr_credit_valid.loc[idx][g_valid]
        g_netdebt_w = _winsorize(g_netdebt)
        g_currentratio_w = _winsorize(g_currentratio)
        lev_z = _cs_zscore(g_netdebt_w)
        liq_z = -_cs_zscore(g_currentratio_w)
        credit_ins_z = _cs_zscore(g_corr_credit)
        g_score = 0.5 * lev_z + 0.25 * liq_z + 0.5 * credit_ins_z
        result = pd.Series(np.nan, index=idx)
        result.loc[g_score.index] = g_score
        return result
    score = panel.groupby(level='date', group_keys=False).apply(
        lambda g: process_group(g.index)
    )
    score = score.reindex(panel.index)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>hidden_dilution_sbc_yield</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Scales share-based compensation by market cap to estimate the annual dilution cost investors bear that is…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Scales share-based compensation by market cap to estimate the annual dilution cost investors bear that is hidden in non-GAAP earnings and operating cash flow. High SBC yield, adjusted for a cash-flow quality check, predicts lower future returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    assets = panel['assets']
    valid = sbcomp.notna() &amp; marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; (sbcomp &gt;= 0)
    sbc_yield = (4.0 * sbcomp) / marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0)
    cash_check_raw = (4.0 * (ncfo - sbcomp)) / assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    cash_check = cash_check_raw.where(
        ncfo.notna() &amp; assets.notna() &amp; (assets &gt; 0), 0.0
    )
    cash_check_clipped = cash_check.clip(lower=-0.5, upper=0.5)
    signal = sbc_yield - 0.5 * cash_check_clipped
    signal = signal.where(valid, np.nan)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>hidden_equity_dilution_cost</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">SBC-to-market and SBC-to-operating-cash-flow burden, demeaned within sector, capturing hidden dilution cost…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>SBC-to-market and SBC-to-operating-cash-flow burden, demeaned within sector, capturing hidden dilution cost that the market underreacts to.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    sector = panel['sector']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    sbc_ann = sbcomp * 4.0
    sbc_ann = sbc_ann.where(sbcomp &gt;= 0)
    valid_mc = marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0)
    burden = sbc_ann / valid_mc
    burden = burden.where(valid_mc.notna())
    ncfo_ann = ncfo * 4.0
    abs_ncfo_ann = ncfo_ann.abs()
    intensity2 = sbc_ann / abs_ncfo_ann
    intensity2 = intensity2.where(abs_ncfo_ann &gt; 0)
    # winsorize intensity2 at cross-sectional 1/99 pct per date
    def winsorize(s):
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    intensity2_w = intensity2.groupby(level='date').transform(
        lambda s: winsorize(s) if s.notna().sum() &gt; 0 else s
    )
    # base drop conditions
    valid_mask = (sbcomp.notna() &amp; (sbcomp &gt;= 0) &amp;
                  marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp;
                  sector.notna())
    burden_valid = burden.where(valid_mask)
    intensity2_valid = intensity2_w.where(valid_mask)
    # exclude stock-dates where both inputs are NaN
    both_nan = burden_valid.isna() &amp; intensity2_valid.isna()
    def cs_rank(s):
        return s.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    rank_burden = cs_rank(burden_valid)
    rank_intensity2 = cs_rank(intensity2_valid)
    raw = 0.7 * rank_burden.fillna(0) + 0.3 * rank_intensity2.fillna(0)
    weight_sum = 0.7 * rank_burden.notna().astype(float) + 0.3 * rank_intensity2.notna().astype(float)
    raw = raw / weight_sum.replace(0, np.nan)
    raw = raw.where(~both_nan)
    raw = raw.where(valid_mask)
    df = pd.DataFrame({'raw': raw, 'sector': sector})
    median_by_sector = df.groupby([df.index.get_level_values('date'), 'sector'])['raw'].transform('median')
    score = raw - median_by_sector
    score = score.where(valid_mask &amp; ~both_nan)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>inflation_passthrough_margin_expansion</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Year-over-year gross margin expansion, weighted more heavily when aggregate inflation is high, capturing…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Year-over-year gross margin expansion, weighted more heavily when aggregate inflation is high, capturing pricing power that lets firms pass through cost shocks. High inflation regimes better reveal true pricing power, so margin gains carry more signal then.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    grossmargin = panel['grossmargin']
    gp = panel['gp']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    gm_primary_valid = grossmargin.notna() &amp; (grossmargin &gt; -1) &amp; (grossmargin &lt; 2)
    gm_fallback = gp / revenue.where(revenue &gt; 0)
    gm = grossmargin.where(gm_primary_valid, gm_fallback)
    dgm = gm - gm.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    macro_cpi = panel['macro_cpi']
    macro_cpi_chg12m = panel['macro_cpi_chg12m']
    denom = macro_cpi - macro_cpi_chg12m
    infl = macro_cpi_chg12m / denom.where(denom &gt; 0)
    infl = infl.where(denom.notna() &amp; macro_cpi_chg12m.notna())
    # date-level series
    infl_by_date = infl.groupby(level='date').first()
    infl_by_date = infl_by_date.sort_index()
    # expanding past-only percentile rank (using only prior dates, excluding current)
    w_t = pd.Series(index=infl_by_date.index, dtype=float)
    vals = infl_by_date.values
    for i in range(len(vals)):
        if i == 0:
            w_t.iloc[i] = np.nan
            continue
        past = vals[:i]
        past_valid = past[~np.isnan(past)]
        cur = vals[i]
        if np.isnan(cur) or len(past_valid) == 0:
            w_t.iloc[i] = np.nan
        else:
            rank = (past_valid &lt; cur).sum() / len(past_valid)
            w_t.iloc[i] = rank
    w_t_full = infl.index.get_level_values('date').map(w_t)
    w_t_full = pd.Series(w_t_full, index=infl.index)
    score = dgm * (0.25 + w_t_full)
    valid = dgm.notna() &amp; infl.notna() &amp; w_t_full.notna()
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>net_trade_credit_expansion</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Change in net trade credit (receivables minus payables scaled by revenue) over the trailing 12 months</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Change in net trade credit (receivables minus payables scaled by revenue) over the trailing 12 months. Rising net trade credit signals loosening credit standards and deteriorating earnings quality, predicting underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    receivables = panel['receivables']
    payables = panel['payables']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    valid = receivables.notna() &amp; payables.notna() &amp; revenue.notna() &amp; (revenue &gt; 0)
    ntc = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    ntc[valid] = (receivables[valid] - payables[valid]) / revenue[valid]
    ntc_lag = ntc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    score = ntc - ntc_lag
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>operating_leverage_industrial_cycle</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Interaction of firm fixed-cost operating leverage (depreciation/revenue and non-current asset intensity) with…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of firm fixed-cost operating leverage (depreciation/revenue and non-current asset intensity) with the industrial production cycle relative to its long-run trailing average. High operating-leverage firms are predicted to outperform when the industrial cycle is accelerating above its long-run norm, and underperform when decelerating.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    depamor = panel['depamor']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    assets = panel['assets']
    assetsc = panel['assetsc']
    # component 1: depreciation intensity relative to revenue
    dep_ratio = depamor / revenue.where(revenue &gt; 0)
    dep_ratio = dep_ratio.where(revenue &gt; 0)
    # component 2: non-current asset intensity
    fixed_ratio = (assets - assetsc) / assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    fixed_ratio = fixed_ratio.where(assets &gt; 0)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    rank1 = dep_ratio.groupby(dates).rank(pct=True)
    rank2 = fixed_ratio.groupby(dates).rank(pct=True)
    oper_lev = 0.5 * rank1 + 0.5 * rank2
    # demean within date to [-0.5, 0.5]
    oper_lev = oper_lev - oper_lev.groupby(dates).transform('mean')
    # macro cycle at date level (past-only expanding mean)
    macro = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(dates).first()
    macro = macro.sort_index()
    macro_mean = macro.expanding(min_periods=12).mean()
    cyc = macro - macro_mean
    cyc = cyc.clip(-4, 4)
    cyc_aligned = dates.map(cyc)
    cyc_series = pd.Series(cyc_aligned, index=panel.index)
    signal = oper_lev * cyc_series
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sbc_adjusted_cashflow_yield</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">SBC-adjusted free cash flow yield: TTM FCF minus TTM |SBC| divided by market cap, capturing the wedge between…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>SBC-adjusted free cash flow yield: TTM FCF minus TTM |SBC| divided by market cap, capturing the wedge between headline FCF and shareholder cash flow after charging equity-based compensation as a real expense.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    fcf = panel['fcf']
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    ttm_fcf = self._ttm(fcf)
    ttm_sbc = self._ttm(sbcomp)
    adj = ttm_fcf - ttm_sbc.abs()
    valid = (
        marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp;
        ttm_fcf.notna() &amp; ttm_sbc.notna()
    )
    signal = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    signal[valid] = adj[valid] / marketcap[valid]
    def winsorize(x: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        if x.notna().sum() == 0:
            return x
        lo = x.quantile(0.01)
        hi = x.quantile(0.99)
        return x.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    signal = signal.groupby(level='date').transform(winsorize)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sbc_inflated_cash_earnings</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">SBC-intensive firms mechanically inflate cash flow/earnings by treating stock-based compensation as a…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>SBC-intensive firms mechanically inflate cash flow/earnings by treating stock-based compensation as a non-cash add-back; high SBC relative to operating cash flow or market cap signals lower earnings quality and future dilution burden, predicting underperformance.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    sbc_ttm = _ttm(sbcomp)
    cfo_ttm = _ttm(ncfo)
    burden1 = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_cfo = cfo_ttm.notna() &amp; (cfo_ttm &gt; 0) &amp; sbc_ttm.notna()
    burden1[valid_cfo] = sbc_ttm[valid_cfo] / cfo_ttm[valid_cfo]
    burden2 = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_mc = marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; sbc_ttm.notna()
    burden2[valid_mc] = sbc_ttm[valid_mc] / marketcap[valid_mc]
    z1 = _zscore_by_date(burden1)
    z2 = _zscore_by_date(burden2)
    signal = 0.5 * z1 + 0.5 * z2
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sbc_inflated_operating_cash_flow</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Quality-of-earnings signal that flags firms whose operating cash flow and free cash flow are heavily inflated…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Quality-of-earnings signal that flags firms whose operating cash flow and free cash flow are heavily inflated by non-cash share-based compensation add-backs relative to true operating cash generation and revenue. High SBC intensity implies overstated cash-flow quality and ongoing dilution; expected to negatively predict future returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    valid = sbcomp.notna() &amp; revenue.notna() &amp; (revenue &gt; 0)
    denom = pd.concat(
        [ncfo.abs(), 0.05 * revenue.abs()], axis=1
    ).max(axis=1)
    intensity = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    mask_intensity = valid &amp; denom.notna() &amp; (denom &gt; 0)
    intensity.loc[mask_intensity] = sbcomp.loc[mask_intensity] / denom.loc[mask_intensity]
    alt = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    alt.loc[valid] = sbcomp.loc[valid] / revenue.loc[valid]
    def rank_pct(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        return s.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True, na_option='keep')
    rank_intensity = rank_pct(intensity)
    rank_alt = rank_pct(alt)
    signal = 0.5 * rank_intensity + 0.5 * rank_alt
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sticky_cost_downturn_drag</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Cost stickiness signal: when revenue declines, firms that fail to cut operating costs proportionally…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cost stickiness signal: when revenue declines, firms that fail to cut operating costs proportionally (opex+cor relative to revenue, log-change difference) carry hidden operating leverage and future earnings drag. Defined only for revenue-declining firms; higher stickiness predicts lower returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    revenue = panel["revenue"]
    opex = panel["opex"]
    cor = panel["cor"]
    opex_tot = opex.where(cor.isna(), opex + cor)
    grp = opex_tot.groupby(level="ticker")
    rev_grp = revenue.groupby(level="ticker")
    rev_lag = rev_grp.shift(12)
    opex_lag = grp.shift(12)
    rev_valid = (revenue &gt; 0) &amp; (rev_lag &gt; 0)
    opex_valid = (opex_tot &gt; 0) &amp; (opex_lag &gt; 0)
    drev = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    drev[rev_valid] = np.log(revenue[rev_valid] / rev_lag[rev_valid])
    dcost = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    dcost[opex_valid] = np.log(opex_tot[opex_valid] / opex_lag[opex_valid])
    stickiness = dcost - drev
    decline_mask = drev &lt; 0
    stickiness = stickiness.where(decline_mask &amp; drev.notna() &amp; dcost.notna())
    return stickiness</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>stock_comp_burden_yield</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Trailing-twelve-month share-based compensation scaled by market cap, demeaned within (date, sector), as a…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Trailing-twelve-month share-based compensation scaled by market cap, demeaned within (date, sector), as a proxy for hidden non-cash compensation burden that overstates reported cash flow quality.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    sector = panel['sector']
    g = sbcomp.groupby(level='ticker')
    lag0 = g.shift(0)
    lag3 = g.shift(3)
    lag6 = g.shift(6)
    lag9 = g.shift(9)
    valid_lags = lag0.notna() &amp; lag3.notna() &amp; lag6.notna() &amp; lag9.notna()
    ttm_sbc = lag0 + lag3 + lag6 + lag9
    valid_mcap = marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
    valid = valid_lags &amp; valid_mcap &amp; (ttm_sbc &gt;= 0)
    burden = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    burden.loc[valid] = ttm_sbc.loc[valid] / marketcap.loc[valid]
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    def cap_99(s):
        valid_vals = s.dropna()
        if valid_vals.empty:
            return s
        cap = valid_vals.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(upper=cap)
    burden = burden.groupby(dates).transform(cap_99)
    min_group_size = 3
    group_keys = [dates, sector]
    grp = burden.groupby(group_keys)
    sector_mean = grp.transform('mean')
    sector_count = burden.notna().groupby(group_keys).transform('sum')
    signal = burden - sector_mean
    signal = signal.where(burden.notna() &amp; (sector_count &gt;= min_group_size), np.nan)
    signal.name = "stock_comp_burden_yield"
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>stock_comp_dilution_earnings_overstatement</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Flags firms whose profitability/cash flow appear inflated by non-cash stock-based compensation (SBC intensity…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Flags firms whose profitability/cash flow appear inflated by non-cash stock-based compensation (SBC intensity relative to gross profit/revenue, SBC relative to operating cash flow) and whose basic-vs-diluted EPS wedge reveals equity overhang. High scores indicate hidden dilution/earnings overstatement and are expected to underperform (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    gp = panel['gp']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    eps = panel['eps']
    epsdil = panel['epsdil']
    # sbc_int: sbcomp / gp where gp &gt; 0 and sbcomp &gt;= 0, fallback sbcomp / revenue where revenue &gt; 0
    sbc_int = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_gp = (gp &gt; 0) &amp; (sbcomp &gt;= 0)
    sbc_int.loc[valid_gp] = sbcomp.loc[valid_gp] / gp.loc[valid_gp]
    valid_rev_fallback = (~valid_gp) &amp; (revenue &gt; 0) &amp; (sbcomp &gt;= 0)
    sbc_int.loc[valid_rev_fallback] = sbcomp.loc[valid_rev_fallback] / revenue.loc[valid_rev_fallback]
    # cf_inflation: sbcomp / ncfo where ncfo &gt; 0
    cf_inflation = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_ncfo = ncfo &gt; 0
    cf_inflation.loc[valid_ncfo] = sbcomp.loc[valid_ncfo] / ncfo.loc[valid_ncfo]
    # wedge: (eps - epsdil) / abs(eps) where abs(eps) &gt; 0.01
    wedge = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    valid_eps = eps.abs() &gt; 0.01
    wedge.loc[valid_eps] = (eps.loc[valid_eps] - epsdil.loc[valid_eps]) / eps.loc[valid_eps].abs()
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'sbc_int': sbc_int,
        'cf_inflation': cf_inflation,
        'wedge': wedge,
    }, index=panel.index)
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    ranks = df.groupby(dates).rank(pct=True)
    score = ranks.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    all_nan_mask = df.isna().all(axis=1)
    score = score.mask(all_nan_mask, np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>stock_comp_earnings_dilution</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Scales share-based compensation by revenue and by absolute operating cash flow to capture stock-comp-driven…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Scales share-based compensation by revenue and by absolute operating cash flow to capture stock-comp-driven earnings/cash-flow dilution. High values indicate heavy reliance on SBC that inflates cash flow and adjusted earnings while diluting shareholders, a lower quality-of-earnings signal expected to underperform.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    sbcomp = panel['sbcomp']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    revenue_valid = revenue.where(revenue &gt; 0)
    sbc_rev = sbcomp / revenue_valid
    sbc_rev = sbc_rev.where(revenue_valid.notna() &amp; sbcomp.notna())
    ncfo_abs = ncfo.abs()
    ncfo_valid = ncfo_abs.where(ncfo_abs &gt; 0)
    sbc_ocf = sbcomp / ncfo_valid
    sbc_ocf = sbc_ocf.where(ncfo_valid.notna() &amp; sbcomp.notna())
    r1 = sbc_rev.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    r2 = sbc_ocf.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    signal = (r1 + r2) / 2
    signal = signal.where(~(r1.isna() &amp; r2.isna()))
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>trade_credit_stretch_quality</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Combines 12-month changes in days payable outstanding (payables/cor) and days sales outstanding…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Combines 12-month changes in days payable outstanding (payables/cor) and days sales outstanding (receivables/revenue) plus an accrual-quality tilt ((netinc-ncfo)/assets) to detect firms stretching trade credit terms to flatter earnings; expected_sign=-1 since higher stretch predicts lower returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    payables = panel['payables']
    cor = panel['cor']
    receivables = panel['receivables']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    assets = panel['assets']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    dpo = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    mask_cor = cor &gt; 0
    dpo[mask_cor] = payables[mask_cor] / cor[mask_cor]
    dso = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    mask_rev = revenue &gt; 0
    dso[mask_rev] = receivables[mask_rev] / revenue[mask_rev]
    dpo_lag = dpo.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    dso_lag = dso.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    d_dpo = dpo - dpo_lag
    d_dso = dso - dso_lag
    d_dpo = d_dpo.where(dpo.notna() &amp; dpo_lag.notna())
    d_dso = d_dso.where(dso.notna() &amp; dso_lag.notna())
    accrual = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    mask_assets = assets &gt; 0
    accrual[mask_assets] = (netinc[mask_assets] - ncfo[mask_assets]) / assets[mask_assets]
    def cross_sectional_rank(s):
        return s.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    rank_dpo = cross_sectional_rank(d_dpo)
    rank_dso = cross_sectional_rank(d_dso)
    rank_accrual = cross_sectional_rank(accrual)
    def neutral_fill(rank_series):
        median_rank = rank_series.groupby(level='date').transform('median')
        return rank_series.fillna(median_rank)
    rank_dpo_filled = neutral_fill(rank_dpo)
    rank_dso_filled = neutral_fill(rank_dso)
    rank_accrual_filled = neutral_fill(rank_accrual)
    signal = rank_dpo_filled + rank_dso_filled + rank_accrual_filled
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>transitory_nonoperating_income_intensity</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Absolute magnitude of the gap between pre-tax income (ebt) and operating income (opinc), scaled by total…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Absolute magnitude of the gap between pre-tax income (ebt) and operating income (opinc), scaled by total assets, as a proxy for reliance on transitory non-operating items. Higher magnitude implies lower earnings persistence and predicts lower subsequent returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    ebt = panel['ebt']
    opinc = panel['opinc']
    assets = panel['assets']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    denom = assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    nonop = ebt - opinc
    raw = nonop.abs() / denom
    valid = (
        ebt.notna()
        &amp; opinc.notna()
        &amp; assets.notna()
        &amp; revenue.notna()
        &amp; (assets &gt; 0)
        &amp; (revenue.abs() &gt; 0)
    )
    raw = raw.where(valid)
    def _winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        if s.dropna().empty:
            return s
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    result = raw.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorize)
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>working_capital_release_under_tightening</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Interacts a firm-level working-capital-efficiency improvement (declining net operating working capital scaled…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interacts a firm-level working-capital-efficiency improvement (declining net operating working capital scaled by assets, demeaned cross-sectionally) with a macro tightening intensity gauge (rising 2y yield, fed funds, and credit spreads), scaled by revenue growth. Captures funding-relief quality of earnings that binds only in tightening regimes.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    receivables = panel['receivables']
    inventory = panel['inventory']
    payables = panel['payables']
    assets = panel['assets']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    assets_safe = assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    nowc = (receivables + inventory - payables) / assets_safe
    nowc_lag12 = nowc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    d_nowc = nowc - nowc_lag12
    revenue_lag12 = revenue.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    rev_g = (revenue / revenue_lag12 - 1).where(revenue_lag12 &gt; 0)
    rev_g_clipped = rev_g.clip(-0.5, 0.5)
    # cross-sectional median of d_nowc per date, computed only from non-NaN obs
    median_d_nowc = d_nowc.groupby(level='date').transform(
        lambda x: x.median(skipna=True)
    )
    wc_release = -(d_nowc - median_d_nowc)
    # Macro tightening intensity: date-level series
    dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date')
    macro_dgs2 = panel['macro_dgs2_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_fedfunds = panel['macro_fedfunds_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_baa = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    z_dgs2 = self._pastonly_zscore(macro_dgs2)
    z_fedfunds = self._pastonly_zscore(macro_fedfunds)
    z_baa = self._pastonly_zscore(macro_baa)
    tighten = (z_dgs2 + z_fedfunds + z_baa).reindex(dates).values
    tighten_series = pd.Series(tighten, index=panel.index)
    score = wc_release * tighten_series * (1 + rev_g_clipped)
    # NaN propagation for invalid inputs
    invalid_mask = (
        receivables.isna() | inventory.isna() | payables.isna() |
        assets.isna() | (assets &lt;= 0) |
        revenue.isna() | nowc_lag12.isna() | revenue_lag12.isna() |
        (revenue_lag12 &lt;= 0) | tighten_series.isna()
    )
    score = score.where(~invalid_mask)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>zero_earnings_threshold_management</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Detects firms with small positive ROA suspiciously close to the zero-earnings threshold (Burgstahler-Dichev…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Detects firms with small positive ROA suspiciously close to the zero-earnings threshold (Burgstahler-Dichev discontinuity), suggesting earnings management to avoid reporting losses. Signal is a Gaussian kernel bump centered at zero-plus, amplified when net income exceeds operating cash flow (weak cash backing). Higher score implies higher suspicion of manipulation and is expected to predict lower future returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    assets = panel['assets']
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    ncfo = panel['ncfo']
    revenue = panel['revenue']
    valid_assets = assets.where(assets &gt; 0)
    x = netinc / valid_assets
    bump = np.exp(-0.5 * (x / 0.004) ** 2) * (x &gt; 0)
    cash_gap = ((netinc - ncfo) / valid_assets).clip(-0.5, 0.5)
    cash_gap_rank = cash_gap.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    signal = bump * (1 + cash_gap_rank)
    invalid = (
        assets.isna() | (assets &lt;= 0)
        | revenue.isna() | (revenue &lt;= 0)
        | netinc.isna()
        | ncfo.isna()
        | x.isna()
    )
    signal = signal.where(~invalid, np.nan)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>attention_shock_at_the_highs</code><span class="la-tag">size</span><span class="gist">Interaction of abnormal dollar-volume (log dvol_21 vs trailing 12m average) with proximity to 52-week high;…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interaction of abnormal dollar-volume (log dvol_21 vs trailing 12m average) with proximity to 52-week high; captures attention-driven speculative buying pressure at the highs that tends to mean-revert.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> size</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dvol = panel['dvol_21']
    high_ratio = panel['high_ratio']
    valid_dvol = dvol &gt; 0
    lv = np.log(dvol.where(valid_dvol))
    grp = lv.groupby(level='ticker')
    lags = [grp.shift(k) for k in range(1, 13)]
    lag_df = pd.concat(lags, axis=1)
    valid_count = lag_df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    baseline = lag_df.mean(axis=1)
    abn = lv - baseline
    abn = abn.where(valid_count &gt;= 9)
    # mask invalid rows
    mask = valid_dvol &amp; high_ratio.notna() &amp; abn.notna()
    abn = abn.where(mask)
    hr = high_ratio.where(mask)
    def pct_rank(s):
        return s.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    a = pct_rank(abn)
    h = pct_rank(hr)
    signal = a * h
    signal = signal.where(mask)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>conditional_size_credit_cycle</code><span class="la-tag">size</span><span class="gist">Size tilt (small minus large) conditioned on the credit cycle: the tilt is amplified when the Baa credit…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Size tilt (small minus large) conditioned on the credit cycle: the tilt is amplified when the Baa credit spread is trending down (easing) and flipped when it is trending up (tightening), based on the 12-month change in the Baa spread with an expanding, past-only z-score.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> size</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    baa_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    # Per-date macro series (broadcast across tickers, same value per date)
    macro_by_date = baa_chg.groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_by_date = macro_by_date.sort_index()
    # Expanding past-only mean/std (min 36 obs), shifted by 1 to avoid look-ahead
    shifted = macro_by_date.shift(1)
    exp_mean = shifted.expanding(min_periods=36).mean()
    exp_std = shifted.expanding(min_periods=36).std()
    zx = (macro_by_date - exp_mean) / exp_std
    zx = zx.where(exp_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    zx_clipped = zx.clip(-2, 2)
    easing = -zx_clipped
    # Only valid where macro_baa_spread_chg12m itself is present
    easing = easing.where(macro_by_date.notna(), np.nan)
    # Broadcast easing to panel index
    easing_panel = panel.index.get_level_values('date').map(easing)
    easing_panel = pd.Series(easing_panel, index=panel.index)
    # Size tilt: -log(marketcap), demeaned per date, marketcap&gt;0 only
    valid_mc = marketcap.where(marketcap &gt; 0, np.nan)
    log_size = -np.log(valid_mc)
    date_mean = log_size.groupby(level='date').transform('mean')
    size_tilt = log_size - date_mean
    score = size_tilt * easing_panel
    # Enforce missing-data policy
    score = score.where(marketcap &gt; 0, np.nan)
    score = score.where(easing_panel.notna(), np.nan)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>size_premium_credit_conditions_switch</code><span class="la-tag">size</span><span class="gist">Size premium (-log(marketcap)) whose sign and magnitude are conditioned on the 12m change in the Baa-Treasury…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Size premium (-log(marketcap)) whose sign and magnitude are conditioned on the 12m change in the Baa-Treasury credit spread: when spreads have tightened over the trailing 12 months (credit conditions improving), the small-cap premium is enhanced; when spreads have widened (credit conditions worsening), the size tilt is reversed. cond = tanh(-macro_baa_spread_chg12m / 0.5).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> size</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    baa_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m']
    dvol = panel.get('dvol_21')
    valid = marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; baa_chg.notna()
    if dvol is not None:
        valid = valid &amp; dvol.notna()
    log_mcap = np.log(marketcap.where(valid))
    size_score = -log_mcap
    # Winsorize size_score cross-sectionally (by date) at 1%/99%
    def _winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        if s.notna().sum() == 0:
            return s
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    size_score_w = size_score.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorize)
    cond = np.tanh(-baa_chg / 0.5)
    signal = cond * size_score_w
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal.reindex(panel.index)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>turnover_shock_price_run_reversal</code><span class="la-tag">size</span><span class="gist">Abnormal turnover (dollar volume scaled by market cap) relative to a stock's own trailing 12-month history,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Abnormal turnover (dollar volume scaled by market cap) relative to a stock's own trailing 12-month history, interacted with 1-month return, proxies for attention-driven overshoot that subsequently reverses.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> size</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the low scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    dvol_21 = panel['dvol_21']
    ret_1m = panel['ret_1m']
    valid_denom = (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; (dvol_21 &gt; 0)
    turn = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    turn.loc[valid_denom] = dvol_21.loc[valid_denom] / marketcap.loc[valid_denom]
    lturn = np.log(turn)
    grouped = lturn.groupby(level='ticker')
    base = grouped.shift(1).groupby(level='ticker').rolling(12, min_periods=6).mean()
    base = base.reset_index(level=0, drop=True)
    base = base.reindex(panel.index)
    abn_turn = lturn - base
    raw = abn_turn * ret_1m
    raw = raw.where(abn_turn.notna() &amp; ret_1m.notna() &amp; base.notna())
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>book_to_market</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Fama-French HML: book-to-market = 1/pb (high = cheap = long)</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Fama-French HML: book-to-market = 1/pb (high = cheap = long).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pb = panel["pb"]
    return (1.0 / pb).where(pb &gt; 0)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>cash_vs_accounting_value_divergence</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Spread between cross-sectional rank of cash-flow yield (FCF/marketcap) and accounting-earnings yield…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Spread between cross-sectional rank of cash-flow yield (FCF/marketcap) and accounting-earnings yield (netinc/marketcap), industry-neutralized within date (fallback to full cross-section median if industry missing). Captures mispricing where GAAP earnings are depressed by non-cash charges relative to cash generation.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    fcf = panel["fcf"]
    netinc = panel["netinc"]
    marketcap = panel["marketcap"]
    industry = panel["industry"]
    valid = (
        marketcap.notna()
        &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
        &amp; fcf.notna()
        &amp; netinc.notna()
    )
    cash_yield = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    acct_yield = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    cash_yield.loc[valid] = fcf.loc[valid] / marketcap.loc[valid]
    acct_yield.loc[valid] = netinc.loc[valid] / marketcap.loc[valid]
    date_level = panel.index.get_level_values("date")
    r1 = cash_yield.groupby(date_level).rank(pct=True)
    r2 = acct_yield.groupby(date_level).rank(pct=True)
    div = r1 - r2
    div = div.where(valid)
    # Industry-date median (fallback to date-level median if industry missing)
    has_industry = industry.notna()
    industry_group_key = pd.Series(
        np.where(has_industry, industry.astype(str), "__NA__"),
        index=panel.index,
    )
    combined_key = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
        [date_level, industry_group_key.values], names=["__date__", "__ind__"]
    )
    industry_median = div.groupby(combined_key).transform("median")
    date_median = div.groupby(date_level).transform("median")
    baseline = pd.Series(
        np.where(has_industry.values, industry_median.values, date_median.values),
        index=panel.index,
    )
    score = div - baseline
    score = score.where(valid)
    return score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>earnings_yield</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Earnings yield = 1/pe (high = cheap = long)</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Earnings yield = 1/pe (high = cheap = long).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pe = panel["pe"]
    return (1.0 / pe).where(pe &gt; 0)</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>equity_duration_rate_trend_interaction</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Fundamental equity-duration proxy (high PB, low dividend yield, low FCF yield) interacted with the trailing…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Fundamental equity-duration proxy (high PB, low dividend yield, low FCF yield) interacted with the trailing 12m change in the 10y Treasury yield. Long-duration growth equity is favored when yields have been falling and disfavored when yields have been rising, conditioning a value/duration tilt on the macro rate trend.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    pb = panel['pb']
    divyield = panel['divyield']
    fcf = panel['fcf']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    macro_chg = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m']
    valid_mc = marketcap &gt; 0
    cfy = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    cfy[valid_mc] = fcf[valid_mc] / marketcap[valid_mc]
    valid = (
        valid_mc
        &amp; pb.notna()
        &amp; divyield.notna()
        &amp; fcf.notna()
        &amp; cfy.notna()
        &amp; macro_chg.notna()
    )
    pb_v = pb.where(valid)
    divyield_v = divyield.where(valid)
    cfy_v = cfy.where(valid)
    rank_pb = pb_v.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    rank_neg_dy = (-divyield_v).groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    rank_neg_cfy = (-cfy_v).groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True)
    dur = 0.4 * rank_pb + 0.3 * rank_neg_dy + 0.3 * rank_neg_cfy
    dur_mean = dur.groupby(level='date').transform('mean')
    dur_c = dur - dur_mean
    signal = -dur_c * macro_chg
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>retained_vs_contributed_capital_value</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Value signal splitting book equity into retained earnings (internally generated) vs contributed capital…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Value signal splitting book equity into retained earnings (internally generated) vs contributed capital (externally raised): (2*retearn - equity) / marketcap, winsorized at 1/99 pct cross-sectionally per date. Higher score (more retained-earnings-driven equity relative to market cap) predicts higher returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> Long the high scores</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    equity = panel['equity']
    retearn = panel['retearn']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid = (marketcap &gt; 0) &amp; equity.notna() &amp; retearn.notna()
    raw = (2 * retearn - equity) / marketcap
    raw = raw.where(valid, np.nan)
    def _winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        if s.notna().sum() == 0:
            return s
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    result = raw.groupby(level='date').transform(_winsorize)
    return result</pre></div></details><h4 class="la-group">Market-timing signals (49)</h4><p class="la-group-note">Scored once per month for the market as a whole. The oriented score sets the desired equity exposure rather than picking names.</p><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_equity_issuance_market_timing</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Aggregate equity issuance market timing signal (Baker-Wurgler style): cross-sectional sum of positive net…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aggregate equity issuance market timing signal (Baker-Wurgler style): cross-sectional sum of positive net equity issuance (ncfcommon) scaled by aggregate market cap, smoothed with a 12-month rolling (past-only) mean. High aggregate issuance signals overvaluation and predicts low subsequent market returns, so exposure should be reduced (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    mcap = panel['marketcap']
    ncf = panel['ncfcommon']
    valid = mcap.notna() &amp; (mcap &gt; 0)
    ncf_pos = ncf.where(ncf.notna() &amp; (ncf &gt; 0), 0.0)
    ncf_pos = ncf_pos.where(valid)
    mcap_valid = mcap.where(valid)
    num = ncf_pos.groupby(level='date').sum(min_count=1)
    den = mcap_valid.groupby(level='date').sum(min_count=1)
    count = valid.groupby(level='date').sum()
    iss = num / den.where(den &gt; 0)
    iss = iss.where(count &gt;= 10)
    iss = iss.sort_index()
    smooth = iss.rolling(window=12, min_periods=6).mean()
    return smooth</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_inventory_overhang_timing</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Cross-sectional median inventory/revenue ratio aggregated over time, normalized by its own trailing 36-month…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-sectional median inventory/revenue ratio aggregated over time, normalized by its own trailing 36-month mean/std to form an inventory overhang z-score, amplified when trailing 12m industrial production growth is negative (slowing IP cycle). High overhang during slowdowns signals margin compression and weaker forward equity returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    inv = panel['inventory']
    rev = panel['revenue']
    valid = (inv &gt; 0) &amp; (rev &gt; 0) &amp; inv.notna() &amp; rev.notna()
    ratio = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index, dtype=float)
    ratio.loc[valid] = inv.loc[valid] / rev.loc[valid]
    agg = ratio.groupby(level='date').median()
    agg = agg.sort_index()
    norm = agg.shift(1).rolling(36, min_periods=18).mean()
    std = agg.shift(1).rolling(36, min_periods=18).std()
    overhang = (agg - norm) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
    macro_indpro_chg12m = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    macro_indpro_chg12m = macro_indpro_chg12m.reindex(agg.index)
    slow = pd.Series(np.nan, index=agg.index, dtype=float)
    mask_valid = macro_indpro_chg12m.notna()
    slow.loc[mask_valid &amp; (macro_indpro_chg12m &lt; 0)] = 1.0
    slow.loc[mask_valid &amp; (macro_indpro_chg12m &gt;= 0)] = 0.5
    signal = overhang * (0.5 + slow)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_inventory_sales_cycle_timing</code><span class="la-tag">investment</span><span class="gist">Aggregate (bottom-up, ex-Financials) inventory/sales ratio built from the equity panel's fundamentals</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aggregate (bottom-up, ex-Financials) inventory/sales ratio built from the equity panel's fundamentals. Rising aggregate inventory intensity (log ratio minus its 12-month lag) signals involuntary inventory buildup, which precedes production cuts and weak market returns, hence a negative expected sign for market timing.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> investment</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['inventory', 'revenue', 'sector']].copy()
    mask = (
        df['inventory'].notna()
        &amp; df['revenue'].notna()
        &amp; (df['inventory'] &gt; 0)
        &amp; (df['revenue'] &gt; 0)
        &amp; (df['sector'] != 'Financials')
    )
    df = df.loc[mask]
    grouped = df.groupby(level='date').agg(
        inv_sum=('inventory', 'sum'),
        rev_sum=('revenue', 'sum'),
    )
    ratio = grouped['inv_sum'] / grouped['rev_sum']
    ratio = ratio.where(grouped['rev_sum'] &gt; 0)
    s = np.log(ratio)
    s = s.sort_index()
    raw = s - s.shift(12)
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_spread_timing</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Time the market on credit conditions: lean in when the Baa-Treasury spread is tight, out when it is wide</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Time the market on credit conditions: lean in when the Baa-Treasury spread is tight, out when it is wide.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    return panel["macro_baa_spread"].groupby(level="date").first()</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>cross_sectional_beta_dispersion_timing</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Market-timing signal based on cross-sectional dispersion of market betas among the most liquid names</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market-timing signal based on cross-sectional dispersion of market betas among the most liquid names. High dispersion (relative to mean beta) indicates a fragile, disagreement-laden market prone to weak/crash-risk future returns; compressed dispersion follows panic comovement and precedes recoveries. expected_sign=-1: high dispersion -&gt; low exposure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['dvol_21', 'beta_252']].copy()
    df = df.dropna(subset=['dvol_21', 'beta_252'])
    df = df[df['dvol_21'] &gt; 0]
    def per_date(g):
        g = g.sort_values('dvol_21', ascending=False)
        g = g.head(1500)
        n = len(g)
        if n &lt; 30:
            return np.nan
        beta = g['beta_252']
        lo = beta.quantile(0.01)
        hi = beta.quantile(0.99)
        beta_w = beta.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
        disp = beta_w.std()
        mean_beta = beta_w.mean()
        if not (mean_beta &gt; 0):
            return np.nan
        return disp / mean_beta
    result = df.groupby(level='date').apply(per_date)
    result = result.astype(float)
    result.index.name = 'date'
    return result</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>cross_sectional_return_dispersion_timing</code><span class="la-tag">low_risk</span><span class="gist">Cross-sectional dispersion of trailing 1-month returns, scaled by its own trailing 36-month average, smoothed…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-sectional dispersion of trailing 1-month returns, scaled by its own trailing 36-month average, smoothed over 3 months, used as a market-timing signal. High dispersion signals elevated uncertainty/regime instability and predicts weak forward market returns (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> low_risk</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = ['ret_1m', 'ret_12m', 'marketcap', 'dvol_21']
    df = panel[cols].copy()
    # replace inf with nan and drop invalid rows
    df = df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    df = df.dropna(subset=cols)
    min_n = 30
    def winsorize(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        lo = s.quantile(0.01)
        hi = s.quantile(0.99)
        return s.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi)
    def disp_for_date(g: pd.DataFrame):
        if len(g) &lt; min_n:
            return np.nan
        w = winsorize(g['ret_1m'])
        return w.std()
    disp = df.groupby(level='date').apply(disp_for_date)
    disp.index = disp.index.get_level_values(0) if isinstance(disp.index, pd.MultiIndex) else disp.index
    disp = disp.sort_index()
    # trailing 36-month rolling std of ret_1m dispersion (past-only, shifted by 1)
    trailing_scale = disp.shift(1).rolling(window=36, min_periods=12).mean()
    scaled_disp = disp / trailing_scale.replace(0, np.nan)
    # rolling 3-month mean, past-only
    signal = scaled_disp.rolling(window=3, min_periods=1).mean()
    signal.name = "cross_sectional_return_dispersion_timing"
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>halloween_volatility_scaled_timing</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Halloween/'Sell in May' seasonal timer scaled by inverse VIX regime (vs expanding past median) and…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Halloween/'Sell in May' seasonal timer scaled by inverse VIX regime (vs expanding past median) and downweighted in NBER recessions or rising-unemployment regimes.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    vix = panel['macro_vix'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    usrec = panel['macro_usrec'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    unrate_chg = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    dates = vix.index.sort_values()
    vix = vix.reindex(dates)
    usrec = usrec.reindex(dates)
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.reindex(dates)
    # forward-fill at most 1 month for sporadic gaps
    vix = vix.ffill(limit=1)
    usrec = usrec.ffill(limit=1)
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.ffill(limit=1)
    # fill remaining NaNs in usrec/unrate_chg with 0
    usrec = usrec.fillna(0.0)
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.fillna(0.0)
    # seasonal component
    months = pd.Series(dates.month, index=dates)
    seas = months.apply(lambda m: 1.0 if m in {11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4} else -0.5)
    # expanding past-only median of vix, min 24 obs
    vix_shifted = vix.shift(1)
    vixmed = vix_shifted.expanding(min_periods=24).median()
    count = vix_shifted.expanding(min_periods=1).count()
    ratio = vix / vixmed
    vscale = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.maximum(0.0, ratio - 1.0))
    vscale = vscale.where(count &gt;= 24, 1.0)
    vscale = vscale.where(vixmed.notna() | (count &lt; 24), 1.0)
    # recession adjustment
    unrate_clip = unrate_chg.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    rec_adj = 1.0 - 0.5 * usrec - 0.25 * unrate_clip
    rec_adj = rec_adj.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    exposure = seas * vscale * rec_adj
    # NaN where vix itself is fully missing after fallback
    exposure = exposure.where(vix.notna(), np.nan)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>market_breadth_high_ratio_timing</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Market breadth signal based on the cross-sectional average and fraction of stocks trading near their 52-week…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market breadth signal based on the cross-sectional average and fraction of stocks trading near their 52-week high (high_ratio). Broadening breadth predicts positive forward market returns; narrowing breadth (deterioration relative to its own trailing 12-month average) predicts weak forward returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    hr = panel['high_ratio']
    valid_count = hr.groupby(level='date').apply(lambda s: s.notna().sum())
    brd = hr.groupby(level='date').mean()
    pct_hi = hr.groupby(level='date').apply(lambda s: (s &gt; 0.95).sum() / max(s.notna().sum(), 1))
    # invalidate months with insufficient valid tickers
    insufficient = valid_count &lt; self.MIN_VALID
    brd = brd.where(~insufficient, np.nan)
    pct_hi = pct_hi.where(~insufficient, np.nan)
    brd = brd.sort_index()
    pct_hi = pct_hi.sort_index()
    # rolling 12-month mean, past-only (shifted 1)
    brd_roll_mean = brd.rolling(window=12, min_periods=12).mean().shift(1)
    pct_hi_roll_mean = pct_hi.rolling(window=12, min_periods=12).mean().shift(1)
    brd_dev = brd - brd_roll_mean
    pct_hi_dev = pct_hi - pct_hi_roll_mean
    def zscore_past(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean_past = s.expanding(min_periods=12).mean().shift(1)
        std_past = s.expanding(min_periods=12).std().shift(1)
        z = (s - mean_past) / std_past.replace(0, np.nan)
        return z
    z_brd = zscore_past(brd_dev)
    z_pct_hi = zscore_past(pct_hi_dev)
    raw = 0.5 * z_brd + 0.5 * z_pct_hi
    # require at least MIN_HISTORY prior months before emitting non-NaN exposure
    n_prior = pd.Series(np.arange(len(raw)), index=raw.index)
    raw = raw.where(n_prior &gt;= self.MIN_HISTORY, np.nan)
    exposure = raw.fillna(0.0)
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>market_trend_timing</code><span class="la-tag">momentum</span><span class="gist">Time-series trend: hold the market when its trailing 12m return is strong, lighten when weak</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Time-series trend: hold the market when its trailing 12m return is strong, lighten when weak.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> momentum</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel: pd.DataFrame) -&gt; pd.Series:
    # market trend proxy = cross-sectional mean of trailing 12m return, per date
    return panel["ret_12m"].groupby(level="date").mean()</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_illiquidity_shock_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Market-timing signal based on Amihud-style aggregate illiquidity shocks: computes cross-sectional median of…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market-timing signal based on Amihud-style aggregate illiquidity shocks: computes cross-sectional median of |ret_1m|/dvol_21 across liquid stocks, log-transforms it, and measures its deviation from a trailing 12-month average (min 6 obs). Spikes in aggregate illiquidity relative to trend signal funding/liquidity stress and precede high subsequent market returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['ret_1m', 'dvol_21', 'marketcap', 'closeunadj']].copy()
    valid = (
        df['dvol_21'].notna() &amp; (df['dvol_21'] &gt; 0) &amp;
        df['ret_1m'].notna() &amp;
        df['marketcap'].notna() &amp;
        df['closeunadj'].notna()
    )
    df = df[valid]
    illiq = df['ret_1m'].abs() / df['dvol_21']
    illiq = illiq.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
    agg = illiq.groupby(level='date').median()
    agg = np.log(agg)
    agg = agg.sort_index()
    trailing_mean = agg.rolling(12, min_periods=6).mean().shift(1)
    exposure = agg - trailing_mean
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_rollover_risk_funding_shock_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Aggregate corporate debt rollover fragility (median debtc/debt across tickers) deviated from its 36m rolling…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aggregate corporate debt rollover fragility (median debtc/debt across tickers) deviated from its 36m rolling mean, interacted with a 12m funding shock (fed funds change + Baa spread change), to time market exposure. Short-maturity debt structures amplify sensitivity to rate/credit shocks, so higher exposure_score predicts lower forward returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    debt = panel['debt']
    debtc = panel['debtc']
    valid = (debt &gt; 0) &amp; debtc.notna() &amp; debt.notna()
    ratio = pd.Series(np.nan, index=panel.index)
    ratio[valid] = debtc[valid] / debt[valid]
    roll = ratio.groupby(level='date').median()
    roll = roll.sort_index()
    roll_mean = roll.rolling(window=36, min_periods=36).mean()
    roll_dev = roll - roll_mean.shift(1)
    macro_ff = panel['macro_fedfunds_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_baa = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_ff, macro_baa = macro_ff.reindex(roll.index), macro_baa.reindex(roll.index)
    shock = macro_ff + macro_baa
    exposure_score = roll_dev * shock
    return exposure_score</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_turnover_sentiment_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Baker-Stein style aggregate turnover sentiment timing: high market-wide turnover (dollar volume / market cap)…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Baker-Stein style aggregate turnover sentiment timing: high market-wide turnover (dollar volume / market cap) relative to its trailing multi-year norm signals sentiment-driven overpricing under short-sale constraints, forecasting LOW subsequent market returns. Exposure is set inverse to the deviation of log turnover from its trailing 36m mean.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dvol = panel['dvol_21']
    mcap = panel['marketcap']
    valid = dvol.notna() &amp; mcap.notna() &amp; (dvol &gt; 0) &amp; (mcap &gt; 0)
    dollar_vol_monthly = (dvol * 21).where(valid)
    mcap_valid = mcap.where(valid)
    agg_dvol = dollar_vol_monthly.groupby(level='date').sum(min_count=1)
    agg_mcap = mcap_valid.groupby(level='date').sum(min_count=1)
    turn = agg_dvol / agg_mcap
    turn = turn.where(agg_mcap &gt; 0)
    x = np.log(turn.where(turn &gt; 0))
    x = x.sort_index()
    rolling_mean = x.shift(1).rolling(window=36, min_periods=24).mean()
    signal = x - rolling_mean
    exposure = -signal
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>average_systematic_comovement_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Pollet and Wilson (2010)-style average comovement timer: cross-sectional mean absolute trailing correlation…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Pollet and Wilson (2010)-style average comovement timer: cross-sectional mean absolute trailing correlation of stocks to VIX, credit, and rates macro shocks. High average comovement signals a high quantity of undiversifiable systematic risk, which should be compensated by higher subsequent market returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = ['corr_vix_252', 'corr_credit_252', 'corr_rates_252']
    comps = []
    for col in cols:
        if col not in panel.columns:
            continue
        s = panel[col].dropna()
        abs_s = s.abs()
        grp = abs_s.groupby(level='date')
        mean_c = grp.mean()
        count_c = grp.count()
        mean_c = mean_c.where(count_c &gt;= self.MIN_STOCKS, np.nan)
        comps.append(mean_c)
    if not comps:
        dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date').unique()
        return pd.Series(np.nan, index=dates)
    df = pd.concat(comps, axis=1)
    comove = df.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    exposure = comove
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>consumer_sentiment_credit_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Times equity exposure using the divergence between consumer sentiment (U</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Times equity exposure using the divergence between consumer sentiment (U. Michigan) and corporate credit spreads (Baa - 10y): gloomy consumers combined with tight/stable credit spreads implies excess equity pessimism and predicts high forward returns, while euphoric sentiment with widening spreads signals hidden balance-sheet stress and predicts poor returns. A momentum overlay on credit spread and unemployment 12m changes refines the timing signal further.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    umcsent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    baa_spread = panel['macro_baa_spread'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    baa_chg12m = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    unrate_chg12m = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    umcsent = umcsent.ffill()
    baa_spread = baa_spread.ffill()
    baa_chg12m = baa_chg12m.ffill()
    unrate_chg12m = unrate_chg12m.ffill()
    s_sent = _zscore_pastonly(umcsent)
    s_credit = _zscore_pastonly(baa_spread)
    s_baa_chg = _zscore_pastonly(baa_chg12m)
    s_unrate_chg = _zscore_pastonly(unrate_chg12m)
    div = (-s_sent) - (-s_credit)
    div2 = div - 0.5 * s_baa_chg - 0.5 * s_unrate_chg
    exposure = div2.dropna()
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_equity_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Times equity market exposure using the divergence between credit-spread improvement and equity-market momentum</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Times equity market exposure using the divergence between credit-spread improvement and equity-market momentum. When credit spreads have been tightening while equities have lagged, exposure rises; the reverse divergence (spreads widening into equity strength) lowers exposure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    macro_spread = panel['macro_baa_spread'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    ret_3m = panel['ret_3m']
    # market return proxy: cross-sectional mean of ret_3m per date, dropping NaN
    mkt = ret_3m.dropna().groupby(level='date').mean()
    # credit improvement: negative of 3-month change in spread
    macro_spread = macro_spread.sort_index()
    credit_imp = -(macro_spread - macro_spread.shift(3))
    credit_imp = credit_imp.dropna()
    # align dates
    common_dates = credit_imp.index.intersection(mkt.index)
    credit_imp = credit_imp.loc[common_dates].sort_index()
    mkt = mkt.loc[common_dates].sort_index()
    min_obs = 12
    def expanding_z(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean = s.expanding().mean()
        std = s.expanding().std()
        count = s.expanding().count()
        z = (s - mean) / std
        z = z.where((count &gt;= min_obs) &amp; (std &gt; 0))
        return z
    z1 = expanding_z(credit_imp)
    z2 = expanding_z(mkt)
    exposure = z1 - z2
    exposure = exposure.reindex(common_dates)
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>credit_vol_complacency_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Cross-asset divergence between credit spread stress and equity implied volatility complacency</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-asset divergence between credit spread stress and equity implied volatility complacency. When Baa-Treasury credit spreads are historically wide relative to VIX, credit markets are pricing stress that equities have not yet discounted, predicting poor subsequent market returns; the converse signals fear-driven overreaction and a buying opportunity.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    baa = panel['macro_baa_spread'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    vix = panel['macro_vix'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    baa_chg = panel['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    vix_chg = panel['macro_vix_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    z_credit = self._past_z(baa)
    z_vix = self._past_z(vix)
    d_credit = self._past_z(baa_chg)
    d_vix = self._past_z(vix_chg)
    raw = 0.5 * (z_credit - z_vix) + 0.5 * (d_credit - d_vix)
    raw.name = self.name
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>dollar_liquidity_cycle_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Times market exposure using the 12-month relative trend in the broad USD index, amplified by the…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Times market exposure using the 12-month relative trend in the broad USD index, amplified by the cross-sectional average absolute USD beta relative to its own expanding history. A strengthening dollar tightens global financial conditions and should be followed by weaker equity risk premia, especially when the equity universe is currently more FX-sensitive than usual; the effect is inverted (i.e. dollar depreciation with high FX-sensitivity favors risk-taking).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    # Date-level average absolute USD beta (ignore NaNs), requiring a minimum count
    beta_usd = panel['beta_usd_252']
    grp = beta_usd.abs().groupby(level='date')
    A_t = grp.mean()
    counts = grp.count()
    min_count = 5
    A_t = A_t.where(counts &gt;= min_count)
    A_t = A_t.sort_index()
    # Expanding mean, past-only (shifted by 1 to avoid look-ahead), min 24 obs
    expanding_mean = A_t.expanding(min_periods=24).mean().shift(1)
    A_hat = A_t / expanding_mean.where(expanding_mean &gt; 0)
    A_hat_clipped = A_hat.clip(lower=0.5, upper=2.0)
    # Macro USD series at date level (broadcast, take first/mean per date)
    macro_usd = panel['macro_usd'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    macro_usd_chg12m = panel['macro_usd_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    macro_usd_lag12 = macro_usd.shift(12)
    trend = macro_usd_chg12m / macro_usd_lag12.where(macro_usd_lag12 &gt; 0)
    exposure_raw = -trend * A_hat_clipped
    exposure_raw = exposure_raw.reindex(A_t.index)
    return exposure_raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>equity_fear_vs_credit_stress_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Cross-asset divergence between equity fear (VIX) and credit stress (Baa spread): z-scores each series over a…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-asset divergence between equity fear (VIX) and credit stress (Baa spread): z-scores each series over a trailing 60m window (min 36m history) and takes their difference. High values mean equity implied volatility is elevated relative to what credit spreads imply, signalling unconfirmed panic/hedging pressure that should mean-revert, warranting higher market exposure; low values mean credit stress is not matched by equity vol, signalling unpriced deterioration and lower exposure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    vix = panel["macro_vix"].groupby(level="date").mean().sort_index()
    baa = panel["macro_baa_spread"].groupby(level="date").mean().sort_index()
    vix = vix.ffill()
    baa = baa.ffill()
    min_p = 36
    window = 60
    vix_mean = vix.rolling(window=window, min_periods=min_p).mean()
    vix_std = vix.rolling(window=window, min_periods=min_p).std()
    baa_mean = baa.rolling(window=window, min_periods=min_p).mean()
    baa_std = baa.rolling(window=window, min_periods=min_p).std()
    z_v = (vix - vix_mean) / vix_std
    z_c = (baa - baa_mean) / baa_std
    z_v = z_v.where(vix_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    z_c = z_c.where(baa_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    signal = z_v - z_c
    signal = signal.where(vix.notna() &amp; baa.notna())
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>equity_rate_correlation_regime_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Times the market using the date-level average stock correlation to rate changes (corr_rates_252)</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Times the market using the date-level average stock correlation to rate changes (corr_rates_252). Positive average correlation signals a growth-driven regime where bonds hedge equities and risk premia are earned; negative correlation signals an inflation/discount-rate regime with weaker forward equity returns. A small penalty is applied when 10y breakeven inflation expectations are elevated (past-only z-score).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    corr = panel['corr_rates_252'].dropna()
    m = corr.groupby(level='date').mean()
    # ensure full date index, forward-fill dates with no valid observations
    all_dates = panel.index.get_level_values('date').unique().sort_values()
    m = m.reindex(all_dates).ffill()
    exposure = m.rolling(3, min_periods=1).mean()
    # inflation penalty using macro_breakeven10, past-only z-score
    if 'macro_breakeven10' in panel.columns:
        be = panel['macro_breakeven10'].groupby(level='date').mean()
        be = be.reindex(all_dates).ffill()
        be_mean = be.expanding(min_periods=1).mean().shift(1)
        be_std = be.expanding(min_periods=1).std().shift(1)
        z = (be - be_mean) / be_std.where(be_std &gt; 0)
        z = z.fillna(0.0)
        exposure = exposure - 0.25 * z
    exposure.name = self.name
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>equity_yield_vs_real_rate_gap_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Market-timing signal based on the gap between the cross-sectional median earnings yield of large-cap stocks…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market-timing signal based on the gap between the cross-sectional median earnings yield of large-cap stocks and the real 10y rate (nominal 10y yield minus 10y breakeven inflation). A wide gap (equities cheap relative to real rates) predicts elevated forward market returns; the level is combined with a deviation from its trailing 36-month mean.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['pe', 'marketcap', 'macro_dgs10', 'macro_breakeven10']].copy()
    # keep valid pe and marketcap
    valid = df['pe'].notna() &amp; (df['pe'] &gt; 0) &amp; df['marketcap'].notna() &amp; (df['marketcap'] &gt; 0)
    df = df[valid]
    def median_top_half_ey(group):
        g = group.dropna(subset=['marketcap'])
        if len(g) == 0:
            return np.nan
        median_mc = g['marketcap'].median()
        top_half = g[g['marketcap'] &gt;= median_mc]
        ey = 100.0 / top_half['pe']
        if len(ey) == 0:
            return np.nan
        return ey.median()
    ey_by_date = df.groupby(level='date').apply(median_top_half_ey)
    ey_by_date = ey_by_date.sort_index()
    # macro series at date level (broadcast, take first per date)
    dgs10 = panel['macro_dgs10'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    breakeven10 = panel['macro_breakeven10'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    # forward-fill from prior month-end (no future values)
    dgs10 = dgs10.ffill()
    breakeven10 = breakeven10.ffill()
