    real_y = dgs10 - breakeven10
    # align all series on the common date index
    all_dates = ey_by_date.index.union(real_y.index).sort_values()
    ey_by_date = ey_by_date.reindex(all_dates)
    real_y = real_y.reindex(all_dates)
    gap = ey_by_date - real_y
    # if macro missing (dgs10 or breakeven10 not available even after ffill), gap is NaN -&gt; skip
    gap = gap.where(real_y.notna() &amp; ey_by_date.notna())
    # trailing 36-month mean of gap, past-only (exclude current observation)
    trailing_mean = gap.shift(1).rolling(window=36, min_periods=36).mean()
    trailing_count = gap.shift(1).rolling(window=36, min_periods=1).count()
    signal = gap.copy()
    has_enough = trailing_count &gt;= 36
    adj = gap - trailing_mean
    signal = gap + 0.5 * adj.where(has_enough, 0.0)
    signal = signal.where(gap.notna())
    signal.name = self.name
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>household_sentiment_fundamental_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Contrarian macro timer using the divergence between consumer sentiment (UMich) and hard real-economy…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Contrarian macro timer using the divergence between consumer sentiment (UMich) and hard real-economy fundamentals (industrial production growth and unemployment dynamics). When sentiment is unusually pessimistic relative to fundamentals, risk premia are elevated and expected returns are high; exposure is negative of this expanding-z-score gap.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    senti = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    indpro_chg = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    unrate_chg = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    senti = senti.sort_index().ffill()
    indpro_chg = indpro_chg.sort_index().ffill()
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.sort_index().ffill()
    first_valid = max(
        senti.first_valid_index(),
        indpro_chg.first_valid_index(),
        unrate_chg.first_valid_index(),
    )
    senti = senti.loc[first_valid:]
    indpro_chg = indpro_chg.loc[first_valid:]
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.loc[first_valid:]
    z_senti = self._expanding_z(senti)
    z_indpro = self._expanding_z(indpro_chg)
    z_unrate_inv = self._expanding_z(-unrate_chg)
    fund = 0.5 * (z_indpro + z_unrate_inv)
    gap = z_senti - fund
    exposure = -gap
    exposure = exposure.reindex(senti.index)
    exposure = exposure.fillna(0.0)
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>labor_cycle_turning_point_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Market timing signal based on labor-market inflection points: combines the unemployment-rate gap from its…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market timing signal based on labor-market inflection points: combines the unemployment-rate gap from its trailing 12-month trough (Sahm-rule style) with confirmation from industrial production growth and consumer sentiment growth. A rising unemployment gap off its trough signals elevated drawdown risk (negative exposure), while unemployment at its trough with expanding industrial production and improving sentiment signals low drawdown risk (positive exposure).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    def z(x: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean = x.expanding(24).mean()
        std = x.expanding(24).std()
        out = (x - mean) / std
        out = out.where(std &gt; 0)
        return out
    u = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').first()
    u = u.sort_index()
    gap = u - u.rolling(12).min()
    ip = panel['macro_indpro'].groupby(level='date').first()
    ip = ip.sort_index()
    ipg = ip / ip.shift(12) - 1.0
    sent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').first()
    sent = sent.sort_index()
    sg = sent / sent.shift(12) - 1.0
    z_gap = z(gap)
    z_ipg = z(ipg)
    z_sg = z(sg)
    exposure = -1.0 * z_gap + 0.5 * z_ipg + 0.25 * z_sg
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_momentum_diffusion_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Date-level macro breadth/diffusion index counting how many independent macro dimensions (industrial…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Date-level macro breadth/diffusion index counting how many independent macro dimensions (industrial production, unemployment, credit spread, consumer sentiment, VIX, term spread) are improving over the trailing 12 months. Exposure is raised when macro breadth broadly improves and cut when several dimensions deteriorate together.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    components = [
        ('macro_indpro_chg12m', 1),
        ('macro_unrate_chg12m', -1),
        ('macro_baa_spread_chg12m', -1),
        ('macro_umcsent_chg12m', 1),
        ('macro_vix_chg12m', -1),
        ('macro_t10y2y_chg12m', 1),
    ]
    date_level_series = {}
    for col, _ in components:
        s = panel[col].groupby(level='date').mean()
        date_level_series[col] = s
    dates = None
    for s in date_level_series.values():
        if dates is None:
            dates = s.index
        else:
            dates = dates.union(s.index)
    dates = dates.sort_values()
    signed_sum = pd.Series(0.0, index=dates)
    count = pd.Series(0, index=dates)
    for col, weight in components:
        s = date_level_series[col].reindex(dates)
        sign_s = np.sign(s)
        valid = sign_s.notna()
        signed_sum = signed_sum.add(sign_s.where(valid, 0.0) * weight, fill_value=0.0)
        count = count.add(valid.astype(int), fill_value=0)
    exposure = signed_sum / count.replace(0, np.nan)
    exposure = exposure.where(count &gt; 0, np.nan)
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_pessimism_contrarian_market_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Contrarian macro timer: goes long equities when consumer sentiment is depressed relative to its own history…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Contrarian macro timer: goes long equities when consumer sentiment is depressed relative to its own history and unemployment has recently risen, harvesting a countercyclical equity risk premium. Built purely from survey/labor/industrial-production data, uncorrelated with credit-spread or volatility-based timers.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = [
        "macro_umcsent",
        "macro_umcsent_chg12m",
        "macro_unrate_chg12m",
        "macro_indpro_chg12m",
    ]
    def first_per_date(col):
        return panel[col].groupby(level="date").first()
    data = pd.DataFrame({c: first_per_date(c) for c in cols})
    data = data.sort_index()
    data = data.ffill()
    def zexp(x: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean = x.expanding().mean().shift(1)
        std = x.expanding().std().shift(1)
        z = (x - mean) / std
        z = z.where(std &gt; 0, np.nan)
        return z
    z_sent = zexp(data["macro_umcsent"])
    z_sent_chg = zexp(data["macro_umcsent_chg12m"])
    z_unrate_chg = zexp(data["macro_unrate_chg12m"])
    z_indpro_chg = zexp(data["macro_indpro_chg12m"])
    raw = (
        -z_sent
        - 0.5 * z_sent_chg
        + 0.5 * z_unrate_chg
        - 0.25 * z_indpro_chg
    )
    exposure = raw.clip(-2, 2)
    exposure = exposure.where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>macro_risk_on_breadth_contrarian_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Counts breadth of risk-on macro trends (tightening credit spreads, falling VIX, steepening curve, rising…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Counts breadth of risk-on macro trends (tightening credit spreads, falling VIX, steepening curve, rising industrial production, rising consumer sentiment, rising oil) and returns the negative breadth as market exposure, contrarian to macro momentum: buy when macro consensus is uniformly deteriorating, de-risk when uniformly benign.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = [
        'macro_baa_spread_chg12m',
        'macro_vix_chg12m',
        'macro_t10y2y_chg12m',
        'macro_indpro_chg12m',
        'macro_umcsent_chg12m',
        'macro_oil_chg12m',
    ]
    date_series = {}
    for c in cols:
        s = panel[c].groupby(level='date').mean()
        s = s.sort_index()
        s = s.ffill()
        date_series[c] = s
    df = pd.DataFrame(date_series)
    def safe_sign(x):
        return x.apply(lambda v: 0.0 if pd.isna(v) else np.sign(v))
    breadth = (
        safe_sign(-df['macro_baa_spread_chg12m'])
        + safe_sign(-df['macro_vix_chg12m'])
        + safe_sign(df['macro_t10y2y_chg12m'])
        + safe_sign(df['macro_indpro_chg12m'])
        + safe_sign(df['macro_umcsent_chg12m'])
        + safe_sign(df['macro_oil_chg12m'])
    )
    breadth.name = self.name
    return breadth</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>oil_demand_vs_supply_shock_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Interacts the cross-sectional average stock-oil correlation with the trailing oil price trend to distinguish…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Interacts the cross-sectional average stock-oil correlation with the trailing oil price trend to distinguish demand-driven vs supply-driven oil shocks, timing market exposure accordingly.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    min_obs = 12
    # Cross-sectional average correlation with oil, per date
    avgcorr_t = panel['corr_oil_252'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    avgcorr_t = avgcorr_t.sort_index()
    # Macro oil series (broadcast per date -&gt; take date-level mean)
    macro_oil = panel['macro_oil'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    macro_oil_chg12m = panel['macro_oil_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    # Oil trend measure: 12m change normalized by lagged price level
    macro_oil_lag12 = macro_oil.shift(12)
    o_raw = macro_oil_chg12m / macro_oil_lag12.where(macro_oil_lag12 &gt; 0)
    # Past-only expanding z-score helper
    def past_only_zscore(s: pd.Series) -&gt; pd.Series:
        mean_shifted = s.expanding().mean().shift(1)
        std_shifted = s.expanding().std().shift(1)
        count_shifted = s.expanding().count().shift(1)
        z = (s - mean_shifted) / std_shifted
        z = z.where((count_shifted &gt;= min_obs) &amp; (std_shifted &gt; 0))
        return z
    c = past_only_zscore(avgcorr_t)
    o = past_only_zscore(o_raw)
    exposure = c * o
    # Neutralize (set to 0) where inputs are missing per policy
    invalid = avgcorr_t.isna() | macro_oil.isna() | macro_oil_chg12m.isna() | c.isna() | o.isna()
    exposure = exposure.where(~invalid, 0.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>oil_shock_demand_supply_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Cross-sectional average trailing correlation of stocks with oil classifies whether oil moves are…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-sectional average trailing correlation of stocks with oil classifies whether oil moves are demand-driven (growth-friendly, positive correlation) or supply-driven (cost shock, negative correlation). Multiplying this revealed correlation by the recent oil trend gives a market-exposure signal: long equities during demand-led oil rallies, defensive during supply-led ones.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    mean_corr = panel['corr_oil_252'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    macro_oil = panel['macro_oil'].groupby(level='date').first()
    macro_oil_chg12m = panel['macro_oil_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    denom = macro_oil.where(macro_oil &gt; 0)
    oil_mom = macro_oil_chg12m / denom
    oil_mom = oil_mom.clip(-1, 1)
    exposure = mean_corr * oil_mom
    # forward-fill exposure when oil_mom is NaN (macro_oil missing/invalid)
    exposure = exposure.where(oil_mom.notna())
    exposure = exposure.ffill()
    # remaining NaNs (e.g., at start) treated as neutral
    exposure = exposure.fillna(0.0)
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>profitless_market_cap_share_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Aggregate market-cap share held by firms with negative trailing twelve-month net income, measured as a…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aggregate market-cap share held by firms with negative trailing twelve-month net income, measured as a deviation from its own 36-month trailing norm. Rising 'froth' share signals speculative excess and contrarian-low future market returns; exposure is the negative of the deviation (harness applies expected_sign).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['netinc', 'marketcap', 'closeunadj', 'dvol_21']].copy()
    # liquidity/data filters
    valid = (
        df['marketcap'].notna() &amp; (df['marketcap'] &gt; 0) &amp;
        df['closeunadj'].notna() &amp;
        df['dvol_21'].notna()
    )
    df = df[valid]
    # TTM net income via lags per ticker
    netinc = df['netinc']
    shift3 = netinc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(3)
    shift6 = netinc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(6)
    shift9 = netinc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(9)
    ttm_netinc = netinc + shift3 + shift6 + shift9
    ttm_valid = netinc.notna() &amp; shift3.notna() &amp; shift6.notna() &amp; shift9.notna()
    df['ttm_netinc'] = ttm_netinc
    df = df[ttm_valid]
    # profitless flag
    df['profitless_mcap'] = np.where(df['ttm_netinc'] &lt; 0, df['marketcap'], 0.0)
    grouped = df.groupby(level='date')
    sum_profitless = grouped['profitless_mcap'].sum()
    sum_total = grouped['marketcap'].sum()
    froth = sum_profitless / sum_total.where(sum_total &gt; 0)
    froth = froth.sort_index()
    rolling_mean = froth.shift(1).rolling(window=36, min_periods=24).mean()
    signal = froth - rolling_mean
    exposure = -signal
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>real_policy_stance_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Real policy stance timing: combines the real fed funds rate (fed funds minus trailing 12m CPI inflation) with…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Real policy stance timing: combines the real fed funds rate (fed funds minus trailing 12m CPI inflation) with the 12m change in fed funds to gauge monetary tightness. A high/rising real policy stance signals scarce liquidity and elevated discount rates, predicting lower forward equity returns; a deeply negative/easing stance predicts higher forward returns (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cpi = panel['macro_cpi'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    fedfunds = panel['macro_fedfunds'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    fedfunds_chg12m = panel['macro_fedfunds_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    cpi = cpi.ffill()
    fedfunds = fedfunds.ffill()
    fedfunds_chg12m = fedfunds_chg12m.ffill()
    cpi_lag12 = cpi.shift(12)
    infl = 100.0 * (cpi / cpi_lag12 - 1.0)
    infl = infl.where(cpi_lag12 &gt; 0, np.nan)
    real_rate = fedfunds - infl
    stance = 0.6 * real_rate + 0.4 * fedfunds_chg12m
    smooth = stance.rolling(3, min_periods=1).mean()
    return smooth</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>real_yield_shock_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Decomposes nominal 10y yield into breakeven inflation and real yield</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Decomposes nominal 10y yield into breakeven inflation and real yield. Rising real yields (12m shock) and elevated real yield relative to its own 60m history signal tightening financial conditions and predict weak equity returns; falling real yields support risk-taking.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    dgs10 = panel['macro_dgs10'].groupby(level='date').first()
    breakeven10 = panel['macro_breakeven10'].groupby(level='date').first()
    dgs10_chg12m = panel['macro_dgs10_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    breakeven10_chg12m = panel['macro_breakeven10_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    dates = dgs10.index.sort_values()
    dgs10 = dgs10.reindex(dates)
    breakeven10 = breakeven10.reindex(dates)
    dgs10_chg12m = dgs10_chg12m.reindex(dates)
    breakeven10_chg12m = breakeven10_chg12m.reindex(dates)
    real10 = dgs10 - breakeven10
    shock12_direct = real10 - real10.shift(12)
    shock12_fallback = dgs10_chg12m - breakeven10_chg12m
    shock12 = shock12_direct.where(shock12_direct.notna(), shock12_fallback)
    roll_mean = real10.rolling(60, min_periods=24).mean().shift(1)
    gap = real10 - roll_mean
    shock12_valid = shock12.notna()
    gap_valid = gap.notna()
    shock12_term = 0.6 * shock12.fillna(0.0)
    gap_term = 0.4 * gap.fillna(0.0)
    signal = shock12_term + gap_term
    signal = signal.where(shock12_valid | gap_valid, np.nan)
    signal.index.name = 'date'
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sahm_labor_deterioration_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Sahm-rule-style labor deterioration timing signal: computes the gap between current unemployment and its…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Sahm-rule-style labor deterioration timing signal: computes the gap between current unemployment and its trailing 12-month minimum, applies a hinge at 0.2pp (nonlinear, near-zero in expansions, positive once labor markets crack), and scales confidence by whether consumer sentiment is deteriorating. Higher exposure_raw indicates rising recession risk and is expected to precede negative equity returns (expected_sign = -1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    unrate = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    umcsent_chg = panel['macro_umcsent_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    unrate = unrate.ffill()
    umcsent_chg = umcsent_chg.ffill()
    u_min12 = unrate.rolling(window=12, min_periods=1).min()
    gap = unrate - u_min12
    hinge = (gap - 0.2).clip(lower=0.0)
    conf = pd.Series(0.5, index=umcsent_chg.index)
    conf[umcsent_chg &lt; 0] = 1.0
    exposure_raw = hinge * conf
    missing_mask = unrate.isna() | umcsent_chg.isna()
    exposure_raw = exposure_raw.where(~missing_mask, 0.0)
    exposure_raw.name = self.name
    return exposure_raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>seasonal_risk_appetite_credit_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Halloween/Sell-in-May seasonal timing rule conditioned on the level of the Baa credit spread: long risk in…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Halloween/Sell-in-May seasonal timing rule conditioned on the level of the Baa credit spread: long risk in the winter half (Nov-Apr) and short/defensive in the summer half (May-Oct), with the winter exposure amplified when the expanding past-only z-score of the Baa credit spread is elevated (wide risk premia).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    baa = panel['macro_baa_spread'].groupby(level='date').mean()
    baa = baa.sort_index()
    baa = baa.ffill()
    baa = baa.dropna()
    dates = baa.index
    # seasonal sign: +1 for Nov-Apr, -1 for May-Oct
    months = pd.Series(dates.month, index=dates)
    hall = months.apply(lambda m: 1.0 if m in (11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4) else -1.0)
    # expanding past-only z-score, min 36 obs, shift(1)
    expanding_mean = baa.expanding(min_periods=36).mean().shift(1)
    expanding_std = baa.expanding(min_periods=36).std().shift(1)
    z = (baa - expanding_mean) / expanding_std
    z = z.where(expanding_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    z = z.fillna(0.0)
    z_clipped = z.clip(lower=0, upper=2)
    exposure = hall * (1.0 + z_clipped)
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_capitulation_recovery_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Countercyclical market-timing signal that goes long equity exposure when consumer sentiment is deeply…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Countercyclical market-timing signal that goes long equity exposure when consumer sentiment is deeply depressed relative to its own trailing history (contrarian level) AND is showing signs of stabilization/improvement over the last 3 months (confirming trend), with a secondary boost from elevated unemployment relative to its trailing history. Combines a contrarian level with a confirming direction to capture the capitulation-then-recovery phase of the sentiment cycle.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    umc = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    umc = umc.ffill()
    lvl_mean = umc.rolling(60, min_periods=24).mean()
    lvl_std = umc.rolling(60, min_periods=24).std()
    lvl_z = (umc - lvl_mean) / lvl_std
    lvl_z = lvl_z.where(lvl_std &gt; 0)
    d3 = umc - umc.shift(3)
    d3_mean = d3.rolling(60, min_periods=24).mean()
    d3_std = d3.rolling(60, min_periods=24).std()
    mom_z = (d3 - d3_mean) / d3_std
    mom_z = mom_z.where(d3_std &gt; 0)
    ur = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    ur = ur.ffill()
    ur_mean = ur.rolling(60, min_periods=24).mean()
    ur_std = ur.rolling(60, min_periods=24).std()
    ur_z = (ur - ur_mean) / ur_std
    ur_z = ur_z.where(ur_std &gt; 0)
    exposure = (-lvl_z + mom_z + 0.5 * ur_z) / 2.5
    exposure = exposure.where(~(lvl_z.isna() | mom_z.isna() | ur_z.isna()), 0.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_fundamental_disagreement_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Orthogonalizes consumer sentiment against a composite of hard macro fundamentals (unemployment level/change,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Orthogonalizes consumer sentiment against a composite of hard macro fundamentals (unemployment level/change, industrial production growth, CPI inflation change). When sentiment is far more pessimistic than hard data warrant, equity risk premia are elevated and subsequent market returns tend to be high; excess euphoria predicts the reverse.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    m = panel.groupby(level='date').first()
    m = m.sort_index()
    umcsent = m['macro_umcsent'].ffill()
    unrate = m['macro_unrate'].ffill()
    unrate_chg12m = m['macro_unrate_chg12m'].ffill()
    indpro_chg12m = m['macro_indpro_chg12m'].ffill()
    cpi_chg12m = m['macro_cpi_chg12m'].ffill()
    z_sent = self._zscore(umcsent)
    z_unrate = self._zscore(unrate)
    z_unrate_chg = self._zscore(unrate_chg12m)
    z_indpro_chg = self._zscore(indpro_chg12m)
    z_cpi_chg = self._zscore(cpi_chg12m)
    z_fund = (-z_unrate - z_unrate_chg + z_indpro_chg - z_cpi_chg) / 4.0
    signal = z_fund - z_sent
    valid = (
        z_sent.notna()
        &amp; z_unrate.notna()
        &amp; z_unrate_chg.notna()
        &amp; z_indpro_chg.notna()
        &amp; z_cpi_chg.notna()
    )
    signal = signal.where(valid)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_fundamental_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Market-timing signal based on divergence between consumer sentiment (level + 12m change) and hard economic…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Market-timing signal based on divergence between consumer sentiment (level + 12m change) and hard economic data (industrial production and unemployment 12m changes). When sentiment is far more depressed than fundamentals justify, expected equity risk premium is high and exposure is increased; when sentiment overshoots fundamentals, exposure is reduced.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    umcsent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    umcsent_chg12m = panel['macro_umcsent_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    indpro_chg12m = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    unrate_chg12m = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    umcsent = umcsent.ffill()
    umcsent_chg12m = umcsent_chg12m.ffill()
    indpro_chg12m = indpro_chg12m.ffill()
    unrate_chg12m = unrate_chg12m.ffill()
    z_umcsent = self._zexp(umcsent)
    z_umcsent_chg12m = self._zexp(umcsent_chg12m)
    z_indpro_chg12m = self._zexp(indpro_chg12m)
    z_unrate_chg12m = self._zexp(unrate_chg12m)
    sent = 0.5 * z_umcsent + 0.5 * z_umcsent_chg12m
    fund = z_indpro_chg12m - z_unrate_chg12m
    exposure = (fund - sent).clip(-2, 2)
    exposure = exposure.where(sent.notna() &amp; fund.notna(), 0.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_fundamental_gap_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Gap between consumer sentiment (level + 12m change) and hard macro fundamentals (unemployment rate/change,…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Gap between consumer sentiment (level + 12m change) and hard macro fundamentals (unemployment rate/change, industrial production growth), z-scored with expanding past-only moments. High sentiment relative to fundamentals signals compressed risk premia and low forward returns (behavioral/affect component isolated from the business cycle itself).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cols = ['macro_umcsent', 'macro_umcsent_chg12m', 'macro_unrate',
            'macro_unrate_chg12m', 'macro_indpro_chg12m']
    date_level = {}
    for c in cols:
        s = panel[c].groupby(level='date').mean()
        s = s.sort_index()
        s = s.ffill()
        date_level[c] = s
    z_umcsent = self._zx(date_level['macro_umcsent']).fillna(0.0)
    z_umcsent_chg = self._zx(date_level['macro_umcsent_chg12m']).fillna(0.0)
    z_unrate = self._zx(date_level['macro_unrate']).fillna(0.0)
    z_unrate_chg = self._zx(date_level['macro_unrate_chg12m']).fillna(0.0)
    z_indpro_chg = self._zx(date_level['macro_indpro_chg12m']).fillna(0.0)
    sentiment = 0.5 * z_umcsent + 0.5 * z_umcsent_chg
    fundamentals = 0.5 * (-z_unrate) + 0.25 * (-z_unrate_chg) + 0.25 * z_indpro_chg
    signal_val = sentiment - fundamentals
    # dates with all-NaN raw inputs should yield NaN
    raw_all_nan = pd.concat(
        [date_level[c] for c in cols], axis=1
    ).isna().all(axis=1)
    signal_val = signal_val.where(~raw_all_nan, np.nan)
    exposure = -signal_val
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_fundamental_pessimism_gap_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Residual of consumer sentiment vs</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Residual of consumer sentiment vs. macro-fundamentals-implied sentiment (unemployment, CPI change, oil change, industrial production change). When sentiment is unjustifiably worse than fundamentals imply, subsequent market returns tend to be higher; positioned as a contrarian macro-timing signal.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    def get_date_series(col):
        s = panel[col].groupby(level='date').mean()
        s = s.sort_index()
        s = s.ffill()
        return s
    umcsent = get_date_series('macro_umcsent')
    unrate = get_date_series('macro_unrate')
    cpi_chg12m = get_date_series('macro_cpi_chg12m')
    oil_chg12m = get_date_series('macro_oil_chg12m')
    indpro_chg12m = get_date_series('macro_indpro_chg12m')
    unrate_chg12m = get_date_series('macro_unrate_chg12m')
    def zx(s):
        mean = s.expanding(36).mean()
        std = s.expanding(36).std()
        z = (s - mean) / std
        z = z.where(std &gt; 0, np.nan)
        return z
    z_umcsent = zx(umcsent)
    z_unrate = zx(unrate)
    z_cpi_chg12m = zx(cpi_chg12m)
    z_oil_chg12m = zx(oil_chg12m)
    z_indpro_chg12m = zx(indpro_chg12m)
    z_unrate_chg12m = zx(unrate_chg12m)
    components = pd.DataFrame({
        'unrate': z_unrate,
        'cpi_chg12m': z_cpi_chg12m,
        'oil_chg12m': z_oil_chg12m,
        'indpro_chg12m': -z_indpro_chg12m,
        'unrate_chg12m': z_unrate_chg12m,
    })
    valid_mask = components.notna().any(axis=1)
    components_filled = components.fillna(0.0)
    misery = (
        components_filled['unrate']
        + components_filled['cpi_chg12m']
        + components_filled['oil_chg12m']
        + components_filled['indpro_chg12m']
        - components_filled['unrate_chg12m']
    )
    implied_sent = -misery / 4.0
    exposure = implied_sent - z_umcsent.fillna(0.0)
    # if z_umcsent itself is NaN and no other component valid either, mark NaN
    all_nan_mask = components.isna().all(axis=1) &amp; z_umcsent.isna()
    exposure = exposure.where(~all_nan_mask, np.nan)
    exposure = exposure.where(valid_mask | z_umcsent.notna(), np.nan)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_gap_contrarian_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Contrarian macro timing signal using consumer sentiment deviation from its trailing 3-year mean…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Contrarian macro timing signal using consumer sentiment deviation from its trailing 3-year mean (countercyclical) combined with unemployment slack and rising unemployment momentum. Elevated risk aversion (low sentiment, high slack, rising unemployment) predicts higher subsequent equity risk premia.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    s = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').first()
    u = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').first()
    du = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    s_mean = s.rolling(36, min_periods=18).mean()
    s_std = s.rolling(36, min_periods=18).std()
    sent_gap = (s - s_mean) / s_std.where(s_std &gt; 0)
    u_mean = u.rolling(36, min_periods=18).mean()
    u_std = u.rolling(36, min_periods=18).std()
    slack = (u - u_mean) / u_std.where(u_std &gt; 0)
    exposure = (-sent_gap + 0.5 * slack + 0.5 * du.clip(lower=0)).clip(-3, 3)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_hard_data_divergence_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Contrarian macro timing signal using the divergence between household sentiment (UMich) and hard data…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Contrarian macro timing signal using the divergence between household sentiment (UMich) and hard data (industrial production, unemployment). When sentiment is high relative to hard data, expected market returns are low (euphoria priced in); when sentiment is depressed relative to solid hard data, expected returns are high (elevated risk premium). Exposure is hard_z - sent_z, expanding-window z-scored, past-only, min 36 obs.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    umcsent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    indpro_chg = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    unrate_chg = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').mean().sort_index()
    umcsent = umcsent.ffill()
    indpro_chg = indpro_chg.ffill()
    unrate_chg = unrate_chg.ffill()
    sent_z = self._expanding_z(umcsent, min_obs=36)
    indpro_z = self._expanding_z(indpro_chg, min_obs=36)
    unrate_z = self._expanding_z(unrate_chg, min_obs=36)
    hard_z = 0.5 * indpro_z - 0.5 * unrate_z
    exposure = hard_z - sent_z
    exposure = exposure.clip(-2.0, 2.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>sentiment_misery_residual_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Times the market using the residual of consumer sentiment relative to the misery index (unemployment +…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Times the market using the residual of consumer sentiment relative to the misery index (unemployment + realized inflation). Excess pessimism relative to observable hardship (a large negative sentiment+misery residual) is a contrarian bullish signal for future market returns; unjustified optimism amid high misery is bearish.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cpi = panel['macro_cpi'].groupby(level='date').first()
    cpi_chg12m = panel['macro_cpi_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    unrate = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').first()
    umcsent = panel['macro_umcsent'].groupby(level='date').first()
    dates = cpi.index.sort_values()
    cpi = cpi.reindex(dates).ffill()
    cpi_chg12m = cpi_chg12m.reindex(dates).ffill()
    unrate = unrate.reindex(dates).ffill()
    umcsent = umcsent.reindex(dates).ffill()
    infl = 100.0 * cpi_chg12m / cpi.where(cpi &gt; 0)
    misery = unrate + infl
    required_valid = umcsent.notna() &amp; misery.notna()
    s_mean = umcsent.expanding(min_periods=36).mean()
    s_std = umcsent.expanding(min_periods=36).std()
    m_mean = misery.expanding(min_periods=36).mean()
    m_std = misery.expanding(min_periods=36).std()
    zs = (umcsent - s_mean) / s_std.where(s_std &gt; 0)
    zm = (misery - m_mean) / m_std.where(m_std &gt; 0)
    residual = zs + zm
    exposure = -residual
    exposure = exposure.clip(-2, 2)
    count = pd.Series(np.arange(1, len(dates) + 1), index=dates)
    has_history = count &gt;= 36
    valid = required_valid &amp; has_history &amp; exposure.notna()
    exposure = exposure.where(valid, 0.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>stagflation_supply_shock_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Decomposes oil price moves by concurrent industrial production impulse to distinguish demand-driven oil…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Decomposes oil price moves by concurrent industrial production impulse to distinguish demand-driven oil rallies (benign for equities) from adverse supply shocks (oil and breakeven inflation rising while industrial production stalls). Exposure is reduced when supply-shock stagflationary conditions are detected.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    oil_chg = panel['macro_oil_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    breakeven_chg = panel['macro_breakeven10_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    cpi_chg = panel['macro_cpi_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    indpro_chg = panel['macro_indpro_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    oil_chg = oil_chg.ffill()
    breakeven_chg = breakeven_chg.ffill()
    cpi_chg = cpi_chg.ffill()
    indpro_chg = indpro_chg.ffill()
    z_oil = self._zexp(oil_chg)
    z_breakeven = self._zexp(breakeven_chg)
    z_cpi = self._zexp(cpi_chg)
    z_indpro = self._zexp(indpro_chg)
    components = pd.concat(
        [
            0.5 * z_oil,
            0.25 * z_breakeven,
            0.25 * z_cpi,
            -0.6 * z_indpro,
        ],
        axis=1,
    )
    all_nan_mask = components.isna().all(axis=1)
    components_filled = components.fillna(0.0)
    supply_shock = components_filled.sum(axis=1)
    supply_shock[all_nan_mask] = np.nan
    exposure = -supply_shock.clip(lower=-2.5, upper=2.5)
    exposure = exposure.where(~all_nan_mask, 0.0)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>taylor_rule_policy_accommodation_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Rule-relative monetary policy stance: compares the effective fed funds rate to a Taylor-rule-implied rate…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Rule-relative monetary policy stance: compares the effective fed funds rate to a Taylor-rule-implied rate based on realized inflation and deviation of unemployment from its trailing 10-year average. Positive accommodation (rule rate above actual fed funds) signals abundant funding liquidity and lower discount rates, predicting higher subsequent equity market returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    cpi = panel['macro_cpi'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    cpi_chg = panel['macro_cpi_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    unrate = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    fedfunds = panel['macro_fedfunds'].groupby(level='date').first().sort_index()
    # forward-fill isolated publication gaps (up to a few months)
    cpi = cpi.ffill(limit=3)
    cpi_chg = cpi_chg.ffill(limit=3)
    unrate = unrate.ffill(limit=3)
    fedfunds = fedfunds.ffill(limit=3)
    # inflation rate (annualized, %) from cpi level and its 12m change
    cpi_base = cpi - cpi_chg
    infl = 100.0 * cpi_chg / cpi_base.where(cpi_base &gt; 0)
    # past-only rolling 120-month mean of unemployment, shifted 1 to avoid look-ahead
    ustar = unrate.shift(1).rolling(window=120, min_periods=36).mean()
    taylor = 2.0 + infl + 0.5 * (infl - 2.0) - 2.0 * (unrate - ustar)
    accommodation = taylor - fedfunds
    exposure = accommodation.dropna()
    exposure.index.name = 'date'
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>unemployment_news_regime_asymmetry_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Sign-flipping labour-market timing signal: rising unemployment is treated as good news for the market during…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Sign-flipping labour-market timing signal: rising unemployment is treated as good news for the market during expansions (implying policy easing) but as bad news during contractions. Recession state is proxied in real time by a Sahm-rule-style rolling-minimum trigger on the unemployment rate (or the NBER indicator), avoiding look-ahead from publication-lagged recession dating.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    u = panel['macro_unrate'].groupby(level='date').first()
    u_chg12m = panel['macro_unrate_chg12m'].groupby(level='date').first()
    usrec = panel['macro_usrec'].groupby(level='date').first()
    u = u.sort_index()
    u_chg12m = u_chg12m.reindex(u.index)
    usrec = usrec.reindex(u.index)
    # rolling 12-month min of past unemployment (excludes current month)
    rolling_min = u.rolling(12, closed='left').min()
    sahm_gap = u - rolling_min
    recession_state = ((sahm_gap &gt; 0.4) | (usrec == 1)).astype(float)
    exposure = u_chg12m * (1 - 2 * recession_state)
    valid = u.notna() &amp; u_chg12m.notna() &amp; usrec.notna() &amp; sahm_gap.notna()
    exposure = exposure.where(valid, np.nan)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>unemployment_trough_breakout_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Sahm-rule-like gap between unemployment rate and its trailing 12-month minimum, amplified when industrial…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Sahm-rule-like gap between unemployment rate and its trailing 12-month minimum, amplified when industrial production momentum is negative. Higher gap signals labor-market deterioration and impending equity drawdown; harness de-risks exposure when the raw score is large (expected_sign=-1).</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    unrate = panel["macro_unrate"].groupby(level="date").first().sort_index()
    indpro_chg = panel["macro_indpro_chg12m"].groupby(level="date").first().sort_index()
    unrate = unrate.ffill()
    indpro_chg = indpro_chg.ffill()
    rolling_min = unrate.rolling(window=12, min_periods=6).min()
    gap = unrate - rolling_min
    slow = (indpro_chg &lt; 0).astype(float)
    raw = gap * (1.0 + slow)
    missing_mask = unrate.isna() | indpro_chg.isna()
    raw = raw.where(~missing_mask, np.nan)
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>valuation_dispersion_market_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Cross-sectional dispersion of log(P/B) across the equity universe, measured as the 90th minus 10th percentile…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Cross-sectional dispersion of log(P/B) across the equity universe, measured as the 90th minus 10th percentile each month. Wide dispersion signals speculative excess/disagreement and historically precedes weak aggregate returns; the signal is dispersion minus its trailing 36-month (past-only) mean, so high (wide) dispersion implies reduced market exposure.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['pb', 'marketcap']].copy()
    df = df[(df['pb'] &gt; 0) &amp; (df['marketcap'] &gt; 0)]
    df['x'] = np.log(df['pb'])
    def disp_fn(group):
        if len(group) &lt; 200:
            return np.nan
        p90 = group.quantile(0.90)
        p10 = group.quantile(0.10)
        return p90 - p10
    disp = df.groupby(level='date')['x'].apply(disp_fn)
    disp = disp.sort_index()
    rolling_mean = disp.rolling(window=36, min_periods=24).mean()
    # ensure past-only: shift by 1 so current month's disp is not in its own rolling mean
    rolling_mean = rolling_mean.shift(1)
    signal = disp - rolling_mean
    signal = signal.reindex(disp.index)
    return signal</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>variance_risk_premium_timing</code><span class="la-tag">other</span><span class="gist">Variance risk premium timing signal: gap between implied volatility (VIX) and realized equity volatility…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Variance risk premium timing signal: gap between implied volatility (VIX) and realized equity volatility (cross-sectional median of trailing 1y stock-level realized vol), smoothed with a 3-month rolling mean. A wide gap indicates elevated compensation for bearing variance risk, forecasting higher subsequent market excess returns.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> other</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> macro, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    vix = panel['macro_vix'].groupby(level='date').first()
    rv = panel['vol_252'].groupby(level='date').median() * 100.0
    vrp = vix - rv
    raw = vrp.rolling(3, min_periods=1).mean()
    return raw</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_accruals_market_timing</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Aggregate accruals (netinc - ncfo)/assets, median across large liquid names, as a macro earnings-quality…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Aggregate accruals (netinc - ncfo)/assets, median across large liquid names, as a macro earnings-quality timing signal; high aggregate accruals predict low subsequent market returns, so exposure = -zscore of smoothed aggregate accruals.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['netinc', 'ncfo', 'assets', 'marketcap']].copy()
    valid = (
        df['assets'].notna() &amp; (df['assets'] &gt; 0) &amp;
        df['netinc'].notna() &amp; df['ncfo'].notna() &amp;
        df['marketcap'].notna()
    )
    df = df[valid]
    acc = (df['netinc'] - df['ncfo']) / df['assets']
    acc = acc.clip(-0.5, 0.5)
    df['acc'] = acc
    # market-cap 40th percentile filter, per date
    pct40 = df.groupby(level='date')['marketcap'].transform(
        lambda x: x.quantile(0.40)
    )
    mask = df['marketcap'] &gt;= pct40
    df = df[mask]
    # count valid names per date
    counts = df.groupby(level='date')['acc'].count()
    agg_t = df.groupby(level='date')['acc'].median()
    agg_t = agg_t.where(counts &gt;= self.MIN_NAMES, np.nan)
    agg_t = agg_t.sort_index()
    smooth = agg_t.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    exp_mean = smooth.expanding(36).mean()
    exp_std = smooth.expanding(36).std()
    z = (smooth - exp_mean) / exp_std
    z = z.where(exp_std &gt; 0, np.nan)
    exposure = -z
    exposure = exposure.clip(-2, 2)
    exposure.name = self.name
    return exposure</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>aggregate_earnings_growth_breadth_timing</code><span class="la-tag">quality</span><span class="gist">Timing signal based on the cross-sectional breadth of YoY earnings growth among top liquid-cap firms</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Timing signal based on the cross-sectional breadth of YoY earnings growth among top liquid-cap firms. Breadth is the fraction of firms with positive YoY net income growth; the signal is the deviation of current breadth from its trailing 12m average, deviation-detrended breadth. Wide breadth (broad earnings improvement) historically precedes weak subsequent market returns (Kothari, Lewellen, Warner), so expected_sign=-1.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> quality</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-off (cut exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> fundamental, price</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    netinc = panel['netinc']
    marketcap = panel['marketcap']
    ni_lag = netinc.groupby(level='ticker').shift(12)
    valid = (
        netinc.notna() &amp; ni_lag.notna()
        &amp; (ni_lag != 0)
        &amp; marketcap.notna() &amp; (marketcap &gt; 0)
    )
    # top liquid universe: top 50% by marketcap within each date among valid entries
    mc_valid = marketcap.where(valid)
    mc_rank = mc_valid.groupby(level='date').rank(pct=True, ascending=True)
    top_liquid = valid &amp; (mc_rank &gt;= 0.5)
    growth = (netinc - ni_lag) / ni_lag.abs()
    imp = (growth &gt; 0).astype(float)
    imp = imp.where(top_liquid)
    breadth_t = imp.groupby(level='date').mean()
    rolling_mean = breadth_t.rolling(12, min_periods=6).mean()
    raw_t = breadth_t - rolling_mean
    return raw_t</pre></div></details><details class="la-sig"><summary><code>money_illusion_real_yield_gap_timing</code><span class="la-tag">value</span><span class="gist">Modigliani-Cohn money illusion timing signal: compares aggregate market earnings yield (median of 1/pe among…</span></summary><div class="la-sig-body"><p>Modigliani-Cohn money illusion timing signal: compares aggregate market earnings yield (median of 1/pe among top-70% marketcap stocks) to the REAL 10y Treasury yield (nominal 10y minus trailing CPI inflation). A wide gap signals equities are irrationally cheap relative to real cash-flow discounting, forecasting high subsequent market returns as the illusion unwinds.</p><div class="la-meta"><span><b>Category</b> value</span><span><b>Direction</b> High score → risk-on (raise exposure)</span><span><b>Data</b> price, fundamental, macro</span></div>
<pre class="la-code">def compute(self, panel) -&gt; pd.Series:
    df = panel[['pe', 'marketcap', 'macro_dgs10', 'macro_cpi', 'macro_cpi_chg12m']].copy()
    valid = (df['pe'] &gt; 0) &amp; df['marketcap'].notna() &amp; (df['marketcap'] &gt; 0)
    df = df[valid]
    # top 70% marketcap per date
    def top70_mask(x):
        thresh = x.quantile(0.30)
        return x &gt;= thresh
    mc = df['marketcap']
    thresh_by_date = mc.groupby(level='date').transform(lambda x: x.quantile(0.30))
    top_df = df[mc &gt;= thresh_by_date]
    ey = 1.0 / top_df['pe']
    agg_ey = ey.groupby(level='date').median()
    macro = panel[['macro_dgs10', 'macro_cpi', 'macro_cpi_chg12m']].groupby(level='date').mean()
    denom = macro['macro_cpi'] - macro['macro_cpi_chg12m']
    valid_macro = macro['macro_dgs10'].notna() &amp; macro['macro_cpi'].notna() &amp; \
        macro['macro_cpi_chg12m'].notna() &amp; (denom &gt; 0)
    infl = 100.0 * macro['macro_cpi_chg12m'] / denom
    real_y = macro['macro_dgs10'] - infl
    signal = 100.0 * agg_ey - real_y
    signal = signal.where(valid_macro)
    signal = signal.dropna()
    signal.index.name = 'date'
    return signal</pre></div></details>
</div>
</details>


::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**Research, not investment advice.** Data ends around February 2024. Transaction
costs use a simple per-unit-traded model with no market-impact term, so capacity
is not addressed. Delisting returns are approximated rather than sourced from the
corporate-actions table. Every number here is a backtest.
:::
